title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子貢問曰賜也何如子曰女器也曰何器
也曰瑚璉也
王弘誨
同考試官教諭蕭〔標〕批子貢之才之美全在器
與瑚璉上見此作不用實事意含語中而文采自
露且得夫子之旨宜錄以式
同考試官教諭曾〔三省〕批提掇聯絡不離本意而
===
詞復清勁當是作者
考試官教諭黃〔士元〕批說器與瑚璉處簡健切
實
考試官學正宋〔奪〕批詞不落套可以為文
聖人因賢者之問而深許其才之美焉甚矣美
才之難得也賢者之才亦器之不凡者聖人之
許之也有以哉昔夫子稱子賤為君子子貢蓋
聞之矣然思齊之念不容自已也乃直以己為
問曰賜也何如將以考其成焉夫子就其才而
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

子貢問曰：「賜也何如？」子曰：「女，器也。」曰：「何器也？」曰：「瑚璉也。」

王弘誨

同考試官教諭蕭〔標〕批：「子貢之才之美，全在器與瑚璉上見。此作不用實事，意含語中，而文采自露，且得夫子之旨，宜錄以式。」

同考試官教諭曾〔三省〕批：「提掇聯絡，不離本意，而詞復清勁，當是作者。」

考試官教諭黃〔士元〕批：「說器與瑚璉處，簡健切實。」

考試官學正宋〔奪〕批：「詞不落套，可以為文。」

聖人因賢者之問，而深許其才之美焉。甚矣，美才之難得也！賢者之才，亦器之不凡者，聖人之許之也有以哉！昔夫子稱子賤為君子，子貢蓋聞之矣。然思齊之念，不容自已也，乃直以己為問，曰：「賜也何如？」將以考其成焉。夫子就其才而
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Zigong asked, “What do you think of me, Ci?” The Master said, “You are a vessel.” He asked, “What kind of vessel?” The Master said, “A hu or lian sacrificial vessel.”

Wang Honghui

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Xiao Biao: “The excellence of Zigong’s talent is revealed entirely through ‘vessel’ and ‘hu and lian.’ This composition uses no concrete historical examples; its meaning is implicit in its language, and its literary brilliance emerges naturally. Moreover, it captures the Master’s intent. It should be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zeng Sansheng: “Its selection and linking of points never depart from the original meaning, while its language is clear and vigorous. This is surely the work of an accomplished writer.”

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Huang Shiyuan: “The passages explaining ‘vessel’ and ‘hu and lian’ are concise, forceful, and directly to the point.”

Comment by Examiner and School Instructor Song Duo [?]: “Its language avoids conventional formulas; it qualifies as accomplished writing.”

In response to a worthy man’s question, the sage warmly acknowledged the excellence of his talent. How difficult it is to find outstanding talent! The worthy man’s talent was likewise that of an extraordinary vessel: the sage had good reason to commend him! Earlier, the Master had called Zijian a gentleman, and Zigong had presumably heard this. Yet he could not restrain his desire to equal him, so he asked directly about himself: “What do you think of me, Ci?” He sought thereby to assess what he had achieved. The Master, considering his talent, …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
許之曰物之言利者莫如器先王制之以前民
用者也女也頴悟幾於上智納之至繁而不匱
通達裕於平居投之所向而各適藏乎身者優
然以待用效之動也恢乎有餘地焉不是之器
而何哉夫子旣命之矣然擬議之間未敢自信
也乃又以器為問曰何器也將以究其歸焉夫
子又就其美而許之曰器之可貴者莫如瑚璉
夏商用之以享宗廟者也女也質美之中涵有
以增天下之重才華之外見又以貴天下之觀
===
俾立朝而潤色皇猷其清廟之望乎或從政而
宣昭物采其邦家之光乎是亦瑚璉也已矣夫
先之以有用之才繼之以不凡之器聖人之敎
人也如此子貢方人其容以器自安哉抑子貢
之在聖門視顏閔亦不多讓似非歉於德者夫
子但器其才而於君子若靳焉何耶蓋自切磋
琢磨之時已知其不器矣勵而進之然後達一
貫之旨至聞性與天道而晚年宮牆之喻天階
日月之說則又造乎高明之域所謂君子者非
punctuated: 許之曰：「物之言利者，莫如器，先王制之以前民用者也。女也頴悟，幾於上智，納之至繁而不匱；通達，裕於平居，投之所向而各適。藏乎身者，優然以待用；效之動也，恢乎有餘地焉。不是之器，而何哉？」夫子旣命之矣，然擬議之間，未敢自信也，乃又以器為問曰：「何器也？」將以究其歸焉。夫子又就其美而許之曰：「器之可貴者，莫如瑚璉，夏商用之以享宗廟者也。女也質美之中涵，有以增天下之重；才華之外見，又以貴天下之觀。俾立朝而潤色皇猷，其清廟之望乎？或從政而宣昭物采，其邦家之光乎？是亦瑚璉也已矣。」夫先之以有用之才，繼之以不凡之器，聖人之敎人也如此。子貢方人，其容以器自安哉？抑子貢之在聖門，視顏閔亦不多讓，似非歉於德者。夫子但器其才，而於君子若靳焉，何耶？蓋自切磋琢磨之時，已知其不器矣。勵而進之，然後達一貫之旨，至聞性與天道，而晚年宮牆之喻、天階日月之說，則又造乎高明之域。所謂君子者，非
translation_en: …endorsed him, saying: “Among things considered in terms of usefulness, none surpass vessels: the former kings fashioned them to further the people’s use. You are perceptive and quick to understand, approaching the highest wisdom; even when given matters of the utmost complexity, your resources are not exhausted. Your understanding is comprehensive, amply sufficient in ordinary life; wherever you are employed, you prove suited to the task. What you possess within yourself awaits employment with ease; when manifested in action, it leaves abundant capacity to spare. If this is not a vessel, what is it?” The Master had thus characterized him, yet as Zigong weighed these words, he did not dare feel assured. He therefore asked further about the vessel: “What kind of vessel?” He wished to ascertain the full import of the judgment. The Master then endorsed his excellence, saying: “Among precious vessels, none surpass the hu and lian, which the Xia and Shang used for offerings in their ancestral temples. The beauty of your substance, contained within, is sufficient to add weight to the world; the brilliance of your talents, manifested outwardly, lends distinction to what the world beholds. Were you to take your place at court and embellish imperial plans, would you not be an ornament of the pure ancestral temple? Were you to administer government and make manifest the splendor of its institutions, would you not be a glory to the state? Such a person is indeed a hu or lian.” First he spoke of useful talent, then of an extraordinary vessel: such was the sage’s way of teaching. Zigong judged other people; how could he allow himself to rest content with being a vessel? Moreover, among the sage’s disciples, Zigong yielded little even to Yan Hui and Min Sun, and seems hardly to have been deficient in virtue. Why, then, did the Master merely treat his talent as that of a vessel, while seeming to withhold the designation “gentleman”? In fact, from the time of their discussion of cutting, filing, carving, and polishing, he already knew that Zigong was no mere vessel. He encouraged him to advance, until Zigong understood the meaning of the single thread running through the Master’s teaching and came to hear of human nature and the Way of Heaven. In his later years, his analogy of the palace wall and his statements about the steps to Heaven [?] and the sun and moon showed that he had attained yet loftier realms of understanding. Was he not what is called a gentleman …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
歟器不足言矣乃知聖人之教所以達材亦以
成德
仲尼祖述堯舜憲章文武
何天衢
同考試官教諭童天胤批場中作者往往於堯舜
文武上發揮而祖述憲章四字殊欠分曉獨此篇
體認親切隨義闡明一洗浮蔓之習非精於理者
不能式之
同考試官教諭孫燿批莊重典雅無一字不從
===
題上發出而末言仲尼得統於人何等氣象大家
之作也
考試官教諭黃尭批自是說理文字
考試官學正宋大昇批渾厚精確迥異他作
帝王之道法聖人兼體之焉夫堯舜盡道文武
盡法也夫子兼之非天下之至聖其孰能與於
此且夫蘊諸心之謂道顯諸政之謂法帝王一
而已矣合而有之其惟仲尼乎何者五帝之先
莫不有道而執一中以建極堯舜之道斯全矣
punctuated:
歟？器不足言矣。乃知聖人之教，所以達材，亦以成德。

仲尼祖述堯舜，憲章文武。
何天衢

同考試官教諭童天胤批：場中作者往往於堯舜文武上發揮，而祖述憲章四字殊欠分曉。獨此篇體認親切，隨義闡明，一洗浮蔓之習，非精於理者不能。式之。

同考試官教諭孫燿批：莊重典雅，無一字不從題上發出，而末言仲尼得統於人，何等氣象！大家之作也。

考試官教諭黃尭批：自是說理文字。

考試官學正宋大昇批：渾厚精確，迥異他作。

帝王之道法，聖人兼體之焉。夫堯舜盡道，文武盡法也。夫子兼之，非天下之至聖，其孰能與於此？且夫蘊諸心之謂道，顯諸政之謂法，帝王一而已矣。合而有之，其惟仲尼乎？何者？五帝之先，莫不有道，而執一中以建極，堯舜之道斯全矣。
translation_en:
…was he not? To speak of him merely as a vessel is inadequate. Thus we understand that the sage’s teaching both develops talent and perfects virtue.

“Zhongni transmitted the tradition of Yao and Shun and took Wen and Wu as his models.”
By He Tianqu 何天衢.

Comment by Associate Examiner Tong Tianyin 童天胤, Instructor: Candidates in this examination often elaborate upon Yao, Shun, Wen, and Wu, yet leave the four characters meaning “transmitted the tradition” and “took as models” quite inadequately explained. This essay alone grasps their meaning intimately and elucidates each expression according to its sense, thoroughly sweeping away the habit of superficial, sprawling exposition. Only someone with a refined understanding of principle could accomplish this. Take it as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun Yao 孫燿, Instructor: Dignified and elegant, with not a single word that does not arise from the topic. At the end it speaks of Zhongni receiving the succession among men—what grandeur! This is the work of a master.

Comment by Examiner Huang Yao 黃尭, Instructor: This is assuredly writing that elucidates principle.

Comment by Examiner Song Dasheng 宋大昇, Director of Studies: Substantial, profound, and precise; markedly different from other compositions.

The sage embodies both the Way and the institutions of the emperors and kings. Yao and Shun fully realized the Way; Wen and Wu fully realized its institutions. The Master combined both. Who but the supreme sage of the world could attain this? What is stored within the heart is called the Way; what is manifested in government is called institutions. For emperors and kings, these are one and the same. Was it not Zhongni alone who possessed them together? Why is this? Those preceding the Five Emperors all possessed the Way; but through holding fast to the single Mean and thereby establishing the supreme standard, the Way of Yao and Shun attained its completeness.

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
仲尼生周之時世相遠也而道之所在其能違
乎是以祖而述之稽神化於唐虞獨宗授受之
秘會幾微於精一庸泯制作之勞於刪書而嘉
其盛焉往者賴以承也於尚論而賛其大焉後
者賴以啓也雖南面之治未甞親炙於其庭而
萬世心學之源若出於口授者矣其所以祖述
堯舜者如此三王之世莫不有法而監二代以
成文文武之法斯備矣仲尼爲周之人時相近
也而法之所在能無從乎是以憲而章之念斯
===
文之未墜遵成度以周旋幸謨烈之具存昭耿
光以對越在周禮者秩之恪乎其持循也在方
策者舉之煥乎其彰明也雖東周之興未能少
酬乎其志而一代維王之制皆由之終身者矣
其所以憲章文武者如此是則遠宗其道道外
無法也近守其法法外無道也玆仲尼集羣聖
之大成而盡中庸之道者歟雖然仲尼之生得
統於天者也故其道法上與天合凡律天時襲
水土行四時明日月育萬物植乾坤於不毀者
punctuated:
仲尼生周之時，世相遠也，而道之所在，其能違乎？是以祖而述之，稽神化於唐虞，獨宗授受之秘；會幾微於精一，庸泯制作之勞？於刪書而嘉其盛焉，往者賴以承也；於尚論而賛其大焉，後者賴以啓也。雖南面之治未甞親炙於其庭，而萬世心學之源若出於口授者矣。其所以祖述堯舜者如此。
三王之世莫不有法，而監二代以成文，文武之法斯備矣。仲尼爲周之人，時相近也，而法之所在，能無從乎？是以憲而章之，念斯文之未墜，遵成度以周旋；幸謨烈之具存，昭耿光以對越。在周禮者秩之，恪乎其持循也；在方策者舉之，煥乎其彰明也。雖東周之興未能少酬乎其志，而一代維王之制皆由之終身者矣。其所以憲章文武者如此。
是則遠宗其道，道外無法也；近守其法，法外無道也。玆仲尼集羣聖之大成而盡中庸之道者歟！雖然，仲尼之生，得統於天者也，故其道法上與天合。凡律天時、襲水土、行四時、明日月、育萬物、植乾坤於不毀者
translation_en:
…Zhongni was born in the Zhou era, far removed from them in time; yet how could he depart from the Way wherever it was found? Thus he took them as his forebears and transmitted their teachings. Investigating the wondrous transformations wrought under Tang Yao and Yu Shun, he especially revered the secret of their transmission and succession; comprehending the subtle workings of discernment and single-mindedness, could he efface their labors in establishing institutions [?]? In editing the Documents, he praised their flourishing achievements, thereby carrying forward what had come before; in discussing the ancients, he extolled their greatness, thereby opening the way for those who came after. Although he had never personally received instruction at their courts in the art of ruling while facing south, the source of the learning of the mind for all ages seemed to have come to him through oral instruction. Such was his way of taking Yao and Shun as his forebears and transmitting their teachings.
The ages of the Three Kings all possessed institutions; but through examining the two preceding dynasties and bringing their cultural forms to completion, the institutions of Kings Wen and Wu became fully developed. Zhongni was a man of Zhou, close to them in time; wherever their institutions remained, how could he fail to follow them? Thus he took them as models and made them manifest. Mindful that this cultural inheritance had not fallen away, he conducted himself according to established standards; rejoicing that their plans and achievements survived intact, he made their brilliant glory shine forth and reverently responded to it. What was contained in the Rites of Zhou he set in order, scrupulously maintaining and following it; what was recorded on tablets and documents he brought forward, splendidly illuminating it. Although the revival of an eastern Zhou never brought even a little fulfillment to his ambition, he followed throughout his life all the royal institutions of that dynasty. Such was his way of modeling himself upon Kings Wen and Wu and making their institutions manifest.
Thus, in looking back to the distant past, he revered their Way, outside which there were no institutions; in adhering to the nearer past, he upheld their institutions, outside which there was no Way. Was this not how Zhongni brought together the great achievements of all the sages and fully realized the Way of the Mean? Nevertheless, Zhongni was born receiving his succession from Heaven; hence his Way and institutions accorded above with Heaven. All that takes Heaven’s seasons as its rule, follows the conditions of water and land, sets the four seasons in motion, gives light to sun and moon, nourishes the myriad things, and establishes Heaven and Earth beyond destruction…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皆是物也豈止宗典謨之數語守周官之一書
而後盡聖人之能事哉故仲尼不獨會帝王之
全而又成天地之大
仁之於父子也義之於君臣也禮之於賓
主也智之於賢者也聖人之於天道也
馬象乾
同考試官教諭翟〔務思〕批此篇機軸變化迥異諸
作且措詞瑩潔可式
考試官教諭黃〔士元〕批結發□聖人盡倫合天
===
處尤妙
考試官學正宋〔大勺〕批順鬯
大賢舉至理各屬於人責成之意有在矣蓋仁
義禮智天道人固有之也而各有所屬焉學者
可不責成於已耶孟子之意以為斯道之在天
下也有不可易之分則體道之在吾人也有不
容已之功今自其分而言之德愛曰仁天下無
適而非仁也而父子之恩則無所解焉其所以
愛而能勞養而能敬怡然有恩以相親者非此
punctuated:
皆是物也，豈止宗典謨之數語、守周官之一書，而後盡聖人之能事哉？故仲尼不獨會帝王之全，而又成天地之大。
仁之於父子也，義之於君臣也，禮之於賓主也，智之於賢者也，聖人之於天道也。
馬象乾
同考試官教諭翟〔務思〕批：此篇機軸變化，迥異諸作，且措詞瑩潔，可式。
考試官教諭黃〔士元〕批：結發□聖人盡倫合天處尤妙。
考試官學正宋〔大勺〕批：順鬯。
大賢舉至理，各屬於人，責成之意有在矣。蓋仁義禮智天道，人固有之也，而各有所屬焉。學者可不責成於已耶？孟子之意以為斯道之在天下也，有不可易之分；則體道之在吾人也，有不容已之功。今自其分而言之，德愛曰仁，天下無適而非仁也，而父子之恩則無所解焉。其所以愛而能勞，養而能敬，怡然有恩以相親者，非此
translation_en:
…all are manifestations of this same thing. How could the full accomplishment of the sage’s work consist merely in taking a few sayings from the Canons and Counsels as his model and adhering to the single book, the Offices of Zhou? Thus Zhongni not only brought together the full accomplishments of emperors and kings, but also brought to fulfillment the greatness of Heaven and Earth.
“Benevolence in the relationship between father and son; righteousness in the relationship between ruler and minister; ritual propriety in the relationship between guest and host; wisdom in relation to the worthy; and the sage in relation to the Way of Heaven.”
Ma Xianggan.
Associate Examiner Zhai Wusi, Instructor, comments: “This essay’s organizing conception varies and develops in ways markedly different from the other compositions. Its wording, moreover, is lucid and polished, worthy of emulation.”
Examiner Huang Shiyuan, Instructor, comments: “The conclusion brings out [?] how the sage fully realizes human relationships and accords with Heaven; this passage is especially fine.”
Examiner Song Dashao, Instructor, comments: “Fluent and clear.”
The great worthy sets forth the ultimate principles, assigning each to its human sphere: his intention is to hold people responsible for bringing them to fulfillment. Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, wisdom, and the Way of Heaven are indeed inherent in human beings, yet each has its particular sphere. Can learners fail to hold themselves responsible for their fulfillment? Mencius means that, since this Way has its unalterable distinctions throughout the world, we who embody the Way must undertake an effort that admits of no cessation. Let us now speak in terms of these distinctions. The virtue of love is called benevolence. Nowhere in the world is benevolence absent, yet the affectionate bond between father and son can never be dissolved. They love and can therefore undertake toil; they provide sustenance and can also show reverence; in glad affection they draw close to one another—is this not through this…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
仁之浹洽乎德宜曰義天下無適而非義也而
君臣之義則無所逃焉其所以令而不違共而
不二恪然有分以相守者非此義之綱維乎以
節文者存乎禮則於賓主焉見之退讓以飾情
嘉會以章度酬酢之秩固會通之觀矣以甄別
者存乎智則於賢否焉見之秉哲以知人作謀
以辨物權度之精固明覺之良矣至於神明之
撰性命之原淵微而莫測於穆而不已者有天
道焉合一而無間其惟聖人乎窮神以繼其志
===
其藏諸用者渾然天道之本體也知化以述其
事其顯諸仁者燦然天道之流行也非聖人其
孰能之哉是則命之在人者固有不同而性之
在我者則無或異矯其異而歸之同盡性者當
知所從事矣大抵仁義禮智之性即天道之流
行而賦於物者蓋五行之生各一其性其在我
者則有厚薄之稟在人者則有遇不遇之殊而
聖人盡性以立極脩人以合天此其所以爲人
倫之至孟子對舉而互言之示人以希聖之準
punctuated: 仁之浹洽乎？德宜曰義，天下無適而非義也，而君臣之義則無所逃焉。其所以令而不違，共而不二，恪然有分以相守者，非此義之綱維乎？以節文者存乎禮，則於賓主焉見之：退讓以飾情，嘉會以章度，酬酢之秩，固會通之觀矣。以甄別者存乎智，則於賢否焉見之：秉哲以知人，作謀以辨物，權度之精，固明覺之良矣。至於神明之撰，性命之原，淵微而莫測，於穆而不已者，有天道焉。合一而無間，其惟聖人乎？窮神以繼其志，其藏諸用者，渾然天道之本體也；知化以述其事，其顯諸仁者，燦然天道之流行也。非聖人，其孰能之哉？是則命之在人者固有不同，而性之在我者則無或異。矯其異而歸之同，盡性者當知所從事矣。大抵仁義禮智之性，即天道之流行而賦於物者。蓋五行之生，各一其性，其在我者則有厚薄之稟，在人者則有遇不遇之殊。而聖人盡性以立極，脩人以合天，此其所以爲人倫之至。孟子對舉而互言之，示人以希聖之準
translation_en:
…is this not the all-pervading influence of benevolence? Virtue expressed in fitting conduct is called righteousness. Nowhere under Heaven is righteousness absent, yet the righteous obligations between ruler and minister cannot be evaded. That commands meet with no disobedience, that service is rendered without divided loyalty, and that each reverently upholds the distinctions of his station—is this not the binding framework of righteousness? Regulation and refinement reside in ritual propriety, and are manifest in the relations between guest and host. Deference and yielding refine their feelings; harmonious gatherings display the proper standards. The orderly exchange of toasts indeed reveals how these come together in practice. Discrimination resides in wisdom, and is manifest in distinguishing the worthy from the unworthy. One employs discernment to understand people and deliberates to distinguish things. Precision in weighing and judging is indeed the excellence of clear awareness.

As for the workings of spiritual intelligence and the source of human nature and Heaven’s mandate—profound and subtle beyond fathoming, solemnly mysterious and unceasing—there is the Way of Heaven. Who but the sage can unite with it without any separation? By fathoming the spiritual, he carries on Heaven’s intent: what is concealed within its operations is the integral underlying substance of the Way of Heaven. By understanding transformation, he carries forward Heaven’s work: what is manifest in benevolence is the radiant unfolding of the Way of Heaven. Who but the sage could accomplish this?

Thus, what is allotted to people by Heaven does indeed differ, but the nature within us is never different. By rectifying these differences and returning to what is shared, those who would fully realize their nature should know where to direct their efforts. Broadly speaking, the nature endowed with benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom is precisely the unfolding of the Way of Heaven as bestowed upon things. In the generation of things through the Five Phases, each has its particular nature. Within ourselves, there are richer and poorer endowments; among people, there are differences between meeting with favorable circumstances and failing to do so. Yet the sage fully realizes his nature to establish the supreme standard, and cultivates the human to accord with Heaven. This is why he represents the highest fulfillment of human relationships. Mencius sets these matters side by side and speaks of each in relation to the other, showing people a standard by which to aspire to sagehood…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也然則學者當何如亦曰盡倫盡性則聖可至
天可合矣故曰道之大原出於天
易
嘉會足以合禮
何天衢
同考試官教諭童天胤批嘉會處便是禮凡一事
一物都到恰好處便是嘉會此作發明殆盡錄之
同考試官教諭孫燿批辭不費而意足得潔淨
精微之旨者
===
考試官教諭黃士元批有體認有布置
考試官學正宋大昇批說理明白
惟君子能全乎禮之德以見其合天之功也夫
禮之德本無不全者也君子能嘉其所會則禮
卽此而在矣是不可見其合天之亨哉文言之
意以爲乾道之亨卽人性之禮而爲嘉之會者
人皆有之也能全之者鮮矣惟君子則反情以
和其志殊事有合敬之休可觀可度煥乎其有
章焉比類以成其行隨在皆文德之懿盡善盡
punctuated:
也。然則學者當何如？亦曰：盡倫盡性，則聖可至，天可合矣。故曰：「道之大原出於天。」

易
嘉會足以合禮
何天衢

同考試官教諭童天胤批：嘉會處便是禮，凡一事一物都到恰好處，便是嘉會。此作發明殆盡，錄之。
同考試官教諭孫燿批：辭不費而意足，得潔淨精微之旨者。
考試官教諭黃士元批：有體認，有布置。
考試官學正宋大昇批：說理明白。

惟君子能全乎禮之德，以見其合天之功也。夫禮之德，本無不全者也。君子能嘉其所會，則禮卽此而在矣。是不可見其合天之亨哉？文言之意，以爲乾道之亨卽人性之禮，而爲嘉之會者，人皆有之也。能全之者鮮矣。惟君子則反情以和其志，殊事有合敬之休，可觀可度，煥乎其有章焉；比類以成其行，隨在皆文德之懿，盡善盡
translation_en:
…Thus, what should learners do? Simply this: fully discharge their human relationships and fully realize their nature; then sagehood can be attained and harmony with Heaven achieved. Hence the saying: “The great source of the Way comes from Heaven.”

Book of Changes
“The gathering of excellences is sufficient to accord with ritual propriety.”
He Tianqu

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Tong Tianyin: Where excellences gather, there is ritual propriety. When every affair and every thing reaches precisely its proper state, this is the gathering of excellences. This composition elucidates the matter almost exhaustively. Include it in the record.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Sun Yao: The wording is economical, yet the meaning is fully conveyed. It captures the purport of purity, refinement, and subtlety.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Huang Shiyuan: It shows personal understanding and thoughtful arrangement.

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Song Dasheng: Its exposition of principle is clear.

Only the gentleman can fully realize the virtue of ritual propriety and thereby manifest his achievement in harmonizing with Heaven. Now, the virtue of ritual propriety is inherently complete in every respect. If the gentleman can bring excellence to what he gathers together, ritual propriety is present therein. Does this not reveal his flourishing in harmony with Heaven? The meaning of the Commentary on the Words is that the flourishing of the Way of Qian is precisely the ritual propriety inherent in human nature. Everyone possesses this gathering of excellences, but few can fully realize it. Only the gentleman returns to his true feelings to harmonize his intent. In diverse affairs there is the beauty of a shared reverence, worthy of observation and emulation, resplendent in its ordered pattern. He brings together like things to perfect his conduct; wherever he may be, there is the excellence of cultivated virtue, perfect in goodness and…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
美郁乎其有文焉苟斯須之未和非嘉會也自
一心以施於四體有周旋焉有折旋焉而動容
所及無一而非莊敬之發見也或彼此之少乖
非嘉會也自一身以達之五倫有主恩焉有主
義焉而交際所接無一而非和順之貫徹也夫
君子嘉其所會如此而謂不足以合禮耶蓋天
理有自然之節文也玆焉觀其會通則文明以
止適得乎天秩之體人事有當然之儀則也玆
焉履其中正則經緯有章允協乎人紀之常周
===
旋者其中規也折旋者其中矩也嘉之所在卽
會之所在其與天道之咸章也夫豈異哉主恩
者其懽然也主義者其燦然也會之所存卽禮
之所存其與品物之咸亨也抑何殊哉噫君子
法天成性之功至矣雖然亨於時爲夏萬物皆
相見於後天之卦爲離文明之象也君子致禮
以飾治囿天下於文明之中使百姓和天地官
羣物咸若若記之所稱述皆大順之實也豈特
嘉會一身而已哉故曰大禮與天地同節
punctuated: 美，郁乎其有文焉。苟斯須之未和，非嘉會也。自一心以施於四體，有周旋焉，有折旋焉，而動容所及，無一而非莊敬之發見也。或彼此之少乖，非嘉會也。自一身以達之五倫，有主恩焉，有主義焉，而交際所接，無一而非和順之貫徹也。夫君子嘉其所會如此，而謂不足以合禮耶？蓋天理有自然之節文也，玆焉觀其會通，則文明以止，適得乎天秩之體；人事有當然之儀則也，玆焉履其中正，則經緯有章，允協乎人紀之常。周旋者，其中規也；折旋者，其中矩也。嘉之所在，卽會之所在，其與天道之咸章也，夫豈異哉？主恩者，其懽然也；主義者，其燦然也。會之所存，卽禮之所存，其與品物之咸亨也，抑何殊哉？噫！君子法天成性之功至矣！雖然，亨於時爲夏，萬物皆相見；於後天之卦爲離，文明之象也。君子致禮以飾治，囿天下於文明之中，使百姓和、天地官、羣物咸若，若記之所稱述，皆大順之實也。豈特嘉會一身而已哉？故曰：「大禮與天地同節。」
translation_en:
…beautiful, richly displaying its refinement. If harmony is lacking even for an instant, this is no gathering of excellence. Extending from the single mind to the four limbs, there are circling movements and angular turns; in every movement and aspect of one’s bearing, nothing fails to manifest solemnity and reverence. If there is even a slight discord between oneself and others, this is no gathering of excellence. Extending from one’s own person to the five human relationships, some are governed principally by affection and others by righteousness; in all one’s dealings, nothing fails to be permeated by harmony and accord. When the gentleman thus brings excellence to what he gathers together, can one say that this is insufficient to accord with ritual propriety?

Heavenly principle possesses its natural articulations and patterns. By discerning here how these converge and interconnect, the gentleman combines cultivated brilliance with restraint, attaining precisely the substance of Heaven’s ordering. Human affairs possess their proper standards of conduct. By practicing here what is central and correct, he brings orderly pattern to their warp and weft, truly conforming to the constant norms of human relationships. His circling movements conform to the compass; his angular turns conform to the square. Wherever excellence is found, there too is its gathering. How could this differ from the Way of Heaven, in which all is made manifest? Where affection governs, there is joy; where righteousness governs, there is a radiant clarity of distinctions. Wherever this gathering abides, there too abides ritual propriety. How could this differ from the flourishing of all the varieties of things? Ah! The gentleman’s achievement in modeling himself on Heaven and fulfilling his nature is consummate indeed!

Yet flourishing corresponds among the seasons to summer, when all things become manifest to one another; among the trigrams of the Later Heaven arrangement, it corresponds to Li, the image of cultivated brilliance. The gentleman brings ritual propriety to its fullest realization to adorn his governance, encompassing all under Heaven within cultivated brilliance. He thereby enables the common people to live in harmony, Heaven and Earth to perform their offices, and all things to follow their proper courses. Such conditions, as recounted in the Record of Rites, are all concrete manifestations of the great accord. How could this gathering of excellence be confined to his own person alone? Thus it is said: “Great ritual shares the rhythms and measures of Heaven and Earth.”

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以言乎天地之間則備矣夫乾其靜也專
其動也直是以大生焉夫坤其靜也翕
其動也闢是以廣生焉廣大配天地
梁紹篊
同考試官教諭童批易之廣大本模倣天地
而有此作推其相生相配始終一貫言之可謂善
發易之精蘊者矣
同考試官教諭孫批天地乾坤廣大其名雖
殊其實皆易理也此作能提出此意非深於易者
不能
考試官教諭黃批精當
考試官學正宋批明淨
大傳論易之廣大察乎天地因推其相生相配
之妙焉蓋天地之間無乎不備易之廣大也然
不推其相生相配之實抑何以知其然哉大傳
贊易之意謂夫易之為書也語法象則謂之天
地語性情則謂之乾坤語功用則謂之廣大是
廣大也不但遠近之不遺已也極而言之仰觀
punctuated:
以言乎天地之間，則備矣。夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。廣大配天地。
梁紹篊
同考試官教諭童批：易之廣大，本模倣天地而有。此作推其相生相配，始終一貫言之，可謂善發易之精蘊者矣。
同考試官教諭孫批：天地、乾坤、廣大，其名雖殊，其實皆易理也。此作能提出此意，非深於易者不能。
考試官教諭黃批：精當。
考試官學正宋批：明淨。
大傳論易之廣大，察乎天地，因推其相生相配之妙焉。蓋天地之間，無乎不備，易之廣大也。然不推其相生相配之實，抑何以知其然哉？大傳贊易之意，謂夫易之為書也，語法象則謂之天地，語性情則謂之乾坤，語功用則謂之廣大。是廣大也，不但遠近之不遺已也。極而言之，仰觀
translation_en:
“Speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, it is complete. Qian, in stillness, is concentrated; in motion, it is direct: thus it generates greatness. Kun, in stillness, gathers in; in motion, it opens out: thus it generates breadth. Its breadth and greatness match Heaven and Earth.”
Liang Shaohong 梁紹篊
Comment by Associate Examiner Tong, Instructor: The breadth and greatness of the Changes arise fundamentally from its modeling itself upon Heaven and Earth. This composition explores how they give rise to and correspond with one another, maintaining a consistent argument from beginning to end. It may well be said to reveal skillfully the profound essence of the Changes.
Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor: Heaven and Earth, Qian and Kun, breadth and greatness—though their names differ, in substance they are all the principles of the Changes. This composition brings out this meaning; only someone deeply versed in the Changes could do so.
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: Precise and apt.
Comment by Examiner Song, Education Official: Clear and lucid.
The Great Commentary discusses the breadth and greatness of the Changes by examining Heaven and Earth, and thereby explores the wondrous ways in which they give rise to and correspond with one another. Everything between Heaven and Earth is fully encompassed: such is the breadth and greatness of the Changes. Yet unless we investigate the actual grounds of their mutual generation and correspondence, how can we know why this is so? The intention of the Great Commentary in praising the Changes is to say that, in this book, when speaking of patterns and images, one calls them Heaven and Earth; when speaking of inherent nature and disposition, one calls them Qian and Kun; when speaking of efficacy and function, one calls them breadth and greatness. This breadth and greatness do more than merely leave out nothing, whether distant or near. To pursue the matter to its utmost, looking upward…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
俯察散殊而不可盡者孰充塞是上際下蟠充
周而不可窮者孰森布是蓋天地之間莫非氣
也而亦莫非理也易之廣大有如此然豈無所
自耶亦本之乾坤耳夫乾天下之至健也其爲
物也一而實靜專以蘊化育之機而動直以達
流行之用藏諸用者顯諸仁舉天下之道器盡
在其包羅之中乾之所以大也易之大不於是
而生耶夫坤天下之至順也其爲物也二而虛
靜翕以涵各正之體而動闢以運無方之化復
===
乎命者育乎神舉天下之形色咸在其含弘之
内坤之所以廣也易之廣不於是而生耶夫廣
大之相生於乾坤若此則其相配乎天地也夫
焉有所强哉蓋天以無不覆爲大而易以無不
備爲德異位同功大有以配乎天矣地以無不
載爲廣而易以無不包爲量異形同體廣有以
配乎地矣天地也乾坤也廣大也一皆易書之
實理也故曰以言乎天地之間則備矣此易之
所以與天地準也與抑天地之廣大由於動靜
punctuated: 俯察，散殊而不可盡者，孰充塞是？上際下蟠，充周而不可窮者，孰森布是？蓋天地之間，莫非氣也，而亦莫非理也。易之廣大有如此，然豈無所自耶？亦本之乾坤耳。夫乾，天下之至健也。其爲物也，一而實，靜專以蘊化育之機，而動直以達流行之用。藏諸用者，顯諸仁，舉天下之道器，盡在其包羅之中，乾之所以大也。易之大，不於是而生耶？夫坤，天下之至順也。其爲物也，二而虛，靜翕以涵各正之體，而動闢以運無方之化。復乎命者，育乎神，舉天下之形色，咸在其含弘之内，坤之所以廣也。易之廣，不於是而生耶？夫廣大之相生於乾坤若此，則其相配乎天地也，夫焉有所强哉？蓋天以無不覆爲大，而易以無不備爲德，異位同功，大有以配乎天矣。地以無不載爲廣，而易以無不包爲量，異形同體，廣有以配乎地矣。天地也，乾坤也，廣大也，一皆易書之實理也。故曰：「以言乎天地之間，則備矣。」此易之所以與天地準也與！抑天地之廣大，由於動靜
translation_en:
…and looking down to examine: what fills this realm with things so various and dispersed that they cannot be exhausted? Reaching to the uppermost limits and extending throughout the depths below, what arrays all that fills every quarter without end? Between Heaven and Earth, nothing is other than vital energy, and nothing is other than principle. Such are the breadth and greatness of the Changes. Yet could these have no source? They too are rooted in Qian and Kun.

Qian is the utmost strength in the world. In its constitution, it is one and solid. In stillness it is concentrated, storing the potential for transformation and nurture; in movement it proceeds directly, realizing its function of circulating everywhere. What is concealed in its functioning is manifest in its benevolence. All the Way and all concrete things under Heaven lie within its encompassing scope: this is what makes Qian great. Does not the greatness of the Changes arise from this? Kun is the utmost compliance in the world. In its constitution, it is twofold and empty. In stillness it draws together, embracing the substance through which each thing attains its proper nature; in movement it opens out, carrying forward transformation unrestricted by any fixed direction. What returns to its allotted nature is nurtured through its numinous power. All forms and colors under Heaven lie within its capacious embrace: this is what makes Kun broad. Does not the breadth of the Changes arise from this?

Since breadth and greatness arise thus from Qian and Kun, how could there be anything forced in their correspondence with Heaven and Earth? Heaven is great because there is nothing it does not cover; the Changes has as its virtue that there is nothing it does not comprise. Different in position but alike in achievement, its greatness is sufficient to match Heaven. Earth is broad because there is nothing it does not support; the Changes has as its capacity that there is nothing it does not encompass. Different in form but alike in substance, its breadth is sufficient to match Earth. Heaven and Earth, Qian and Kun, breadth and greatness—all are the substantive principles of the book of Changes. Thus it says: “Speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, it comprises everything.” Is this not why the Changes accords with Heaven and Earth? Moreover, the breadth and greatness of Heaven and Earth derive from movement and stillness…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之互根而人心之廣大則由於主靜以立體蓋
靜無不存則動無不得矣性由此盡命由此立
而參賛位育之功有不難致者至此則廣大不
在易而在吾身不以易配天地而以吾身配天
地矣體易之功於是為大
書
夔曰於予擊石拊石百獸率舞庶尹允諧
帝庸作歌曰勅天之命惟時惟幾乃歌
曰股肱喜哉元首起哉百工熙哉皐陶
===
拜手稽首颺言曰念哉率作興事慎乃
憲欽哉屢省乃成欽哉乃賡載歌曰元
首明哉股肱良哉庶事康哉
葉夢熊
同考試官敎授秦 批 史臣先述作樂以紀成
後述賡歌以示警事不相蒙而意實相成此篇發
明意在言外可與言史者矣
考試官敎諭黃 批 善模寫太和氣象
考試官學正宋 批 明順
punctuated:
之互根，而人心之廣大則由於主靜以立體。蓋靜無不存，則動無不得矣。性由此盡，命由此立，而參賛位育之功有不難致者。至此，則廣大不在易而在吾身，不以易配天地而以吾身配天地矣。體易之功於是為大。
書
夔曰：「於！予擊石拊石，百獸率舞，庶尹允諧。」帝庸作歌曰：「勅天之命，惟時惟幾。」乃歌曰：「股肱喜哉！元首起哉！百工熙哉！」皐陶拜手稽首，颺言曰：「念哉！率作興事，慎乃憲。欽哉！屢省乃成。欽哉！」乃賡載歌曰：「元首明哉！股肱良哉！庶事康哉！」
葉夢熊
同考試官敎授秦批：史臣先述作樂以紀成，後述賡歌以示警。事不相蒙，而意實相成。此篇發明意在言外，可與言史者矣。
考試官敎諭黃批：善模寫太和氣象。
考試官學正宋批：明順。
translation_en:
…being rooted in one another, whereas the breadth and greatness of the human mind arise from taking stillness as primary in establishing its foundation. For when nothing is left unpreserved in stillness, nothing fails to find its proper realization in activity. Through this, one fully realizes one’s nature and establishes one’s Heaven-bestowed destiny; the achievement of assisting Heaven and Earth in bringing all things to their proper places and nurturing their growth is then attainable without difficulty. At this point, breadth and greatness reside not in the Changes but in ourselves. It is no longer the Changes that we match with Heaven and Earth, but our own persons. Thus great indeed is the achievement of embodying the Changes.
Book of Documents
Kui said: “Ah! I strike the sounding stones, gently tapping them, and all the beasts dance together; the many officials are truly in harmony.” The emperor thereupon composed a song, saying: “Attend diligently to Heaven’s mandate, mindful of timing and the first stirrings of events.” Then he sang: “When the arms and legs rejoice, the head rises to action, and the hundred officials flourish!” Gao Yao bowed with hands joined and touched his forehead to the ground, proclaiming: “Be mindful! In leading undertakings and initiating affairs, be careful of your rules. Be reverent! Repeatedly examine your accomplishments. Be reverent!” Then he continued the song: “When the head is enlightened, the arms and legs are worthy, and all affairs prosper!”
Ye Mengxiong
Comment by Associate Examiner Qin, Professor: The court historian first recounts the making of music to record achievement, and then recounts the continuation of the song to convey an admonition. The events do not directly bear upon one another, yet their meanings in fact complement one another. This essay elucidates the meaning beyond the words; its author is someone with whom one may discuss history.
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: Skillfully depicts the atmosphere of supreme harmony.
Comment by Examiner Song, School Instructor: Clear and fluent.

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
史臣卽樂以徵治而因述夫君臣交儆之言焉
夫樂以象成功而昭治道者也有虞之治而君
臣責難之無已此其不可及也歟作虞史者以
爲作樂之本在上不在下感召之機以實不以
文觀夔之言曰莫難和者石聲之立辨也予則
於石之小者輕以擊之而其聲清以揚焉於石
之大者重以擊之而其聲濁以下焉石聲旣和
八音有不和者乎莫難感者人物之異情也今
則見夫百獸之舞而物無不和可徵焉見夫庶
===
尹之諧而人無不和可徵焉人物旣和政治有
不和者乎此皆君德之至而風動之象也治云
尚矣而虞之君臣未已焉帝用作歌以爲靡常
者天之命也而可弗敬乎天無時而不在則無
時而不敬可也天無事而不在則無事而不敬
可也然豈徒君爲然哉乃歌曰君之資臣猶元
首之資股肱也股肱而喜則元首之起庶事之
熙自有不期而然者矣敕天之道不有望于臣
乎臯陶賡歌以爲惟艱者君之位也而可弗念
punctuated:
史臣卽樂以徵治，而因述夫君臣交儆之言焉。
夫樂以象成功而昭治道者也。有虞之治，而君臣責難之無已，此其不可及也歟？作虞史者以爲作樂之本在上不在下，感召之機以實不以文。觀夔之言曰：「莫難和者，石聲之立辨也。予則於石之小者，輕以擊之，而其聲清以揚焉；於石之大者，重以擊之，而其聲濁以下焉。石聲旣和，八音有不和者乎？莫難感者，人物之異情也。今則見夫百獸之舞，而物無不和可徵焉；見夫庶尹之諧，而人無不和可徵焉。人物旣和，政治有不和者乎？」此皆君德之至而風動之象也。治云尚矣，而虞之君臣未已焉。帝用作歌，以爲靡常者天之命也，而可弗敬乎？天無時而不在，則無時而不敬可也；天無事而不在，則無事而不敬可也。然豈徒君爲然哉？乃歌曰：「君之資臣，猶元首之資股肱也。股肱而喜，則元首之起、庶事之熙，自有不期而然者矣。」敕天之道，不有望于臣乎？臯陶賡歌，以爲惟艱者君之位也，而可弗念
translation_en:
The historian draws upon music to attest to good government, and accordingly recounts the words by which ruler and ministers admonished one another.
Music represents accomplished achievement and makes manifest the way of government. Under the rule of Yu, ruler and ministers never ceased demanding difficult accomplishments of one another. Was this not what made their government impossible to equal? The author of the history of Yu held that the foundation for making music lay with those above, not those below, and that the power to evoke a response depended on substance, not outward embellishment. Consider Kui’s words: “Nothing is harder to harmonize than the sharply differentiated sounds of stone chimes [?]. I strike the smaller stones lightly, and their sounds are clear and rise high; I strike the larger stones heavily, and their sounds are deep and descend low. Once the stone chimes are harmonious, can any of the eight classes of musical instruments remain out of harmony? Nothing is harder to move than the differing dispositions of people and other creatures. Yet now we see the hundred beasts dancing: this attests that all creatures are in harmony. We see the various officials acting in concord: this attests that all people are in harmony. Once people and other creatures are harmonious, can government remain out of harmony?” All these are manifestations of the ruler’s consummate virtue and its influence, which moves others as the wind does.
Such government may be called exalted indeed, yet the ruler and ministers of Yu did not stop there. The emperor therefore composed a song, considering that Heaven’s mandate is inconstant: could one fail to be reverent? Since there is no time when Heaven is absent, one should never be without reverence; since there is no affair in which Heaven is absent, one should be reverent in every affair. Yet could this apply to the ruler alone? Thus he sang: “The ruler’s reliance on his ministers is like the head’s reliance on the limbs. When the limbs are joyful, the head rises to action and the many affairs flourish: these results naturally follow without being sought.” Does not the way of reverently attending to Heaven place expectations upon ministers? Gao Yao continued the song, considering that the ruler’s position is fraught with difficulty: could one fail to bear this in mind …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
哉興事之難而成始不可以不敬也考成之難
而成終不可以不敬也然豈臣所敢與哉乃歌
曰臣之輔君猶股肱之輔元首也元首而明則
股肱之良庶事之康亦有不期而然者矣御下
之權是不在於君乎噫于功成作樂之後而不
忘交相警戒之言有虞太和氣象不可以想見
其盛歟雖然天運于上而百物生者以雨風露
雷之各成其能焉耳君運于上而萬事理者以
禮樂刑政之各舉其職焉耳故簡以御煩而責
===
成乎臣者此之謂善用其明勞以代逸而效法
乎君者此之謂善用其言口蓋君道猶天然而臣
道也地道也終其事而不敢有其功者也
六服羣辟罔不承德
蔡蘭
同考試官教授秦批成王承文武大定之後
而首勤攘外安內之功可謂纘戎無虞者矣此作
體貼得出錄之
考試官教諭黃批六服通乎內外此篇發
punctuated:
哉？興事之難，而成始不可以不敬也；考成之難，而成終不可以不敬也。然豈臣所敢與哉？乃歌曰：「臣之輔君，猶股肱之輔元首也。元首而明，則股肱之良、庶事之康，亦有不期而然者矣。御下之權，是不在於君乎？」噫！于功成作樂之後，而不忘交相警戒之言，有虞太和氣象，不可以想見其盛歟？雖然，天運于上而百物生者，以雨風露雷之各成其能焉耳；君運于上而萬事理者，以禮樂刑政之各舉其職焉耳。故簡以御煩，而責成乎臣者，此之謂善用其明；勞以代逸，而效法乎君者，此之謂善用其言口。蓋君道猶天，然而臣道也，地道也，終其事而不敢有其功者也。

六服羣辟罔不承德

蔡蘭

同考試官教授秦批：「成王承文武大定之後，而首勤攘外安內之功，可謂纘戎無虞者矣。此作體貼得出，錄之。」

考試官教諭黃批：「六服通乎內外，此篇發
translation_en:
…could he fail to bear it in mind? Initiating undertakings is difficult, so bringing their beginnings to fruition requires reverence; assessing their completion is difficult, so bringing their conclusion to fruition likewise requires reverence. Yet how could a minister presume to intervene in this? Thus he sang: “A minister supports his ruler as the limbs support the head. When the head is enlightened, the excellence of the limbs and the well-being of all affairs will likewise follow of themselves. Does not authority over subordinates rest with the ruler?” Ah! Even after their achievements were complete and music had been composed, they did not forget words of mutual admonition. Can we not thus imagine the flourishing atmosphere of supreme harmony under Youyu? Even so, Heaven moves above and the myriad things grow because rain, wind, dew, and thunder each fulfill their capacities. The ruler acts above and the myriad affairs are ordered because rites, music, punishments, and government each perform their functions. Thus, to govern complexity through simplicity and hold ministers responsible for results is what is called making good use of one’s discernment. To undertake the toil in place of the ruler’s ease and take the ruler as one’s model is what is called making good use of one’s words [?]. The ruler’s way resembles Heaven; the minister’s way is the way of Earth: to complete the undertaking without presuming to claim its merit.

“Among the many lords of the six service zones, none failed to uphold his virtue.”

Cai Lan

He may indeed be said to have continued their great work without mishap. This composition successfully brings out that meaning. Selected for inclusion.”

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
發揮承德處殆盡
考試官學正宋批典雅可錄
觀羣侯之尊王而聖世之治昭矣夫臣者行君
之令而致之民者也于其承德也不可以見一
王之治哉史臣將記成王之訓官而先之以此
意謂人君之御天下也惟德之所施者博則威
之所制者廣周王之撫萬邦也果何如哉但見
自王畿而外有所謂侯甸男采衛焉分土之廣
狹不必其盡同均之爲天子之土也自天子而
===
下有所謂公侯伯子男焉列爵之崇卑不必其
皆齊均之爲天子之臣也侯度固其所素謹者
今則覩王政之惟新益篤其忠貞之念成憲固
其所克遵者今則仰王威之丕振益勤其嚮往
之心知王之考度凡以爲民也而所以承順其
德意者不但朝聘之禮爲然也凡夫敷五典時
地利而聚民之所欲者莫不事爲之制焉知王
之戡亂亦以爲民也而所以對揚其休命者不
但征伐之事爲然也凡夫詰姦慝刑暴亂而去
punctuated:
發揮承德處殆盡。
考試官學正宋批：典雅可錄。
觀羣侯之尊王，而聖世之治昭矣。夫臣者，行君之令而致之民者也。于其承德也，不可以見一王之治哉？史臣將記成王之訓官，而先之以此，意謂人君之御天下也，惟德之所施者博，則威之所制者廣。周王之撫萬邦也，果何如哉？但見自王畿而外，有所謂侯甸男采衛焉。分土之廣狹，不必其盡同，均之爲天子之土也。自天子而下，有所謂公侯伯子男焉。列爵之崇卑，不必其皆齊，均之爲天子之臣也。侯度固其所素謹者，今則覩王政之惟新，益篤其忠貞之念；成憲固其所克遵者，今則仰王威之丕振，益勤其嚮往之心。知王之考度，凡以爲民也，而所以承順其德意者，不但朝聘之禮爲然也。凡夫敷五典、時地利，而聚民之所欲者，莫不事爲之制焉。知王之戡亂，亦以爲民也，而所以對揚其休命者，不但征伐之事爲然也。凡夫詰姦慝、刑暴亂，而去
translation_en:
…fully develops the passage concerning the reception of royal virtue.
Examiner Song, an Instructor, comments: “Classical and elegant; worthy of inclusion.”
Observe how the assembled lords honor the king, and the good order of a sage age becomes manifest. Ministers carry out their ruler’s commands and convey them to the people. Can we not discern a king’s governance in their reception of his virtue? The court historian, about to record King Cheng’s instructions to his officials, prefaced them with this statement. Its meaning is that, when a ruler governs All under Heaven, the broader the reach of his virtue, the wider the sway of his authority. How, then, did the king of Zhou nurture the myriad states?
Beyond the royal domain were the zones called hou, dian, nan, cai, and wei. The territories allotted to them were not necessarily equal in extent, yet all alike were the Son of Heaven’s lands. Below the Son of Heaven were the ranks of duke, marquis, earl, viscount, and baron. These noble ranks were not equal in dignity, yet all alike were the Son of Heaven’s subjects. They had always scrupulously observed the rules governing the lords; now, seeing the royal administration renewed, they became still firmer in their loyalty and constancy. They had faithfully followed the established statutes; now, looking up to the great resurgence of royal authority, they became still more earnest in their devotion.
They knew that the king’s examination of institutions and measures was entirely for the people’s sake. Thus, their obedient acceptance of his virtuous intentions was expressed in more than the rites of court attendance and diplomatic visits. In everything that involved spreading the five moral teachings, making timely use of the land’s resources, and bringing together what the people desired, they made provision for each undertaking. They knew that the king’s suppression of disorder was likewise for the people’s sake. Thus, their response to and propagation of his beneficent commands were expressed in more than military campaigns. In everything that involved investigating wickedness, punishing violence and disorder, and removing …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
民之所惡者靡不曲爲之防焉外攘之舉卽內
治之脩其在外服者猶其在內服也孰有違上
所命而棄于王化之外者哉畏威之念卽懷德
之心其在大邦者猶其在小邦也孰有自作不
典以干夫王法之譴者哉吁觀此而周王大一
統之治可見矣抑成王承文武之後謨烈具存
固無所謂不庭者淮夷之征止于一隅又安有
所謂四征哉史臣紀成王之初政固以見安不
忘危之心亦以見王者無外之化耳噫有周官
===
以訓百官則自公孤而至卿牧皆有常職治人
備矣有周禮以治天下則自朝廷而達邦國皆
有常禮治法具矣人法具備此有周之治所以
享國長久也歟
詩
天生烝民有物有則民之秉彞好是懿德
王弘誨
同考試官教諭蕭 批 〔此題性理之學場中作者非浮卽枯是篇以本色語發之沛然殆無餘蘊〕
punctuated:
民之所惡者，靡不曲爲之防焉。外攘之舉，卽內治之脩；其在外服者，猶其在內服也，孰有違上所命而棄于王化之外者哉？畏威之念，卽懷德之心；其在大邦者，猶其在小邦也，孰有自作不典以干夫王法之譴者哉？吁！觀此而周王大一統之治可見矣。抑成王承文武之後，謨烈具存，固無所謂不庭者；淮夷之征，止于一隅，又安有所謂四征哉？史臣紀成王之初政，固以見安不忘危之心，亦以見王者無外之化耳。噫！有《周官》以訓百官，則自公孤而至卿牧，皆有常職，治人備矣；有《周禮》以治天下，則自朝廷而達邦國，皆有常禮，治法具矣。人法具備，此有周之治所以享國長久也歟？

詩
天生烝民，有物有則。民之秉彞，好是懿德。
王弘誨
同考試官教諭蕭批〔此題性理之學，場中作者非浮卽枯。是篇以本色語發之，沛然殆無餘蘊〕
translation_en:
…whatever the people detested, they invariably took every care to guard against it. Repelling external threats was itself the cultivation of internal government. Those in the outer domains were like those in the inner domains: who would disobey commands from above and cast himself beyond the king’s transforming influence? Awe before his might was itself affection for his virtue. Those in the great states were like those in the small states: who would commit unlawful acts on his own initiative and incur condemnation under the king’s laws? Ah! In this we can see the comprehensive unity of the Zhou king’s government. Yet King Cheng succeeded Kings Wen and Wu, whose plans and achievements remained fully intact; surely there were none who refused to attend his court. The campaign against the Huai Yi was confined to a single corner of the realm: how, then, could there have been campaigns in all four directions? In recording King Cheng’s early government, the court historian certainly showed his resolve not to forget danger in times of peace, but also showed that the king’s transforming influence excluded no one.

Ah! With the Officers of Zhou to instruct the officials, all—from the Three Dukes and Three Solitaries down to the ministers and regional governors—had their regular duties: the personnel for government were fully provided. With the Rites of Zhou to govern all under Heaven, all—from the royal court to the various states—had their regular rites: the institutions of government were fully established. With both personnel and institutions fully provided, was this not why the Zhou government preserved its dynasty for so long?

Book of Odes
“Heaven gives birth to the multitude of people; for every thing there is a norm. The people hold fast to their constant nature and love this beautiful virtue.”
Wang Honghui
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: 〔This topic concerns the study of human nature and principle. Those writing on it in the examination hall are either superficial or dry. This essay expounds it in plain, natural language, with such abundance that scarcely any underlying meaning remains unexpressed.〕…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其深造而有得者歟
同考試官教諭曾批發則與彝德處精潤透
徹可與語心學矣
考試官教諭黃批善發性情之蘊足見理
者
考試官學正宋批至微之理文足以發
詩人原天之生人性善而情亦善也蓋性命於
天而情發乎性本無不善也天之所以生人者
固如此哉昔尹吉甫作詩以送仲山甫而推其
===
所由生也若曰明於天之道者斯可以言性察
於民之故者斯可以言情求之生人之初而知
天之所以篤生賢哲矣是故天之生烝民也太
極儲其精未有物先而此理爲之不息二五凝
其化既有物後而此理爲之各具由氣而生者
必有主乎氣者畀之以昭當然之極蓋時有古
今而此無虧欠也依形而立者必有形而上者
付之以植天然之中蓋人有智愚而此無豐嗇
也是物則也帝降之衷本之於有生之初而恒
punctuated:
其深造而有得者歟？

同考試官教諭曾批：發則與彝德處，精潤透徹，可與語心學矣。

考試官教諭黃批：善發性情之蘊，足見理者。

考試官學正宋批：至微之理，文足以發。

詩人原天之生人，性善而情亦善也。蓋性命於天，而情發乎性，本無不善也。天之所以生人者，固如此哉！昔尹吉甫作詩以送仲山甫，而推其所由生也。若曰：明於天之道者，斯可以言性；察於民之故者，斯可以言情。求之生人之初，而知天之所以篤生賢哲矣。是故天之生烝民也，太極儲其精，未有物先，而此理爲之不息；二五凝其化，既有物後，而此理爲之各具。由氣而生者，必有主乎氣者，畀之以昭當然之極，蓋時有古今，而此無虧欠也；依形而立者，必有形而上者，付之以植天然之中，蓋人有智愚，而此無豐嗇也。是物則也，帝降之衷，本之於有生之初，而恒
translation_en:
…Is he not one who has pursued his studies deeply and gained an understanding of his own?

Associate Examiner Zeng, an Instructor, comments: “The passages expounding the norms and the enduring virtues are refined, rich, and penetrating. Here is someone with whom one can discuss the learning of the mind.”

Examiner Huang, an Instructor, comments: “He skillfully reveals the depths of human nature and feelings, sufficiently demonstrating his understanding of principle.”

Examiner Song, a Director of Studies, comments: “His writing adequately reveals the most subtle principles.”

The poet traces Heaven’s generation of human beings to its source: their nature is good, and their feelings are good as well. For human nature is ordained by Heaven, while feelings issue from that nature; originally, neither is anything but good. Surely this is how Heaven generates human beings! In former times, Yin Jifu composed a poem to send off Zhong Shanfu and traced the source of his coming into being. It was as though he said: Only those who understand Heaven’s Way can speak of human nature; only those who discern the circumstances of the people can speak of feelings. By seeking at the very beginning of human generation, one comes to understand how Heaven brings forth worthy and wise men in abundance.

Thus, when Heaven generates the multitude of people, the Supreme Ultimate holds its essence in store: before things exist, this principle operates unceasingly. The two forces and five phases consolidate their transformations: after things exist, this principle is fully present in each. Whatever is born through material force must be endowed with that which governs material force, thereby making manifest the ultimate standard of what ought to be. Though times differ as ancient and modern, in this there is no deficiency. Whatever is established through physical form must be entrusted with that which is above physical form, thereby implanting the mean bestowed by Heaven. Though people differ in wisdom and foolishness, in this there is neither abundance nor scarcity. These are the things and their norms. The balanced endowment sent down by the Lord on High is rooted in the very beginning of life, and the enduring…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
性在焉原於天而不可易者備於已而不可離
也繼善之理得之為固有之良而成性存焉命
之流行而不已者性之一定而不移也非民之
秉彝乎是以至德中涵旣原天下之一而無有
不善故循性而動自統天下之同而無不好善
好爵之縻根心而不容已理與心融未有人而
不好是德者其諸天下之達德乎理義之悅同
然而無所間心與理契未有懿德而人不好之
者其諸人情之大順乎茲見性情之善賦予之
===
===
公夫人之同得於天者而山甫獨全美德此所
以異於凡民歟雖然心統性情者也惟能善事
其心然後是非好惡出於性情自無不正此大
較也仲山甫小心翼翼大本已端故能不茹不
吐保身事君職業備舉以光中興偉業而為當
時之賢佐也吉甫之言不為無助矣故曰為此
詩者其知道乎
我受命溥將自天降康豐年穰穰
鍾維藩
punctuated:
性在焉。原於天而不可易者，備於已而不可離也。繼善之理，得之為固有之良，而成性存焉。命之流行而不已者，性之一定而不移也。非民之秉彝乎？是以至德中涵，旣原天下之一而無有不善，故循性而動，自統天下之同而無不好善。好爵之縻，根心而不容已，理與心融，未有人而不好是德者，其諸天下之達德乎？理義之悅，同然而無所間，心與理契，未有懿德而人不好之者，其諸人情之大順乎？茲見性情之善，賦予之公。夫人之同得於天者，而山甫獨全美德，此所以異於凡民歟？雖然，心統性情者也。惟能善事其心，然後是非好惡出於性情，自無不正，此大較也。仲山甫小心翼翼，大本已端，故能不茹不吐，保身事君，職業備舉，以光中興偉業，而為當時之賢佐也。吉甫之言，不為無助矣。故曰：「為此詩者，其知道乎？」
「我受命溥將，自天降康，豐年穰穰。」
鍾維藩
translation_en:
…nature resides therein. What originates in Heaven and cannot be altered is fully present in oneself and cannot be separated from oneself. The principle whose continuation is goodness is received as one's inherent goodness, and therein resides the nature brought to completion. What flows unceasingly as Heaven's mandate is fixed and unchanging as human nature. Is this not the enduring norm that the people hold fast to? Thus, consummate virtue is contained within: its source is the unity underlying all under Heaven, and nothing in it is other than good. Accordingly, when people act in accordance with their nature, they share what is common to all under Heaven, and none fails to love goodness. The bond of noble rank [?] is rooted in the heart and cannot be restrained. Principle and the heart are united; no person fails to love this virtue. Is this not the virtue universally shared throughout the world? The delight in principle and righteousness is alike in everyone, admitting no division. The heart accords with principle; there is no admirable virtue that people fail to love. Is this not the great accord of human feelings? Here we see the goodness of human nature and feelings, and the impartiality with which they are bestowed.
What people alike receive from Heaven was nevertheless preserved in its full excellence by Shanfu alone: is this what distinguished him from ordinary people? Yet the heart governs both nature and feelings. Only when one can properly tend one's heart will judgments of right and wrong, likes and dislikes, issue from one's nature and feelings with nothing that is not correct. This is the general outline. Zhong Shanfu was cautious and reverent; the great foundation within him was already upright. Thus he neither swallowed the weak nor spat out the strong, preserved himself while serving his ruler, and fulfilled all the duties of his office. He thereby brought lustre to the great achievement of dynastic restoration and became a worthy assistant of his age. The words of Jifu were not without their contribution. Hence it is said: “Did not the author of this poem understand the Way?”
“I have received a mandate vast and great; from Heaven descends peace, and abundant harvests come in profusion.”
Zhong Weifan.

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭蕭批受命降康處都是得天
是篇以此貫說甚有照應且詞藻煥發盛世之音
也取式多士
同考試官教諭曾批題意正大士子多□陳
言束縛未見發明是作清暢脫俗塲中少見錄之
考試官教諭黃批語明意盡善作頌者
考試官學正宋批文思雋永且得詩人口
氣
商王膺天眷之隆而獲有年之慶此祀典之由
===
秩也夫君德莫大於得天也商王祀事之所由
備者何莫而非天之所與哉此祀成湯之樂及
此若曰王者繼統而御世也固天命之所歸而
備物以用享也亦天休之所及蓋商之先后受
命固不殆矣使不得乎天亦不敢以祭也今則
保玆世序而景命之有僕者以一人而統其盛
克享天心而駿命之不易者以一身而會其全
臨君師之任而貴爲天子所以主鬯而殷薦者
此也昭受于天不旣廣乎紹神明之統而富有
punctuated:
同考試官教諭蕭批：受命降康處，都是得天。是篇以此貫說，甚有照應，且詞藻煥發，盛世之音也，取式多士。

同考試官教諭曾批：題意正大，士子多□陳言束縛，未見發明。是作清暢脫俗，塲中少見，錄之。

考試官教諭黃批：語明意盡，善作頌者。

考試官學正宋批：文思雋永，且得詩人口氣。

商王膺天眷之隆，而獲有年之慶，此祀典之由秩也。夫君德莫大於得天也。商王祀事之所由備者，何莫而非天之所與哉？此祀成湯之樂及此，若曰：王者繼統而御世也，固天命之所歸；而備物以用享也，亦天休之所及。蓋商之先后受命，固不殆矣。使不得乎天，亦不敢以祭也。今則保玆世序，而景命之有僕者，以一人而統其盛；克享天心，而駿命之不易者，以一身而會其全。臨君師之任，而貴爲天子，所以主鬯而殷薦者此也。昭受于天，不旣廣乎？紹神明之統，而富有
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Xiao, an Instructor, comments: Both “receiving the mandate” and “sending down well-being” concern gaining Heaven’s favor. This essay develops that idea throughout, with excellent correspondence between its parts. Its language is also brilliant—the voice of a flourishing age. It is selected as a model for the many candidates.

Associate Examiner Zeng, an Instructor, comments: The topic’s meaning is upright and grand. Most candidates are constrained by conventional expressions [one character illegible], without offering fresh elucidation. This composition is lucid, fluent, and free of commonplace writing, something seldom seen in the examination hall. It is included here.

Examiner Huang, an Instructor, comments: The language is clear and the meaning fully expressed: a writer skilled in composing hymns of praise.

Examiner Song, a School Instructor, comments: The essay’s thought has lasting savor, and it also captures the poet’s voice.

The king of Shang received Heaven’s abundant favor and enjoyed the blessing of a plentiful harvest: this is why the sacrificial observances were duly ordered. Of all a ruler’s virtues, none is greater than gaining Heaven’s favor. What enabled the king of Shang to provide fully for the sacrifices, if not Heaven’s gifts in every instance? The music for the sacrifice to Cheng Tang touches upon this, as if to say: When a king succeeds to the royal line and governs the world, he is indeed the one upon whom Heaven’s mandate rests; when he prepares the offerings for sacrifice, he likewise enjoys Heaven’s blessings. The former sovereigns of Shang had assuredly received the mandate. Had they not gained Heaven’s favor, they would not have dared to offer sacrifice.

Now, preserving this succession through the generations, the king gathers in his single person the full splendor of the great mandate bestowed repeatedly upon his line. Having won Heaven’s favor, he embodies in his own person the entirety of that mighty mandate, so difficult to maintain. Undertaking the responsibilities of ruler and teacher, and honored as the Son of Heaven, he thereby presides over the sacrificial wine and makes abundant offerings. Is not what he manifestly receives from Heaven exceedingly extensive? Continuing the divinely enlightened succession, and possessing in abundance …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
四海所以假廟而萃渙者此也靈承于帝不旣
大乎夫我之受命固溥將矣使年不順成亦難
乎其成享也兹則天心仁愛而太和之氣布濩
於兩間厚之以明昭之賜帝命不違而絪縕之
化徧及於庶彙畀之以大有之祥我田旣臧普
美利於不言而黍稷介倉箱之富則夫載清酤
而賫思成者其將有攸賴乎我稼旣同示豐亨
於有象而收成極萬億之多則夫戒和羹而綏
眉壽者其將有所資乎夫受命之隆是天與之
===
使之主祭也降康之裕是天與之得以備物也
由是而假先獲福也固其所哉抑成湯敬德享
天已非一日而桑林數語尤足以綿亳都命脉
之長故奕世發祥豐年疊見脩禮作樂致力於
廟祏上下洽神人聲靈所振天地為昭而玄王
之緒賴以不墜何者而非先澤之所留也噫頌
明德歸功於祖受明命求端於天若湯孫者其
察於天人之道也歟
春秋
punctuated:
四海，所以假廟而萃渙者，此也。靈承于帝，不旣大乎？夫我之受命固溥將矣，使年不順成，亦難乎其成享也。兹則天心仁愛，而太和之氣布濩於兩間，厚之以明昭之賜；帝命不違，而絪縕之化徧及於庶彙，畀之以大有之祥。我田旣臧，普美利於不言，而黍稷介倉箱之富，則夫載清酤而賫思成者，其將有攸賴乎？我稼旣同，示豐亨於有象，而收成極萬億之多，則夫戒和羹而綏眉壽者，其將有所資乎？夫受命之隆，是天與之使之主祭也；降康之裕，是天與之得以備物也。由是而假先獲福也，固其所哉！抑成湯敬德享天，已非一日，而桑林數語，尤足以綿亳都命脉之長。故奕世發祥，豐年疊見，脩禮作樂，致力於廟祏，上下洽神人，聲靈所振，天地為昭，而玄王之緒賴以不墜。何者而非先澤之所留也？噫！頌明德，歸功於祖；受明命，求端於天。若湯孫者，其察於天人之道也歟！

春秋
translation_en:
…all within the Four Seas: this is what enables him to enter the ancestral temple and gather together what is dispersed. Is not his wondrous reception of the Supreme Lord’s favor indeed great? The mandate we have received is surely vast and mighty; yet, if the year did not bring a successful harvest, it would still be difficult to complete the sacrificial offering. Now Heaven’s heart is benevolent and loving, and the breath of supreme harmony spreads between Heaven and Earth, enriching us with its radiant gifts. The Supreme Lord’s mandate does not fail, and the transforming power of intermingling cosmic forces reaches every kind of being, bestowing the auspicious blessing of great abundance. Our fields are good: Heaven silently extends its benefits everywhere, and the millet adds to the wealth of granaries and carts. Thus, when we bring clear sacrificial wine and seek the fulfillment of our thoughts of the ancestors, shall we not have something upon which to rely? Our crops have all ripened together: abundance manifests itself in visible form, and the harvest reaches countless millions. Thus, when we prepare the seasoned broth and seek the blessing of long life, shall we not have the means to do so?

The exalted mandate we have received is Heaven’s gift, enabling us to preside over the sacrifices; the ample prosperity sent down is Heaven’s gift, enabling us to provide the offerings. That we thereby approach our ancestors and receive blessings is surely fitting! Moreover, Cheng Tang had long revered virtue and offered sacrifice to Heaven, and the few words of his prayer at Sanglin were especially sufficient to prolong the lifeblood of the capital at Bo. Thus, auspicious signs appeared generation after generation, and abundant harvests followed one another. Rituals were cultivated and music composed, and devoted service was rendered at the ancestral temple and its spirit tablets. Those above and below brought spirits and men into harmony; wherever their awe-inspiring spiritual power reached, Heaven and Earth shone forth, and the legacy of the Dark King was thereby preserved from falling away. What among these things was not a blessing left by the ancestors? Ah! In praising illustrious virtue, they credited their ancestors; in receiving the illustrious mandate, they sought its source in Heaven. Did not the descendants of Tang discern the Way of Heaven and humanity!

Spring and Autumn Annals

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
秋及江人黃人伐陳僖公四年
馬象乾
同考試官教諭翟批此題會合兩傳以見齊
桓之得失作者牽制文義難於峻整是篇渾融精
切且有斷制宜錄之以式多士
考試官教諭黃批得聖人予奪之旨
考試官學正宋批體裁正大
伯主用遠國以討貳春秋善其謀而病其德也
此齊於江黃用以制楚則善用以虐陳則非也
===
而功過不相掩矣且轅濤塗倡避軍之謀申侯
行師老之譖齊桓所爲怒也乃率江黃以伐之
夫伐陳而後動二國之兵前此未之與也何以
爲驗其謀也蓋用師之道貴萬全而取勝故有
正有奇法之所以爲善也彼楚之陵駕中華也
得非以江黃與國爲之捍蔽矣乎齊欲制楚而
非此以爲掎角之資吾見厚集之衆雖當其前
八國之師孰援其後二廣之雄未可以遽帖也
惟其申以陽谷之好授以按兵之寄迨夫盟禮
punctuated:
秋，及江人、黃人伐陳。僖公四年。
馬象乾
同考試官教諭翟批：此題會合兩傳，以見齊桓之得失。作者牽制文義，難於峻整。是篇渾融精切，且有斷制，宜錄之以式多士。
考試官教諭黃批：得聖人予奪之旨。
考試官學正宋批：體裁正大。
伯主用遠國以討貳，春秋善其謀而病其德也。此齊於江黃，用以制楚則善，用以虐陳則非也，而功過不相掩矣。且轅濤塗倡避軍之謀，申侯行師老之譖，齊桓所爲怒也，乃率江黃以伐之。夫伐陳而後動二國之兵，前此未之與也，何以爲驗其謀也？蓋用師之道，貴萬全而取勝，故有正有奇，法之所以爲善也。彼楚之陵駕中華也，得非以江黃與國爲之捍蔽矣乎？齊欲制楚，而非此以爲掎角之資，吾見厚集之衆雖當其前，八國之師孰援其後？二廣之雄，未可以遽帖也。惟其申以陽谷之好，授以按兵之寄，迨夫盟禮
translation_en:
“In autumn, [we] joined the men of Jiang and Huang in attacking Chen.” Fourth year of Duke Xi.
Ma Xianggan
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhai, Instructor: This topic brings together the two commentaries to reveal Duke Huan of Qi’s successes and failings. Writers are constrained by the meaning of the text and find it difficult to achieve a sharply defined, orderly treatment. This essay is integrated, precise, and pertinent, and also offers decisive judgments. It should be recorded as a model for the candidates.
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: It grasps the Sage’s intent in granting approval and withholding it.
Comment by Examiner Song, School Director: Its form and style are correct and dignified.
When the hegemon employed distant states to punish disloyalty, the Spring and Autumn Annals approved his strategy but found fault with his virtue. In this instance, Qi’s employment of Jiang and Huang to check Chu was commendable; employing them to oppress Chen was wrong. His achievement and his fault do not obscure one another.
Yuan Taotu proposed a plan to divert the army, while Lord Shen slanderously alleged that this would exhaust the troops. This was what angered Duke Huan of Qi, who consequently led Jiang and Huang in attacking Chen. Only when attacking Chen did he mobilize the forces of these two states; previously they had not participated. How does this attest to his strategy?
The art of employing armies prizes attaining victory with complete security. Thus there are both regular and extraordinary methods: this is what makes military methods effective. Was not Chu’s domination of the Central States due to its allies Jiang and Huang serving as its protective screen? If Qi wished to restrain Chu but did not use these states to provide a coordinated attack from different directions, I contend that, though its massed forces might confront Chu’s front, who among the armies of the eight states would strike at its rear in support? The might of Chu’s two chariot divisions could not readily be subdued.
It was precisely because he renewed the friendship established at Yanggu and entrusted them with holding their troops in readiness that, when the covenant ceremony …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之既定然後連兵以伐陳則知侵蔡次陘之不
與者非不用夫江黃也羽翼方城之外使進焉
有所憑坐制漢水之境使退焉有所據伏至險
於大順藏不測於至靜兵法之奇將以待敵之
可勝者也斯非謀之成乎夫師老而後致不共
之問兵出非無名也何以為病其德也蓋持勝
之道貴克終而不替故有容有忍德之所以為
大也彼陳之謀避軍道也無乃以伯政無良莫
之攸思矣乎齊欲討陳而反巳以省見斁之由
===
吾見愛人不親將以反仁治人不治將以反智
一謀之愆何至於大逞也夫何恣勝外之餘威
忘輔伯之舊好械執之辱未巳撻伐之師繼之
其視勤鄭禮楚之不同者非偶拂其初心也志
溢於功成之後而弗克自持氣驕於克敵之餘
而莫能自抑包荒之量巳淺容受之度不弘匡
救之仁假之不久而遽歸者也斯非德之衰乎
噫此一役也明於制楚而暗於懷陳桓之得失
如此宜其止於伯而不得進於王也抑考江黃
punctuated: 之既定，然後連兵以伐陳，則知侵蔡次陘之不與者，非不用夫江黃也。羽翼方城之外，使進焉有所憑；坐制漢水之境，使退焉有所據。伏至險於大順，藏不測於至靜，兵法之奇，將以待敵之可勝者也。斯非謀之成乎？夫師老而後致不共之問，兵出非無名也，何以為病其德也？蓋持勝之道，貴克終而不替，故有容有忍，德之所以為大也。彼陳之謀避軍道也，無乃以伯政無良，莫之攸思矣乎？齊欲討陳，而反巳以省見斁之由，吾見愛人不親，將以反仁；治人不治，將以反智。一謀之愆，何至於大逞也？夫何恣勝外之餘威，忘輔伯之舊好，械執之辱未巳，撻伐之師繼之？其視勤鄭禮楚之不同者，非偶拂其初心也。志溢於功成之後，而弗克自持；氣驕於克敵之餘，而莫能自抑。包荒之量巳淺，容受之度不弘，匡救之仁，假之不久而遽歸者也。斯非德之衰乎？噫！此一役也，明於制楚而暗於懷陳。桓之得失如此，宜其止於伯而不得進於王也。抑考江黃
translation_en:
…once the covenant rites had been settled, only then did they join forces to attack Chen. Thus we know that Jiang and Huang’s absence from the invasion of Cai and the encampment at Xing did not mean that their forces went unused. They provided support beyond Fangcheng, giving the advancing army something to rely upon; they held command over the Han River region, giving it a secure position should it retreat. Concealing the utmost danger within complete conformity, and hiding the unpredictable within perfect stillness—these were unconventional military methods, awaiting the moment when the enemy could be defeated. Was this not the successful realization of his strategy?

Now, only after the army had grown weary did he call Chen to account for its failure to render service [?]. The expedition was not without a stated justification. Why, then, should it be considered a flaw in his virtue? The way to preserve victory depends upon carrying through to the end without decline. Hence magnanimity and forbearance are what make virtue great. As for Chen’s scheme to divert the army’s route away from itself, was it not perhaps because the hegemon’s government lacked goodness and gave Chen no consideration? Had Qi, when wishing to punish Chen, instead examined itself to discover why it had become an object of aversion, I believe it would have reflected upon its benevolence when its love for others brought no affection in return, and upon its wisdom when its government of others failed to bring order. How could the fault of a single scheme justify giving such full vent to its anger?

Why indulge the lingering might of victory abroad and forget the old friendship that had supported his hegemony? Before the humiliation of arrest and shackling was over, a punitive army followed. The contrast with his solicitude for Zheng and his courtesy toward Chu was no mere accidental departure from his original intentions. After success, his ambitions overflowed and he could no longer restrain himself; after overcoming his enemies, his spirit grew arrogant and he could no longer curb it. His capacity to embrace others’ shortcomings had already become shallow, and his tolerance was narrow. The benevolence with which he had set the world right and rescued it was something he had borrowed, only to return it hastily after a short time. Was this not the decline of his virtue?

Alas! In this single campaign, he understood how to check Chu but failed to understand how to win Chen’s allegiance. Such were Duke Huan’s successes and failings. It is fitting that he attained only hegemony and could not advance to true kingship. Yet, if we examine Jiang and Huang…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
受盟管仲能鏡其終矣殊無一語以箴伐陳之
失豈其懵於此也蓋量淺之桓而仲以小器佐
之數年經營惟一楚耳召陵之後侈心生焉自
脩乏制心之學事君無格心之功宜誠偽勤怠
互異如此然一匡之績叔世賴焉聖人且以仁
稱之仲固不可多得也
春公孫歸父會楚子于宋宣公十有五年
關玉成
同考試官教諭翟批發揮聖人經世之略精
===
確顯明是深于經學者
考試官教諭黃批詞嚴義正
考試官學正宋批整飭有體
春秋志望國交外之迹所以示經世之略也此
觀魯之屈志以下楚其自治者疎矣春秋得無
譏乎昔楚師在宋虐焰張甚魯宣懼其及也乃
從獻子之謀遣歸父而為宋之會君子所以譏
之者蓋以攘夷安夏匡時之偉略强本治內保
邦之良圖當時荊楚為讎於大邦重兵橫加于
punctuated:
受盟，管仲能鏡其終矣，殊無一語以箴伐陳之失，豈其懵於此也？蓋量淺之桓，而仲以小器佐之，數年經營，惟一楚耳。召陵之後，侈心生焉，自脩乏制心之學，事君無格心之功，宜誠偽勤怠互異如此。然一匡之績，叔世賴焉，聖人且以仁稱之，仲固不可多得也。
春，公孫歸父會楚子于宋。宣公十有五年。
關玉成
同考試官教諭翟批：發揮聖人經世之略，精確顯明，是深于經學者。
考試官教諭黃批：詞嚴義正。
考試官學正宋批：整飭有體。
春秋志望國交外之迹，所以示經世之略也。此觀魯之屈志以下楚，其自治者疎矣，春秋得無譏乎？昔楚師在宋，虐焰張甚，魯宣懼其及也，乃從獻子之謀，遣歸父而為宋之會。君子所以譏之者，蓋以攘夷安夏，匡時之偉略；强本治內，保邦之良圖。當時荊楚為讎於大邦，重兵橫加于
translation_en:
…when they entered the covenant, Guan Zhong could foresee how it would end. Yet he offered not a single word to remonstrate against the error of attacking Chen. Could he have been ignorant of this? Duke Huan was limited in magnanimity, and Zhong assisted him with his own narrow capacity. Their several years of planning were directed solely at Chu. After Shaoling, extravagant ambitions arose. In cultivating himself, Zhong lacked the learning needed to govern his own mind; in serving his ruler, he failed to rectify his ruler’s mind. It is therefore understandable that sincerity and insincerity, diligence and indolence, alternated in this way. Nevertheless, his achievement in restoring order sustained a declining age. Even the Sage praised him for benevolence. Men like Zhong were indeed rare.
“In spring, Gongsun Guifu met the Viscount of Chu at Song.” Fifteenth year of Duke Xuan.
Guan Yucheng
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhai, Instructor: “This elucidates the Sage’s strategy for ordering the world with precision and clarity. Here is someone deeply versed in classical scholarship.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The language is rigorous and the principles correct.”
Comment by Examiner Song, School Instructor: “Orderly and well composed.”
The Spring and Autumn Annals records the dealings of prominent states [?] with outside powers in order to reveal a strategy for ordering the world. Here we see Lu compromising its aspirations to submit to Chu: its efforts to put its own affairs in order were lax. Could the Spring and Autumn Annals refrain from censuring it? Formerly, when Chu’s army was in Song and its violent aggression raged fiercely, Duke Xuan of Lu feared that it would reach him. He therefore followed Xianzi’s counsel and sent Guifu to hold the meeting at Song. The reason the gentleman censures this is that repelling the outsiders and securing the Xia states was the great strategy for setting the age right, while strengthening the foundations and ordering internal affairs was the sound plan for preserving the state. At that time, Jing-Chu was acting as an enemy to the great states, wantonly bringing its mighty army to bear upon…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
上國其目中已無諸夏矣此不獨當為宋人計
當為天下計也魯宣於此誠能擇義而行則畏
簡書以攘夷狄存先代於垂亡此其策之上也
如欲相時而動則嚴兵旅以為聲援消外患於
方張未為謀之失也奈何內政罔脩惟懷不免
之懼剝牀是慮遂忘下比之傷周公之裔義非
不明也以此制人何向而不克顧乏有為之志
未及而薦賄何其鄙也千乘之國力非不足也
以此備豫何敵之敢窺顧忽深長之思千里而
===
畏人何其陋也若曰庭實之獻以脩睦也然鄰
封告急乃以壇坫之好而往與亂華者同焉屈
我之體而示之弱使益肆其桀驁之威則將何
以待之若曰禮幣之交以行成也然四境無虞
乃以下敵之禮而遠於殘夏者施焉畏人之勢
而中之利使益恣其無厭之求又將何以應之
魯之君臣筭不及此何國之能為也吾知非惟
無以制楚也適以長楚憑陵之志非惟無以恤
宋也適以怠宋堅守之心夷夏盛衰之由蓋決
punctuated: 上國，其目中已無諸夏矣。此不獨當為宋人計，當為天下計也。魯宣於此誠能擇義而行，則畏簡書以攘夷狄，存先代於垂亡，此其策之上也。如欲相時而動，則嚴兵旅以為聲援，消外患於方張，未為謀之失也。奈何內政罔脩，惟懷不免之懼，剝牀是慮，遂忘下比之傷。周公之裔，義非不明也，以此制人，何向而不克？顧乏有為之志，未及而薦賄，何其鄙也！千乘之國，力非不足也，以此備豫，何敵之敢窺？顧忽深長之思，千里而畏人，何其陋也！若曰庭實之獻以脩睦也，然鄰封告急，乃以壇坫之好而往，與亂華者同焉，屈我之體而示之弱，使益肆其桀驁之威，則將何以待之？若曰禮幣之交以行成也，然四境無虞，乃以下敵之禮而遠於殘夏者施焉，畏人之勢而中之利，使益恣其無厭之求，又將何以應之？魯之君臣筭不及此，何國之能為也？吾知非惟無以制楚也，適以長楚憑陵之志；非惟無以恤宋也，適以怠宋堅守之心。夷夏盛衰之由，蓋決
translation_en:
…the central states; in its eyes, the states of Xia already counted for nothing. This called for deliberation not merely on behalf of the people of Song, but on behalf of all under Heaven. Had Duke Xuan of Lu truly chosen to act according to righteousness in these circumstances, he would have stood in awe of the royal commands, driven back the Yi and Di, and preserved the state descended from a former dynasty when it stood on the brink of destruction. This would have been his best policy. If he wished instead to assess the circumstances before acting, he could have put his troops in readiness to provide supporting force and checked the external threat while it was growing. That, too, would not have been a mistaken plan. Why, then, did he neglect internal government and harbor only the fear that he would not escape? Concerned only that destruction would reach his very bed, he forgot the harm of subordinating himself to an unworthy power. As a descendant of the Duke of Zhou, he was surely not ignorant of righteousness. Had he used it to restrain others, where could he have turned without success? Yet he lacked the resolve to act, presenting gifts before the danger had even reached him. How contemptible! As ruler of a state of a thousand chariots, he surely did not lack strength. Had he used it to prepare his defenses, what enemy would have dared covet his territory? Yet he neglected far-reaching reflection and feared another power a thousand li away. How small-minded!

One might say that presenting gifts in the court was a means of cultivating amity. Yet when a neighboring state appealed for help, he went instead to establish ceremonial friendship, joining those who were throwing the Hua states into disorder. By lowering his own standing and displaying weakness, he would allow them to wield their overbearing might still more freely. How, then, would he deal with them? One might say that exchanging ceremonial gifts was a means of making peace. Yet when his own borders were free of danger, he went far afield to offer the rites of submission to an enemy that was ravaging the Xia states. By fearing another power’s might and serving its interests, he would allow it to indulge its insatiable demands still further. How, then, would he answer them? If the ruler and ministers of Lu failed to reckon with these consequences, how could they govern a state? I know that this not only failed to restrain Chu; it positively encouraged Chu’s ambition to dominate and encroach. It not only failed to aid Song; it positively weakened Song’s resolve to hold firm. The rise and decline of the Yi and Xia were surely determined…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
於此矣聖人脩經至此蓋曰中國有常尊之體
則外勢自屈有常勝之謀則外侮自消治內以
馭外蓄威以奠邦斯非經世者所宜知乎直書
其事而義自見矣抑楚之橫晉成之也徇小利
而忽遠猷楚得以竊義自張矣桓文而在能無
少戢乎魯宣負惡而不能自固齊猶足以奔走
之欲其不惴於楚焉難矣然華元當危急而不
受城下之盟曾於無事乃切後時之虞何節槩
之相遠也君子於獻子有遺論矣其於宣也何
===
尤
禮記
故樂者天地之命中和之紀人情之所不
能免也
陳維翰
同考試官教諭曾 批 命紀必須融會體貼上
文作者不泛則統此篇意盡而詞復警健可式
考試官教諭黃 批 詞意精確
考試官學正宋 批 明順
punctuated:
於此矣。聖人脩經至此，蓋曰：中國有常尊之體，則外勢自屈；有常勝之謀，則外侮自消。治內以馭外，蓄威以奠邦，斯非經世者所宜知乎？直書其事，而義自見矣。抑楚之橫，晉成之也。徇小利而忽遠猷，楚得以竊義自張矣。桓文而在，能無少戢乎？魯宣負惡而不能自固，齊猶足以奔走之，欲其不惴於楚焉，難矣。然華元當危急而不受城下之盟，曾於無事乃切後時之虞，何節槩之相遠也！君子於獻子有遺論矣，其於宣也何尤？

禮記
故樂者，天地之命，中和之紀，人情之所不能免也。
陳維翰

同考試官教諭曾批：命紀必須融會體貼上文，作者不泛，則統此篇意盡，而詞復警健，可式。
考試官教諭黃批：詞意精確。
考試官學正宋批：明順。
translation_en:
…was determined by this. When the Sage reached this point in compiling the Classic, his meaning was surely this: if the Central States maintain an enduringly honorable standing, outside powers will submit of themselves; if they possess plans that consistently secure victory, foreign aggression will subside of itself. To govern within so as to control what lies beyond, and to build up authority so as to secure the state—is this not what those who would order the world ought to understand? He records the events directly, and their moral significance becomes apparent of itself.

Yet it was Jin that enabled Chu’s arrogance. Pursuing petty gains while neglecting far-reaching plans, Jin allowed Chu to appropriate the mantle of righteousness and magnify its own power. Had Duke Huan and Duke Wen been alive, could Chu have failed to show at least some restraint? Duke Xuan of Lu, burdened with wrongdoing and unable to secure his own position, could be made to run at Qi’s bidding alone; it would have been difficult to expect him not to tremble before Chu. Yet Hua Yuan, in a moment of grave danger, refused a covenant imposed beneath the city walls, whereas in a time free of trouble, there was such acute anxiety about being too late. How far apart these displays of integrity were! The gentleman has further criticism to make of Xianzi; what blame, then, need he lay upon Duke Xuan?

Book of Rites
“Thus music is the mandate of Heaven and Earth, the ordering principle of equilibrium and harmony, and something human feelings cannot do without.”
Chen Weihan

Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor: “The words ‘mandate’ and ‘ordering principle’ must be understood together and grasped in close relation to the preceding text. The writer avoids generalities and thus comprehensively draws together the meaning of this chapter. His language is also striking and vigorous, worthy of serving as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The language and ideas are precise.”

Comment by Examiner Song, School Instructor: “Clear and fluent.”

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
論正樂之在人其功大而不可離也蓋人莫不
有天地中和之理也樂以命之紀之人情其得
而免乎樂記結言樂之切於人也曰人知凡樂
之動不能外乎情而不知人情之治實有資於
樂蓋甞於其聲容之感化者而觀其深矣今夫
天地之賦於人者有曰親曰敬曰順之道焉樂
聲之作而因以廣之則德音之洋溢有以感觸
夫天性之眞中聲之揄楊有以啓發其秉彝之
懿以達其神以興其德而凡天地之所不及者
===
皆正樂以鼓舞之也樂非天地之命乎中和之
具於人者有曰莊曰正曰齊之儀焉樂舞之舉
而因以飭之則干羽之習合有以遠暴慢而攝
威儀綴兆之周旋有以黜邪僻而全恭敬以動
血脉以通精神而凡中和之在於吾身者皆正
樂以綱維之也樂非中和之紀乎夫樂為天地
之命則致樂以治心而精粗相凝之體實平心
宣化之資樂為中和之紀則致樂以治躬而情
文兼備之具為志和行成之本養德養身而有
punctuated:
論正樂之在人，其功大而不可離也。蓋人莫不有天地中和之理也，樂以命之、紀之，人情其得而免乎？樂記結言樂之切於人也，曰：人知凡樂之動不能外乎情，而不知人情之治實有資於樂。蓋甞於其聲容之感化者而觀其深矣。

今夫天地之賦於人者，有曰親、曰敬、曰順之道焉。樂聲之作而因以廣之，則德音之洋溢，有以感觸夫天性之眞；中聲之揄楊，有以啓發其秉彝之懿。以達其神，以興其德，而凡天地之所不及者，皆正樂以鼓舞之也。樂非天地之命乎？中和之具於人者，有曰莊、曰正、曰齊之儀焉。樂舞之舉而因以飭之，則干羽之習合，有以遠暴慢而攝威儀；綴兆之周旋，有以黜邪僻而全恭敬。以動血脉，以通精神，而凡中和之在於吾身者，皆正樂以綱維之也。樂非中和之紀乎？

夫樂為天地之命，則致樂以治心，而精粗相凝之體，實平心宣化之資；樂為中和之紀，則致樂以治躬，而情文兼備之具，為志和行成之本。養德養身而有
translation_en:
In considering proper music in human life, its efficacy is great, and one cannot be separated from it. Everyone possesses the principles of Heaven and Earth, centrality and harmony. Music gives these their mandate and regulates them: how, then, could human feelings dispense with it? The Record of Music (Yueji), concluding its discussion of music’s vital importance to humanity, says: People know that every stirring of music necessarily involves feeling, but they do not know that the ordering of human feelings actually depends upon music. By considering how its sounds and movements influence and transform people, one can perceive the depth of its effects.

Among the things Heaven and Earth endow people with are the ways of affection, reverence, and obedience. When musical sounds arise, these qualities are thereby enlarged. The overflowing sounds of virtue can touch the genuineness of our heavenly nature; the flourishing of balanced tones can awaken the excellence of our constant moral endowment. Music gives expression to the spirit and invigorates virtue. Wherever Heaven and Earth do not reach, proper music supplies encouragement and inspiration. Is music not, then, the mandate of Heaven and Earth? Centrality and harmony, as possessed by human beings, include the forms of bearing called solemnity, uprightness, and composure. When musical dances are performed, these are thereby put in order. Practising in concert with shields and plumes can keep violence and arrogance at a distance and bring dignified deportment under control; turning and moving through the prescribed dance positions can expel perversity and preserve complete respect and reverence. Music stirs the blood and vessels and enables the vital spirit to circulate. All the centrality and harmony within our persons are sustained and regulated by proper music. Is music not, then, the regulating thread of centrality and harmony?

Since music is the mandate of Heaven and Earth, one brings music to its fullest realization to order the heart. Its constitution, in which the subtle and the coarse coalesce, is truly a resource for calming the heart and spreading transforming influence. Since music is the regulating thread of centrality and harmony, one brings music to its fullest realization to order one’s person. Its resources, encompassing both feeling and patterned expression, form the foundation for harmonizing the will and perfecting conduct. It nurtures virtue and nurtures the person, and its presence …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
無關性術之理亂是日用之所必資焉者而可
以終身違哉成身成性而得失係志氣之安危
誠吾人之所必有事焉者而可以斯須去哉由
是而知正樂之感其化甚神而生民之道惟樂
爲大也先王立樂之方不其盡善盡美矣乎抑
君子於天地之命而見樂有盡性之功焉於中
和之紀而見樂有踐形之功焉踐形盡性樂之
於情甚切矣故曰禮樂之說管乎人情記者於
此可謂達樂之本矣作樂者夫苟不知天地中
===
和命紀之理而但求之文采節奏之間抑末矣
又安能感人動物之神速也哉故正樂之功於
是爲大
天子者與天地參故德配天地兼利萬物
林華
同考試官教諭曾批題本明白正大場中士
子頗能敷演成篇求其渾厚精粹者亦不多見錄
此以式
考試官教諭黃批文理嚴整可誦
punctuated:
無關性術之理亂，是日用之所必資焉者，而可以終身違哉？成身成性，而得失係志氣之安危，誠吾人之所必有事焉者，而可以斯須去哉？由是而知正樂之感，其化甚神，而生民之道惟樂爲大也。先王立樂之方，不其盡善盡美矣乎？抑君子於天地之命而見樂有盡性之功焉，於中和之紀而見樂有踐形之功焉。踐形盡性，樂之於情甚切矣。故曰：「禮樂之說，管乎人情。」記者於此，可謂達樂之本矣。作樂者夫苟不知天地中和命紀之理，而但求之文采節奏之間，抑末矣，又安能感人動物之神速也哉？故正樂之功於是爲大。
天子者，與天地參，故德配天地，兼利萬物。
林華
同考試官教諭曾批：題本明白正大，場中士子頗能敷演成篇，求其渾厚精粹者，亦不多見。錄此以式。
考試官教諭黃批：文理嚴整，可誦。
translation_en:
…its presence or absence bears upon order or disorder in one’s nature and conduct. It is indispensable to daily life: how could one turn away from it throughout one’s lifetime? In bringing one’s person and nature to fulfillment, attaining or losing it determines the security or peril of one’s resolve and vital energies. It is truly something to which we must apply ourselves: how could we dispense with it even for a moment? From this we know that the influence of correct music effects a wondrous transformation, and that in the Way governing human life nothing is greater than music. Was not the former kings’ method of establishing music perfectly good and perfectly beautiful? Moreover, in music as the mandate of Heaven and Earth, the gentleman sees its power to fulfill human nature; in music as the ordering principle of equilibrium and harmony, he sees its power to realize what one’s bodily form entails. In realizing one’s bodily form and fulfilling one’s nature, music bears most intimately upon human feelings. Thus it is said: “The teachings of ritual and music encompass human feelings.” In this, the author of the Record may be said to have comprehended music’s foundation. If those who compose music do not understand the principles by which it is the mandate of Heaven and Earth and the ordering principle of equilibrium and harmony, but seek it merely in ornament and rhythm, they attend only to its outermost details. How could they then achieve its wondrous swiftness in influencing people and moving other beings? Hence the great efficacy of correct music.
“The Son of Heaven forms a triad with Heaven and Earth; therefore his virtue matches Heaven and Earth, and he benefits all things alike.”
Lin Hua
Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor: “The topic is inherently clear, upright, and grand. The examination candidates have shown considerable ability to elaborate it into complete essays, but few works of depth, substance, refinement, and purity are to be found. This one is recorded as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The essay’s reasoning and organization are rigorous and orderly; it merits recitation.”

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正宋批順暢
聖君之合乎造化於其德業徵之矣夫德配天
地德之盛也兼利萬物業之大也天子如此其
參於天地也宜哉經解記孔子之言也嘗謂天
地之大也夫人難乎其參矣獨不觀聖人在天
子之位乎是故乾稱乎父坤稱乎母而大君則
宗子於其間天位乎上地位乎下而聖人則成
位於其中崇效卑法而神化以備仰觀俯察而
人極以立參乎天地者其惟天子也已矣蓋甞
===
自其盛德大業而觀之今夫大哉至哉天地之
爲德固極盛而無以加矣惟天子者以一心涵
性命之原而剛健中正之懿與之相似而不違
以一身建中和之極而含弘光大之體與之克
肖而無忝其發之也高大光明而高明之德與
天配也其積之也廣博深厚而博厚之德與地
配也上下同流而渾合無間日新之盛德謂不
克配於天地矣乎大生廣生萬物之並育固至
賾而不可限矣惟天子者裁成天地之道而一
punctuated:
考試官學正宋批：順暢。

聖君之合乎造化，於其德業徵之矣。夫德配天地，德之盛也；兼利萬物，業之大也。天子如此，其參於天地也宜哉！《經解》記孔子之言也，嘗謂天地之大也，夫人難乎其參矣。獨不觀聖人在天子之位乎？是故乾稱乎父，坤稱乎母，而大君則宗子於其間；天位乎上，地位乎下，而聖人則成位於其中。崇效卑法，而神化以備；仰觀俯察，而人極以立。參乎天地者，其惟天子也已矣！蓋甞自其盛德大業而觀之。今夫大哉至哉，天地之爲德，固極盛而無以加矣。惟天子者，以一心涵性命之原，而剛健中正之懿，與之相似而不違；以一身建中和之極，而含弘光大之體，與之克肖而無忝。其發之也，高大光明，而高明之德與天配也；其積之也，廣博深厚，而博厚之德與地配也。上下同流，而渾合無間，日新之盛德，謂不克配於天地矣乎？大生廣生，萬物之並育，固至賾而不可限矣。惟天子者，裁成天地之道，而一
translation_en:
Examiner Song, an Instructor, comments: “Smooth and fluent.”

The sage ruler’s accord with the workings of creation is demonstrated in his virtue and achievements. For virtue to match Heaven and Earth is virtue at its fullest; to benefit all things together is achievement at its greatest. With the Son of Heaven being such, how fitting that he should stand alongside Heaven and Earth! “Explanation of the Classics” records Confucius’s words. It has been said that Heaven and Earth are so great that people find it difficult to stand alongside them. Yet have we not observed the sage occupying the position of Son of Heaven? Thus Qian is called father, and Kun is called mother, while the great ruler is the heir to the ancestral line between them. Heaven takes its place above, Earth below, and the sage establishes his place between them. He emulates the lofty and takes the lowly as his model, thereby bringing spiritual transformation to completion; he looks upward and examines what is below, thereby establishing the supreme standard for humanity. Surely it is the Son of Heaven alone who stands alongside Heaven and Earth!

Let us consider this through his abundant virtue and great achievements. How great, how consummate! The virtue of Heaven and Earth is indeed supremely abundant, with nothing that could be added to it. The Son of Heaven alone embraces within his single heart the source of nature and destiny: his excellence in strength, vigor, centrality, and correctness resembles theirs without departing from them. In his own person he establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony: his capacious, generous, luminous, and great constitution faithfully resembles theirs without dishonoring them. When his virtue issues forth, it is lofty, great, luminous, and bright; thus his lofty and luminous virtue matches Heaven. As it accumulates, it becomes broad, extensive, deep, and substantial; thus his broad and substantial virtue matches Earth.
