Flowing together with what is above and below, it forms a seamless whole with them. Can one say that this abundant virtue, daily renewed, fails to match Heaven and Earth?

Through their great power of generation and their extensive nurture, Heaven and Earth foster all things together: this is indeed supremely intricate and cannot be bounded. The Son of Heaven alone regulates and brings to completion the Way of Heaven and Earth, and with a single …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
體之公能使天下無一物不得其所輔相天地
之宜而茂對之心能使天下無一物不被其澤
盡已之性而盡人之性則自夫物之同類者而
利之也盡人之性而盡物之性則自夫物之異
類者而利之也過化存神而曲成不遺富有之
大業謂不兼利夫萬物矣乎夫曰德配天地則
天子與天地同體曰兼利萬物則天子與天地
同用體用備而法象昭信乎可以與天地參矣
抑先儒有云仁者以天地萬物為一體是故天
===
子之參於天地非有所增益於性分之外也夫
亦全乎其所謂一體者而已矣然天地之大也
人猶有所憾惟天子建中和之極而後覆載生
成之偏者得以彌綸而範圍之則雖謂天子之
有功於天地可也故曰天者羣物之祖地者羣
物之母聖人者羣物之命
第貳場
論
萬世文字之祖
punctuated:
體之公，能使天下無一物不得其所；輔相天地之宜，而茂對之心，能使天下無一物不被其澤。盡已之性而盡人之性，則自夫物之同類者而利之也；盡人之性而盡物之性，則自夫物之異類者而利之也。過化存神，而曲成不遺，富有之大業，謂不兼利夫萬物矣乎？夫曰德配天地，則天子與天地同體；曰兼利萬物，則天子與天地同用。體用備而法象昭，信乎可以與天地參矣！抑先儒有云：「仁者以天地萬物為一體。」是故天子之參於天地，非有所增益於性分之外也，夫亦全乎其所謂一體者而已矣。然天地之大也，人猶有所憾。惟天子建中和之極，而後覆載生成之偏者，得以彌綸而範圍之，則雖謂天子之有功於天地可也。故曰：「天者羣物之祖，地者羣物之母，聖人者羣物之命。」

第貳場

論

萬世文字之祖
translation_en:
…the impartiality of treating all as one body can ensure that nothing under Heaven fails to find its proper place. By assisting Heaven and Earth in what is fitting, his resolve to respond fully to them can ensure that nothing under Heaven fails to receive his beneficence. By fully realizing his own nature and then the nature of others, he benefits beings of his own kind; by fully realizing the nature of others and then the nature of things, he benefits beings of other kinds. Wherever he passes, transformation follows; wherever he abides, his influence is numinous. He brings each thing to fulfillment according to its particular circumstances, leaving none out. Could his great undertaking, embracing all in its abundance, be said not to benefit the myriad things alike? To say that his virtue matches Heaven and Earth means that the Son of Heaven shares their substance; to say that he benefits the myriad things alike means that he shares their functioning. With substance and functioning complete, and their exemplary patterns manifest, he can indeed stand as a third alongside Heaven and Earth!

Moreover, an earlier Confucian said: “The benevolent person regards Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as one body.” Thus, when the Son of Heaven stands as a third alongside Heaven and Earth, he adds nothing beyond what is allotted to his nature. He merely brings to completeness what is called this unity of body. Yet, vast as Heaven and Earth are, people still find grounds for regret. Only when the Son of Heaven establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony can he comprehensively order and regulate the partialities in their sheltering, supporting, generating, and bringing things to completion. It is therefore permissible even to say that the Son of Heaven renders service to Heaven and Earth. Hence the saying: “Heaven is the ancestor of all things; Earth is the mother of all things; the sage is the life of all things.”

Second Session

Discourse

The Progenitor of Writing for All Ages

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
王弘誨
同考試官教諭蕭批論塲不知易者每至空
疎固陋而知者又復散漫支離惟此篇融會先天
之圖深於理數而復文勢沛然若江河之决而莫
之禦是宜錄出
同考試官教諭曾批萬世文字之祖人多知
出陳氏而不知爲朱子之論司馬遷此作考據精
詳而步驟縱逸抑揚開闔俱有程度眞佳作也可
以式矣
===
考試官教諭黃批詞宏氣昌大家氣象
考試官學正宋批雄健之作
道之大原出於天也聖人承天心以闡道而人
文於是乎啓矣作易非聖人意也天也太極動
而陽生焉靜而陰生焉動靜互爲其根而循環
無窮焉此天之道也天不能自秘其道而於圖
乎見之聖人者發天地之蘊通神明之德而援
此以立象而先天之圖畫焉蓋先天地而知天
地之終後天地而知天地之始惟以闡道也而
punctuated:
王弘誨

同考試官教諭蕭批：論塲不知易者，每至空疎固陋；而知者，又復散漫支離。惟此篇融會先天之圖，深於理數，而復文勢沛然，若江河之决而莫之禦，是宜錄出。

同考試官教諭曾批：萬世文字之祖，人多知出陳氏，而不知爲朱子之論司馬遷。此作考據精詳，而步驟縱逸，抑揚開闔俱有程度，眞佳作也，可以式矣。

考試官教諭黃批：詞宏氣昌，大家氣象。

考試官學正宋批：雄健之作。

道之大原出於天也。聖人承天心以闡道，而人文於是乎啓矣。作易，非聖人意也，天也。太極動而陽生焉，靜而陰生焉，動靜互爲其根，而循環無窮焉，此天之道也。天不能自秘其道，而於圖乎見之。聖人者，發天地之蘊，通神明之德，而援此以立象，而先天之圖畫焉。蓋先天地而知天地之終，後天地而知天地之始，惟以闡道也，而
translation_en:
Wang Honghui 王弘誨

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: In the discourse examination, those who do not understand the Book of Changes repeatedly lapse into emptiness, superficiality, and narrow ignorance; those who do understand it, however, become diffuse and disjointed. This essay alone achieves an integrated understanding of the Diagram of the Prior Heaven, penetrating deeply into principle and number. Moreover, its prose flows abundantly, like the Yangzi and Yellow Rivers bursting forth with an irresistible force. It deserves to be selected for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor: Many know that the phrase “the progenitor of writing for all ages” comes from Master Chen, but do not know that it was Master Zhu’s assessment of Sima Qian. This composition is precise and thorough in its examination of sources, yet free and untrammeled in its progression. Its rises and falls, expansions and contractions, all observe due measure. Truly an excellent work: it may serve as a model.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: Grand diction and flourishing vigor—the bearing of a great master.

Comment by Examiner Song, School Instructor: A powerful and vigorous composition.

The great source of the Way issues from Heaven. The sage receives Heaven’s intent and elucidates the Way; human culture thus begins. The making of the Book of Changes proceeded not from the sage’s intention, but from Heaven. When the Supreme Ultimate moves, yang is generated; when it rests, yin is generated. Movement and stillness each serve as the other’s root, cycling without end. This is the Way of Heaven. Heaven cannot keep its Way concealed, and so manifests it in a diagram. The sage brings forth what is hidden within Heaven and Earth and comprehends the potency of the spirits. Drawing upon this, he establishes the images, and thus the Diagram of the Prior Heaven is delineated. Indeed, preceding Heaven and Earth, he knows their end; following Heaven and Earth, he knows their beginning. His purpose is solely to elucidate the Way, and…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
非以為文也而天下後世之文卒不能外焉天
地之紀典則之會萬事萬化之原胥於是乎出
是豈聖人有所强於天下後世哉聖人無所强
於天下後世而道之所在天下後世不得不從
天下後世未始求文於聖人而文之所在天下
後世不得不祖非祖其文也祖其道也非祖聖
人之道祖天之道也大矣哉先天之易也茲其
為萬世文字之祖乎今夫鴻濛之世顓侗沕穆
雖有畫前之易與天下相忘於無言之天聖人
===
之所樂也逮伏羲氏作而先天之圖畫焉聖人
豈故為是贅哉風氣日開人文漸著造化之精
天亦不能自秘而河圖於是乎出焉一六居下
二七居上三八居左四九居右五十居中此自
然之數也天之文亦天之道也然是圖也夫人
而皆見之不夫人而皆知之伏羲氏之王天下
也首出庶物因天開人於是神道設教而卦畫
焉虛五與十而太極之體立矣積二十之奇合
二十之偶以一二三四合七八九六而儀象定
punctuated: 非以為文也，而天下後世之文卒不能外焉。天地之紀，典則之會，萬事萬化之原，胥於是乎出。是豈聖人有所强於天下後世哉？聖人無所强於天下後世，而道之所在，天下後世不得不從；天下後世未始求文於聖人，而文之所在，天下後世不得不祖。非祖其文也，祖其道也；非祖聖人之道，祖天之道也。大矣哉，先天之易也！茲其為萬世文字之祖乎！今夫鴻濛之世，顓侗沕穆，雖有畫前之易，與天下相忘於無言之天，聖人之所樂也。逮伏羲氏作，而先天之圖畫焉，聖人豈故為是贅哉？風氣日開，人文漸著，造化之精，天亦不能自秘，而河圖於是乎出焉。一六居下，二七居上，三八居左，四九居右，五十居中，此自然之數也。天之文，亦天之道也。然是圖也，夫人而皆見之，不夫人而皆知之。伏羲氏之王天下也，首出庶物，因天開人，於是神道設教而卦畫焉。虛五與十，而太極之體立矣；積二十之奇，合二十之偶，以一二三四合七八九六，而儀象定
translation_en:
…not to create literary forms; yet the writings of all subsequent generations ultimately could not go beyond them. The ordering principles of Heaven and Earth, the convergence of canonical norms, and the source of all affairs and transformations all issue from this. Could the sage have imposed anything upon the world and later generations? The sage imposed nothing upon them, yet wherever the Way resides, the world and later generations cannot but follow. They never initially sought literary forms from the sage, yet wherever those forms reside, they cannot but take them as their model. It is not his literary forms that they take as their model, but his Way; nor is it the sage’s Way, but the Way of Heaven. Great indeed is the Prior Heaven Changes! Is this not the progenitor of writing for all ages?
Now, in the age of primordial obscurity, when all was simple, undifferentiated, and mysterious, although the Changes already existed before the drawing of the trigrams, the sage and the world dwelt in mutual oblivion within wordless Heaven: this was what the sage delighted in. When Fuxi arose and the Prior Heaven diagram was drawn, did the sage deliberately introduce something superfluous? As the prevailing influences unfolded day by day and human cultural patterns gradually became manifest, even Heaven could no longer keep the essence of creative transformation concealed, and thus the River Chart appeared. One and six occupy the bottom; two and seven, the top; three and eight, the left; four and nine, the right; and five and ten, the center. These are the numbers of the natural order. Heaven’s patterned forms are also Heaven’s Way. Yet although everyone could see this chart, not everyone could understand it.
When Fuxi ruled all under Heaven, he stood foremost among all beings and, following Heaven, enlightened humanity. Thus he established instruction through the numinous Way, and the trigrams were drawn. By leaving five and ten vacant, the substance of the Supreme Ultimate was established. By accumulating the odd numbers totaling twenty and combining the even numbers totaling twenty, and by pairing one, two, three, and four with seven, eight, nine, and six, the two modes and four images were determined…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
矣析四方之合補四隅之空而八卦位矣是豈
聖人勉强矯拂於其間哉一因其數之自然而
不可易道之本然而不可容强者耳自今觀之
圖之從中起也易之本太極也是卽萬事萬化
生於心也乾健坤順也艮止震動也離麗而兌
說也坎陷而巽入也卽吾心性情之德也萬之
原於一也奇者陽之文也偶者陰之文也奇奇
偶偶者象之文也三畫皆奇乾之文也三畫皆
偶坤之文也以至奇偶之或上或下或多或寡
===
則震巽坎離艮兌之文也因而重之則自復至
乾自姤至坤六十四卦之文也縱横錯綜莫不
各有其理對待流行莫不各有其義而天下之
文昭矣蓋自本而榦自榦而枝若有所迫而自
不能已何莫而非自然之數自然之道耶由是
聖人發揮於辭而筆之經無不可者何止于圖
而靳於言耶噫聖人之精因畫以示使天下後
世有因畫而求吾心焉則文固燦然而具陳道
固渾然而具在如以畫而已矣則盈天地間皆
punctuated: 矣。析四方之合，補四隅之空，而八卦位矣。是豈聖人勉强矯拂於其間哉？一因其數之自然而不可易，道之本然而不可容强者耳。自今觀之，圖之從中起也，易之本太極也，是卽萬事萬化生於心也。乾健坤順也，艮止震動也，離麗而兌說也，坎陷而巽入也，卽吾心性情之德也。萬之原於一也，奇者陽之文也，偶者陰之文也，奇奇偶偶者象之文也。三畫皆奇，乾之文也；三畫皆偶，坤之文也。以至奇偶之或上或下，或多或寡，則震巽坎離艮兌之文也。因而重之，則自復至乾，自姤至坤，六十四卦之文也。縱横錯綜，莫不各有其理；對待流行，莫不各有其義，而天下之文昭矣。蓋自本而榦，自榦而枝，若有所迫而自不能已，何莫而非自然之數、自然之道耶？由是聖人發揮於辭而筆之經，無不可者，何止于圖而靳於言耶？噫！聖人之精，因畫以示，使天下後世有因畫而求吾心焉，則文固燦然而具陳，道固渾然而具在。如以畫而已矣，則盈天地間皆
translation_en: …are established. By separating the combined numbers of the four directions and filling the empty spaces at the four corners, the eight trigrams take their positions. Could this be a matter of the sage forcibly intervening and bending things against their nature? He simply follows the natural and unalterable character of these numbers, and the inherent character of the Way, which admits no coercion. Viewed from the present, the Diagram’s arising from its center and the Changes’ being rooted in the Supreme Ultimate are precisely the same as the myriad affairs and transformations arising from the mind. Qian is vigorous and Kun compliant; Gen is still and Zhen moving; Li is clinging and Dui joyous; Kan is sinking and Xun entering. These are precisely the powers of our minds’ nature and feelings. The myriad have their source in the one: odd numbers are the pattern of yang, even numbers the pattern of yin, and combinations of odd and even are the patterns of the images. Three lines all odd constitute the pattern of Qian; three lines all even constitute the pattern of Kun. As for odd and even lines appearing above or below, in greater or smaller numbers, these constitute the patterns of Zhen, Xun, Kan, Li, Gen, and Dui. Building upon these and doubling them yields the patterns of the sixty-four hexagrams, from Fu to Qian and from Gou to Kun. In their vertical and horizontal arrangements, interweavings and combinations, each has its own principle; in their oppositions and ongoing transformations, each has its own meaning. Thus the patterns of all under Heaven become manifest. From root to trunk, and from trunk to branches, they seem impelled by something, unable to stop of themselves. What among them is not the natural working of numbers and the natural Way? On this basis, there is nothing inappropriate in the sage’s expounding these in statements and committing them to writing in the classic. Why should he stop at the Diagram and begrudge words? Ah! The sage’s subtle understanding is revealed through the lines, so that people throughout the world and in later ages may use the lines to seek within their own minds. Then the patterns are indeed brilliantly and fully displayed, and the Way is indeed present in its integrated entirety. If one regards them merely as lines, then everything filling the space between Heaven and Earth…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
神化之糟粕耳此則聖人意也然雖無文也而
天下之至文存焉無言也而天下之至言在焉
聖人非有求於天下萬世而其文其道自有以
通乎天下萬世之人心天下萬世非有期於聖
人而不能不取足於聖人之文之道是故黃帝
堯舜得之而爲垂衣之治湯武得之而爲順應
之舉文王箕子得之而爲艱貞之行莫非此道
也莫非此文之祖也夏后氏之連山商人之歸
藏文王之彖辭周公之爻辭孔子之十翼莫非
===
此道也莫非此文之祖也以動者尚其變以言
者尚其辭以制器者尚其象以卜筮者尚其占
莫非此道也莫非此文之祖也溫柔敦厚之詩
疏通知遠之書恭敬退讓之禮廣博易良之樂
屬辭此事之春秋莫非此道也莫非此文之祖
也以至萬事萬化稼穡耒耜舟車宮室書契臼
杵弧矢市易以開天下之物以成天下之務何
莫而非此道何莫而非此文之祖耶是非聖人
之意之也先天無言之秘實有以闡三才之理
punctuated: 神化之糟粕耳，此則聖人意也。然雖無文也，而天下之至文存焉；無言也，而天下之至言在焉。聖人非有求於天下萬世，而其文其道自有以通乎天下萬世之人心；天下萬世非有期於聖人，而不能不取足於聖人之文之道。是故黃帝、堯、舜得之，而爲垂衣之治；湯、武得之，而爲順應之舉；文王、箕子得之，而爲艱貞之行。莫非此道也，莫非此文之祖也。夏后氏之《連山》、商人之《歸藏》、文王之彖辭、周公之爻辭、孔子之十翼，莫非此道也，莫非此文之祖也。以動者尚其變，以言者尚其辭，以制器者尚其象，以卜筮者尚其占，莫非此道也，莫非此文之祖也。溫柔敦厚之《詩》，疏通知遠之《書》，恭敬退讓之《禮》，廣博易良之《樂》，屬辭此事之《春秋》，莫非此道也，莫非此文之祖也。以至萬事萬化，稼穡、耒耜、舟車、宮室、書契、臼杵、弧矢、市易，以開天下之物，以成天下之務，何莫而非此道？何莫而非此文之祖耶？是非聖人之意之也？先天無言之秘，實有以闡三才之理
translation_en: …merely the dregs of numinous transformation. This, then, is the sage’s intention. Yet although there is no writing, the supreme pattern of all under Heaven is preserved therein; although there are no words, the supreme utterance of all under Heaven is present therein. The sage seeks nothing from the world through all ages, yet his writing and his Way can of themselves communicate with the hearts of people throughout the world and across all ages. The people of the world through all ages expect nothing of the sage, yet they cannot but find all they need in his writing and his Way. Thus Huangdi, Yao, and Shun attained it and governed with their robes hanging down, without exertion; Tang and Wu attained it and undertook actions that accorded with Heaven and responded to the people; King Wen and Jizi attained it and remained steadfast amid hardship. All embody this Way; all are sources of this cultural pattern. The Xia rulers’ Linked Mountains (Lianshan), the Shang people’s Return to the Hidden (Guicang), King Wen’s judgments on the hexagrams, the Duke of Zhou’s statements on the individual lines, and Confucius’s Ten Wings all embody this Way; all are sources of this cultural pattern. Those who act esteem its changes; those who speak esteem its statements; those who fashion implements esteem its images; those who divine by turtle shell or milfoil esteem its prognostications. All embody this Way; all are sources of this cultural pattern. The Poetry, fostering gentleness, sincerity, and generosity; the Documents, fostering breadth of understanding and knowledge of the distant past; the Rites, fostering reverence and deference; the Music, fostering breadth, ease, and goodness; and the Spring and Autumn Annals, linking words and events [?]—all embody this Way; all are sources of this cultural pattern. Extending even to the myriad affairs and transformations—to sowing and reaping, ploughs and ploughshares, boats and carts, palaces and dwellings, writing and tallies, mortars and pestles, bows and arrows, and trade in markets—these develop the things of the world and accomplish its tasks. Which does not embody this Way? Which is not a source of this cultural pattern? Is this not the sage’s intention [?]? The wordless mystery of the Prior Heaven truly serves to elucidate the principles of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
則立極垂憲一無言之圖而固有以冒天下之
道矣由是千百世之下有聖人出焉非祖其文
祖其道非祖聖人之道天不變則道亦不變自
有以範圍而不過焉耳易不云乎聖人立象以
盡意知象之可以盡意則知圖之可以盡文矣
又云天生神物聖人則之則圖之原於天而不
可易不亦彰彰著明矣哉夫先天之圖為萬世
文字之祖史遷紀五帝而顧獨遺焉陋矣宜子
朱子之所為興慨也若之何後之言易者紛紛
===
也有五行有卦氣有太玄有洞極有潛虛其不
知所祖而昧焉者乎有圖說有通書有易傳有
啓蒙有皇極經世其知所祖而明焉者乎夫先
天之學多言以晦之固易之障也而得諸儒以
為之羽翼而大明又易之幸也哉
同前
何天衢
同考試官教諭童批〔卦畫所以為文字之祖處模寫殆盡非潛心易學者未易到此佳士佳士〕
punctuated:
則立極垂憲，一無言之圖，而固有以冒天下之道矣。由是千百世之下，有聖人出焉，非祖其文，祖其道；非祖聖人之道，天不變則道亦不變，自有以範圍而不過焉耳。《易》不云乎：「聖人立象以盡意。」知象之可以盡意，則知圖之可以盡文矣。又云：「天生神物，聖人則之。」則圖之原於天而不可易，不亦彰彰著明矣哉！夫先天之圖為萬世文字之祖，史遷紀五帝，而顧獨遺焉，陋矣！宜子朱子之所為興慨也。若之何後之言《易》者紛紛也？有五行，有卦氣，有《太玄》，有《洞極》，有《潛虛》，其不知所祖而昧焉者乎？有《圖說》，有《通書》，有《易傳》，有《啓蒙》，有《皇極經世》，其知所祖而明焉者乎？夫先天之學，多言以晦之，固《易》之障也；而得諸儒以為之羽翼而大明，又《易》之幸也哉！

同前。
何天衢。
同考試官教諭童批〔卦畫所以為文字之祖處，模寫殆盡，非潛心易學者未易到此。佳士！佳士！〕
translation_en:
…then it establishes the supreme standard and transmits enduring rules: a single wordless diagram nevertheless encompasses the Way of all under Heaven. Thus, should a sage arise hundreds or thousands of generations later, he would take as his source not its written forms but its Way. Nor would he take merely the sages’ Way as his source: so long as Heaven does not change, the Way likewise does not change, and of itself provides an encompassing framework whose bounds are not overstepped. Does not the Book of Changes say, “The sages established images to express their meaning fully”? Knowing that images can fully express meaning, we know that the diagram can fully encompass written expression. It also says, “Heaven produces numinous things, and the sages take them as models.” Is it not therefore abundantly clear that the diagram originates in Heaven and cannot be altered? The Before-Heaven Diagram is the ancestor of written characters for all ages; yet Sima Qian, in recording the Five Emperors, omitted this alone. How narrow his understanding! No wonder our Master Zhu sighed over this. Why, then, have later interpreters of the Changes produced such a welter of views? There are the theories of the Five Phases and hexagram qi, the Supreme Mystery (Taixuan), Penetrating the Ultimate (Dongji), and Latent Emptiness (Qianxu): are these instances of obscurity arising from failure to recognize their source? There are the Explanation of the Diagram (Tushuo), the Comprehensive Writings (Tongshu), the Commentary on the Changes (Yizhuan), the Introduction to Learning (Qimeng), and the Supreme Principles Governing the World (Huangji jingshi): are these instances of clarity arising from recognition of their source? To obscure the learning of Before Heaven with excessive words certainly obstructs the Changes; yet to have these scholars lend it their support and bring it fully to light is also the good fortune of the Changes!

Same as above.
He Tianqu.
Comment by Associate Examiner Tong, Instructor: 〔The way in which the hexagram lines constitute the ancestor of written characters is depicted almost exhaustively. Someone who had not devoted himself deeply to studying the Changes could hardly attain this level. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!〕

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭孫批詞格高古氣象宏大開
闔變化意趣不窮亦文字之有數者錄之
考試官教諭黃批有源委有波瀾
考試官學正宋批氣槩闊大
天有顯道也聖人作易以開斯道之原其達諸
天乎夫天者道之原也天不言而以道示人夫
人囿于斯道日用而不知也不能不賴聖人以
開其原聖人者天之所命首出庶物神靈特異
先天地而知天地之終後天地而知天地之始
===
承天之意而作易以開斯道之原使天下後世
緣其原而得其所以達諸天者斯文賴以著明
謂非聖人立道之極而為吾道之祖不可也孔
子傳易而首包犧曰包犧氏始作作者創之謂
也後有作者述之而已知乎此則伏羲作易而
為萬世文字之祖者可得而論矣爰自混沌未
鑿鴻濛未闢一元之氣渾淪而已矣固無所謂
道也迨夫天開於子而為羣物之祖地闢於丑
而為羣物之母人生於寅而聖人成位乎中故
punctuated:
同考試官教諭孫批：詞格高古，氣象宏大，開闔變化，意趣不窮，亦文字之有數者，錄之。
考試官教諭黃批：有源委，有波瀾。
考試官學正宋批：氣槩闊大。
天有顯道也，聖人作易以開斯道之原，其達諸天乎？夫天者，道之原也。天不言，而以道示人。夫人囿于斯道，日用而不知也，不能不賴聖人以開其原。聖人者，天之所命，首出庶物，神靈特異，先天地而知天地之終，後天地而知天地之始。承天之意而作易，以開斯道之原，使天下後世緣其原而得其所以達諸天者，斯文賴以著明。謂非聖人立道之極而為吾道之祖，不可也。孔子傳易而首包犧，曰：「包犧氏始作。」作者，創之謂也；後有作者，述之而已。知乎此，則伏羲作易而為萬世文字之祖者，可得而論矣。爰自混沌未鑿，鴻濛未闢，一元之氣渾淪而已矣，固無所謂道也。迨夫天開於子而為羣物之祖，地闢於丑而為羣物之母，人生於寅而聖人成位乎中，故
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “The diction and style are lofty and antique; the overall conception is grand. Its unfolding, gathering, and transformations offer inexhaustible interest. This, too, ranks among distinguished compositions. Include it.”
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “It has a source and a course, and surging waves.”
Examiner Song, School Instructor, comments: “Its spirit is expansive and grand.”
Heaven has a manifest Way. The sage made the Changes to disclose the source of this Way: was this how he attained communion with Heaven? Heaven is the source of the Way. Heaven does not speak, but reveals the Way to humanity. People dwell within this Way and use it daily without knowing it; they cannot but rely on the sage to disclose its source. The sage is commissioned by Heaven, standing foremost among all beings, endowed with extraordinary spiritual intelligence. Preceding Heaven and Earth, he knows their end; following Heaven and Earth, he knows their beginning. He received Heaven’s intent and made the Changes to disclose the source of this Way, enabling all under Heaven and later generations to trace its source and discover the means of attaining communion with Heaven. Through this, our cultural tradition was made manifest. One cannot deny that the sage established the highest standard of the Way and became the progenitor of our Way. In transmitting the Changes, Confucius placed Baoxi first, saying: “Baoxi first created it.” To create means to originate something; those who created afterward merely transmitted it. Once this is understood, we can discuss how Fuxi, by making the Changes, became the progenitor of writing for all ages. At the outset, before primordial chaos had been opened and the vast undifferentiated expanse had been divided, there was only the primal vital force, wholly commingled. There was as yet nothing that could be called the Way. Then Heaven opened in the zi epoch and became the progenitor of all things; Earth opened in the chou epoch and became the mother of all things; humanity arose in the yin epoch, and the sage took his place between them. Thus …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖人者天地之宗子民物之祖也三皇之時風
氣未開太朴未琢民生其間與草木鹿豕何異
巢窟可居未有宮室之文羽毛可蔽未有冠裳
之文男女無別未有嫁娶之文結繩而治未有
書契之文斯時也道固未彰也及夫包犧氏作
以木德王天下天地之盛德在木帝出乎震包
犧氏應運而興時則於氣為泰於令為春故曰
其帝太昊蓋又天地一大開闢也是故華渚流
虹明象日月而聖德徵矣天應以鳥獸文章地
===
應以河圖洛書而貞符協矣伏羲氏亦烏能如
渾敦之時與斯世相忘於沕穆之天哉夫龍馬
負圖而出也固天所以示文明之精而洩斯道
之原也伏羲仰觀俯察遠求近取則其圖稽其
數由太極而兩儀由兩儀而四象由四象而八
卦剛柔以立其本動靜以互其根是故其體微
而彰其事閎而肆其理約而精聖人者由此而
發揮於詞摸寫於經可也包犧氏何靳於言而
不與天下萬世立敎哉噫聖人非不言也聖人
punctuated:
聖人者，天地之宗子，民物之祖也。三皇之時，風氣未開，太朴未琢，民生其間，與草木鹿豕何異？巢窟可居，未有宮室之文；羽毛可蔽，未有冠裳之文；男女無別，未有嫁娶之文；結繩而治，未有書契之文。斯時也，道固未彰也。及夫包犧氏作，以木德王天下，天地之盛德在木，帝出乎震，包犧氏應運而興。時則於氣為泰，於令為春，故曰其帝太昊，蓋又天地一大開闢也。是故華渚流虹，明象日月，而聖德徵矣；天應以鳥獸文章，地應以河圖洛書，而貞符協矣。伏羲氏亦烏能如渾敦之時，與斯世相忘於沕穆之天哉？

夫龍馬負圖而出也，固天所以示文明之精而洩斯道之原也。伏羲仰觀俯察，遠求近取，則其圖，稽其數，由太極而兩儀，由兩儀而四象，由四象而八卦，剛柔以立其本，動靜以互其根。是故其體微而彰，其事閎而肆，其理約而精。聖人者，由此而發揮於詞，摸寫於經，可也。包犧氏何靳於言，而不與天下萬世立敎哉？噫！聖人非不言也，聖人
translation_en:
…the sage is the principal heir of Heaven and Earth and the progenitor of the people and all creatures. In the time of the Three Sovereigns, civilizing influences had not yet unfolded, and primordial simplicity remained uncarved. How did the people living then differ from plants and trees, deer and swine? Nests and caves provided dwellings, but there were as yet no cultural refinements of palaces and houses; feathers and fur provided covering, but there were no cultural refinements of caps and robes. Men and women were undifferentiated, and there were no marriage rites; affairs were managed with knotted cords, and there was no written documentation. At that time, the Way had certainly not yet become manifest. Then Baoxi arose and ruled all under Heaven through the potency of Wood. The flourishing potency of Heaven and Earth resides in Wood, and the Lord comes forth in Zhen, the trigram of Thunder. Baoxi arose in response to the cosmic cycle. In terms of vital energy, his time was one of harmonious conjunction; in terms of the seasons, it was spring. Thus it is said, “Its sovereign is Taihao.” This was indeed another great opening of Heaven and Earth. Hence a rainbow streamed at Huazhu, with luminous signs of sun and moon [?], attesting to his sagely virtue. Heaven responded with the patterned markings of birds and beasts, and Earth responded with the River Chart and the Luo Writing: the auspicious tokens were in accord. How, then, could Fuxi, as in the age of primordial chaos, remain in mutual oblivion with the world beneath the deep and silent heavens?

The dragon-horse’s emergence bearing the Chart was surely Heaven’s means of revealing the essence of luminous culture and disclosing the source of this Way. Fuxi looked upward and observed, looked downward and examined, sought in distant things and drew upon things close at hand. He took the Chart as his model and investigated its numbers: from the Supreme Ultimate came the Two Modes; from the Two Modes, the Four Images; and from the Four Images, the Eight Trigrams. The firm and yielding established their foundation; movement and stillness served as each other’s root. Thus its substance was subtle yet manifest, its operations vast and far-reaching, and its principles concise and refined. The sage could have proceeded from this to expound it in words and portray it in a classic. Why did Baoxi begrudge words and fail to establish teachings for all under Heaven and the myriad generations to come? Ah! It was not that the sage did not speak. The sage…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之意以爲吾示以畫使天下後世緣畫而求諸
心焉則得意忘象得象忘言盈天地間糟粕煨
燼固無非敎也徒以畫而已則圖書不過象數
之迹雖言焉亦贅疣矣噫此聖人待天下意也
自今觀之一奇一偶者儀之文也奇偶各二者
象之文也奇偶之純乾坤之文也奇偶之雜則
震巽坎離艮兌之文也因而重之則六十四卦
之文昭矣斯不亦微而彰乎日月星辰水火土
石剛柔之體用也寒暑晝夜風雨露雷陰陽之
===
消息也性情形體飛走草木象形之變動也斯
不亦閎而肆乎虛五與十而爲太極所以具吾
心之體也健順動止麗說陷入所以達性情之
用也神明之德通焉性命之理寓焉斯不亦約
而精乎噫此圖之所以至妙至妙也無文也而
實萬世之至文無言也而實萬世之至言道不
在玆乎後有作者堯舜紹之而作十六字湯武
承之而作誓誥文王衍之而作卦辭周公係爻
孔子著傳蓋統於六經而文字始盛矣至於孟
punctuated:
之意以爲：吾示以畫，使天下後世緣畫而求諸心焉，則得意忘象，得象忘言，盈天地間糟粕煨燼，固無非敎也。徒以畫而已，則圖書不過象數之迹，雖言焉，亦贅疣矣。噫！此聖人待天下意也。
自今觀之，一奇一偶者，儀之文也；奇偶各二者，象之文也；奇偶之純，乾坤之文也；奇偶之雜，則震巽坎離艮兌之文也。因而重之，則六十四卦之文昭矣。斯不亦微而彰乎？日月星辰，水火土石，剛柔之體用也；寒暑晝夜，風雨露雷，陰陽之消息也；性情形體，飛走草木，象形之變動也。斯不亦閎而肆乎？虛五與十而爲太極，所以具吾心之體也；健順動止，麗說陷入，所以達性情之用也。神明之德通焉，性命之理寓焉。斯不亦約而精乎？噫！此圖之所以至妙至妙也。無文也，而實萬世之至文；無言也，而實萬世之至言。道不在玆乎？
後有作者，堯舜紹之而作十六字，湯武承之而作誓誥，文王衍之而作卦辭，周公係爻，孔子著傳，蓋統於六經而文字始盛矣。至於孟
translation_en:
…the sage’s intention was this: “I show them the lines, so that all under Heaven and later generations may follow these lines and seek within their own minds. Then, apprehending the meaning, they may forget the images; apprehending the images, they may forget the words. Even the dregs and ashes that fill Heaven and Earth are assuredly all sources of instruction. If they attend merely to the lines, however, the River Chart and the Luo Writing amount to no more than traces of images and numbers; even words added to them would be superfluous growths.” Ah! Such was what the sage expected of all under Heaven.
Viewed from the present, one odd and one even line constitute the patterns of the Two Modes; combinations of two odd or even lines constitute the patterns of the Four Images. Pure odd or pure even lines constitute the patterns of Qian and Kun; mixtures of odd and even constitute the patterns of Zhen, Xun, Kan, Li, Gen, and Dui. By doubling these, the patterns of the sixty-four hexagrams become manifest. Is this not subtle yet evident? The sun, moon, and stars, water, fire, earth, and stone are the substance and functioning of the firm and yielding. Cold and heat, day and night, wind, rain, dew, and thunder are the waxing and waning of yin and yang. Nature and feelings, forms and bodies, flying and running creatures, grasses and trees are the transformations and movements of images and forms. Is this not vast and far-reaching? Leaving five and ten vacant to constitute the Supreme Ultimate provides the full substance of our minds. Strength, compliance, movement, stillness, attachment, joy, sinking, and entering give expression to the functioning of our nature and feelings. Through these, the potency of spiritual illumination finds expression, and within them reside the principles of human nature and destiny. Is this not concise yet refined? Ah! This is why this Chart is wondrous beyond all wonder. It has no writing, yet is truly the supreme writing for all ages; it has no words, yet is truly the supreme utterance for all ages. Does not the Way reside here?
Later, creators arose: Yao and Shun continued it and composed the sixteen words; Tang and Wu inherited it and composed the oaths and proclamations. King Wen elaborated it and composed the hexagram statements; the Duke of Zhou appended statements to the individual lines; Kongzi wrote the commentaries. These were brought together in the Six Classics, and only then did written expression flourish. By the time of Meng…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
子七篇而文字始辨矣然何莫而非祖於圖哉
蓋數聖人者冥會於異世之感神明其得意之
象所以作之於經垂之於訓凡言乎陰陽者體
其微而彰者也言乎天地萬物者發其閎而肆
者也言乎人心性情者闡其約而精者也不求
之詞而求之畫不求之畫而求之心眞可以上
接包犧氏之統而得文字正脉之傳也故論文
字而始於八卦祖伏羲也精於十六字宗堯舜
禹也盛於六經子湯文周孔也辨於七篇孫孟
===
軻也至於諸子百家非無作者不過文字之餘
裔謂其有得於祖述不可也傳易者曰書不盡
言言不盡意聖人立象以盡意知象之可以盡
意則知圖之可以盡文字矣說經者曰易爲五
經之原蓋五經皆祖於易而易則祖於畫知易
爲五經之祖則圖爲文字之祖又可知矣然則
聖人之立卦也果在於文字之間乎蓋聖人之
道達諸天者也天不言而二曜循環列宿經緯
四維奠位莫非文也莫非道也二氣之推遷五
punctuated:
子七篇，而文字始辨矣。然何莫而非祖於圖哉？蓋數聖人者，冥會於異世之感，神明其得意之象，所以作之於經，垂之於訓。凡言乎陰陽者，體其微而彰者也；言乎天地萬物者，發其閎而肆者也；言乎人心性情者，闡其約而精者也。不求之詞而求之畫，不求之畫而求之心，眞可以上接包犧氏之統，而得文字正脉之傳也。故論文字，而始於八卦，祖伏羲也；精於十六字，宗堯舜禹也；盛於六經，子湯文周孔也；辨於七篇，孫孟軻也。至於諸子百家，非無作者，不過文字之餘裔，謂其有得於祖述，不可也。
傳易者曰：「書不盡言，言不盡意，聖人立象以盡意。」知象之可以盡意，則知圖之可以盡文字矣。說經者曰：「易爲五經之原。」蓋五經皆祖於易，而易則祖於畫。知易爲五經之祖，則圖爲文字之祖，又可知矣。然則聖人之立卦也，果在於文字之間乎？蓋聖人之道，達諸天者也。天不言，而二曜循環，列宿經緯，四維奠位，莫非文也，莫非道也。二氣之推遷，五
translation_en:
…with the seven books of Mencius, writing first became discriminating. Yet what among these did not take the Diagram as its ancestor? These several sages, though living in different ages, met in an unspoken communion of responsiveness. With spiritual insight they understood the images that conveyed their meaning, and thus embodied this understanding in the classics and bequeathed it in their teachings. Whatever speaks of yin and yang gives substance to what is subtle yet manifest in the Diagram; whatever speaks of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things unfolds what is broad and expansive in it; whatever speaks of the human mind, nature, and feelings elucidates what is concise and refined in it. Seek this not in words but in the drawn lines; seek it not in the drawn lines but in the mind. Then one can truly connect with the lineage of Baoxi above and receive the transmission of the orthodox line of writing. Thus, in discussing writing, its beginning in the Eight Trigrams makes Fuxi its ancestor; its refinement in the sixteen characters makes Yao, Shun, and Yu its ancestral patriarchs; its flourishing in the Six Classics makes Tang, King Wen, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius its sons; and its discriminating expression in the seven books makes Meng Ke its grandson. As for the various masters and hundred schools, they certainly had their authors, but these were merely collateral descendants of writing. One cannot say that they attained an understanding of how to carry forward the ancestral tradition.
The commentator on the Changes says: “Writing does not exhaust words, and words do not exhaust meaning; the sages established images to exhaust meaning.” Once we understand that images can exhaust meaning, we understand that the Diagram can encompass all writing. An interpreter of the classics says: “The Changes is the source of the Five Classics.” For the Five Classics all take the Changes as their ancestor, while the Changes takes the drawn lines as its ancestor. Knowing that the Changes is the ancestor of the Five Classics, we can also know that the Diagram is the ancestor of writing. Yet was the sages’ establishment of the hexagrams really confined to writing? The Way of the sages reaches to Heaven. Heaven does not speak, yet the two luminaries revolve in their cycles, the constellations are arrayed like warp and weft, and the four corners take their appointed places: all are pattern, and all are the Way. The successive transformations of the two vital forces, the five…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
行之順布以至品物之流形莫非文也莫非道
也聖人法天以作易則圖位布列爻象交錯寧
非所以成天地之文而呈斯道之體哉故天者
道之祖也畫者文之祖也聖人者萬世之祖也
由此而書契易焉甲曆著焉嫁娶辨焉衣裳制
焉宮室作焉朴野變焉文教興焉由此而口代
天言焉手代天工焉心代天意焉身代天事焉
故謂聖人建天下萬世之極可也謂聖人裁成
輔相以左右民亦可也前乎此者三皇莫神焉
===
史稱其澹泊無為造化之眞宰未彰陰陽之氣
方孕而未育也後乎此者堯舜莫盛焉史稱其
放勳重華造化之元神已暢陰陽之氣長養而
蕃廡也包犧氏上繼三皇應運而生下開羣聖
撫運而治故稱乎祖焉是以論帝系者以包犧
為五帝之首著月令者以太昊為四時之春序
書言三墳而首伏羲六經首易而伏羲為道統
之始合而言之則伏羲信乎為羣聖民物開物
成務之祖非特文字之祖巳也故乾稱父坤稱
punctuated: 行之順布，以至品物之流形，莫非文也，莫非道也。聖人法天以作易，則圖位布列，爻象交錯，寧非所以成天地之文而呈斯道之體哉？故天者，道之祖也；畫者，文之祖也；聖人者，萬世之祖也。由此而書契易焉，甲曆著焉，嫁娶辨焉，衣裳制焉，宮室作焉，朴野變焉，文教興焉。由此而口代天言焉，手代天工焉，心代天意焉，身代天事焉。故謂聖人建天下萬世之極可也，謂聖人裁成輔相以左右民亦可也。前乎此者，三皇莫神焉，史稱其澹泊無為，造化之眞宰未彰，陰陽之氣方孕而未育也。後乎此者，堯舜莫盛焉，史稱其放勳重華，造化之元神已暢，陰陽之氣長養而蕃廡也。包犧氏上繼三皇，應運而生，下開羣聖，撫運而治，故稱乎祖焉。是以論帝系者，以包犧為五帝之首；著月令者，以太昊為四時之春；序書言三墳而首伏羲，六經首易而伏羲為道統之始。合而言之，則伏羲信乎為羣聖民物開物成務之祖，非特文字之祖巳也。故乾稱父，坤稱
translation_en:
…the orderly distribution of the Five Phases, extending to the myriad things taking form in their unfolding: all are pattern, and all are the Way. The sage modeled himself on Heaven in making the Changes. The positions in its diagrams were arrayed, and its lines and images interwoven: was this not how he completed the patterns of Heaven and Earth and displayed the substance of this Way? Thus Heaven is the progenitor of the Way; drawn lines are the progenitor of writing; and the sage is the progenitor of all generations. From this came the substitution of written documents and tallies, the establishment of calendrical reckoning, the distinctions governing marriage, the institution of upper and lower garments, the construction of palaces and dwellings, the transformation of rustic simplicity, and the flourishing of literary and moral instruction. Through this, his mouth spoke for Heaven, his hands performed Heaven’s workmanship, his mind expressed Heaven’s intent, and his person carried out Heaven’s affairs. Thus one may say that the sage established the supreme standard for all under Heaven and for all generations; one may also say that the sage shaped and completed the work of transformation, assisted its workings, and thereby guided the people.
Among those before him, none were more spiritually potent than the Three Sovereigns. The histories describe them as tranquil and free of deliberate action: the true governing power of creation and transformation was not yet manifest, and the vital energies of yin and yang were only gestating, not yet brought forth. Among those after him, none were more glorious than Yao and Shun. The histories describe their “expansive achievement” and “successive splendor”: the primal spirit of creation and transformation had already found full expression, and the vital energies of yin and yang nourished growth into luxuriant abundance. Baoxi succeeded the Three Sovereigns above him, born in response to the destined course of time; he opened the way for the many sages below him, governing in accord with that course. Hence he is called the progenitor. Thus those who discuss imperial genealogies place Baoxi first among the Five Emperors; those who composed the Monthly Ordinances associate Taihao with spring among the four seasons. The preface to the Documents speaks of the Three Ancient Records and places Fuxi first; among the Six Classics, the Changes comes first, and Fuxi stands at the beginning of the transmission of the Way. Taken together, these points show that Fuxi was indeed the progenitor who opened an understanding of things and brought undertakings to completion for the many sages, the people, and all beings—not merely the progenitor of writing. Thus Qian is called father, and Kun is called…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
母乾坤者大父母也伏羲氏其天地之惟肖乎
使無伏羲則如日之夜如月之晦蠢愚之習喬
野之俗民未知書何以同文民未知禮何以辨
等民未知樂何以和行又安能楊天地之大業
而昭耿光於萬世哉故先儒斷其畫易為文字
之祖而開萬世人文之治也說者曰酒醴之美
而明水之尚反其本也文繡之美而疏布之尚
貴其質也三皇之世渾樸未鑿民偽未生包犧
氏作八卦制六書視三皇之脩意已不同矣堯
===
舜益之十六字至於六經詳矣何數聖人者遊
心犧皇不欲與天下相安於忘言哉蓋包犧之
世河出天苞所以開文明之漸時也至堯舜則
著矣所謂堯舜通變垂裳而治亦時也若湯文
周孔則時之異為之也數聖人雖欲與斯世同
躋三皇之治不可得矣故曰作易者其有憂患
乎六經之作亦聖人不得已也孔子欲無言而
祖述惟堯舜聖人之意可識矣厥後文字愈繁
而心學愈支大玄潜虚洞極皆所以病易宋儒
punctuated:
母。乾坤者，大父母也。伏羲氏其天地之惟肖乎！使無伏羲，則如日之夜，如月之晦。蠢愚之習，喬野之俗，民未知書，何以同文？民未知禮，何以辨等？民未知樂，何以和行？又安能楊天地之大業，而昭耿光於萬世哉？故先儒斷其畫易為文字之祖，而開萬世人文之治也。
說者曰：「酒醴之美，而明水之尚，反其本也；文繡之美，而疏布之尚，貴其質也。」三皇之世，渾樸未鑿，民偽未生。包犧氏作八卦，制六書，視三皇之脩意已不同矣。堯舜益之十六字，至於六經詳矣。何數聖人者遊心犧皇，不欲與天下相安於忘言哉？蓋包犧之世，河出天苞，所以開文明之漸，時也；至堯舜則著矣。所謂堯舜通變，垂裳而治，亦時也。若湯文周孔，則時之異為之也。數聖人雖欲與斯世同躋三皇之治，不可得矣。故曰：「作易者，其有憂患乎！」六經之作，亦聖人不得已也。孔子欲無言，而祖述惟堯舜，聖人之意可識矣。厥後文字愈繁，而心學愈支，《大玄》《潜虚》《洞極》皆所以病《易》。宋儒
translation_en:
…mother. Qian and Kun are the great father and mother. Was not Fuxi the very likeness of Heaven and Earth! Without Fuxi, it would have been as when the sun gives way to night or the moon is dark. Amid ignorant habits and uncouth customs [?], if the people did not know writing, how could they share a common script? If they did not know ritual, how could they distinguish ranks? If they did not know music, how could they harmonize their conduct? How, then, could they advance the great work of Heaven and Earth and make its brilliant light shine through all ages? Thus earlier Confucian scholars judged that his drawing of the figures of the Changes made him the progenitor of writing and inaugurated government through human culture for all ages.
An interpreter says: “Though wine and sweet liquor are fine, pure water is esteemed: this is a return to the source. Though patterned and embroidered fabrics are fine, coarse cloth is esteemed: this is valuing the unadorned substance.” In the age of the Three Sovereigns, primordial simplicity had not yet been carved away, and artifice had not yet arisen among the people. Baoxi created the eight trigrams and established the six categories of writing; compared with the Three Sovereigns, his intent in cultivation [?] was already different. Yao and Shun added the sixteen words; with the Six Classics, the teaching became fully elaborated. Why would these several sages, whose thoughts dwelt upon the age of Fuxi, not have wished to rest content with all under Heaven in a state where words were forgotten? In Baoxi’s age, the Yellow River brought forth Heaven’s treasure, thereby initiating the gradual emergence of civilized culture: this was what the times required. By Yao and Shun’s time, that culture had become manifest. The saying that Yao and Shun adapted to change and governed with their robes hanging down likewise describes what the times required. As for Tang, King Wen, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius, their actions arose from differences in their times. Even had these sages wished to bring their age up to the level of government under the Three Sovereigns, they could not have done so. Hence the saying: “Did not the author of the Changes have anxieties and troubles?” The composition of the Six Classics was likewise something the sages could not avoid. Confucius wished to dispense with speech, yet took Yao and Shun alone as his models and transmitted their teachings: from this we may discern the sage’s intent. Thereafter, writings grew ever more abundant, while the learning of the mind branched ever further afield. The Great Mystery [?], the Latent Void, and Penetrating the Ultimate all served to impair the understanding of the Changes. The Confucian scholars of the Song…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
曰圖雖無文吾終日言不離乎是此可與見易
矣
表
擬宋曾公亮進新唐書表嘉祐五年
馬象乾
同考試官教諭翟批場中多務浮詞此作獨
敷叙典實而忠愛之心油然具見宜錄以式
考試官教諭黃批典則可錄
考試官學正宋批有體制
===
嘉祐五年六月某日具官臣曾公亮謹以
所撰新唐書
上進者伏以
道闡
皇猷昭一代經綸之跡史傳
國是備
九重清暇之觀荷掄選以編摩敢對揚而進
獻臣公亮誠惶誠恐稽首頓首上言竊惟握幾
圖理常重保邦之謨因事納忠貴得資治
punctuated:
曰：「圖雖無文，吾終日言不離乎是。」此可與見易矣。

表
擬宋曾公亮進新唐書表，嘉祐五年。
馬象乾

同考試官教諭翟批：「場中多務浮詞，此作獨敷叙典實，而忠愛之心油然具見，宜錄以式。」
考試官教諭黃批：「典則可錄。」
考試官學正宋批：「有體制。」

嘉祐五年六月某日，具官臣曾公亮謹以所撰《新唐書》上進者。伏以道闡皇猷，昭一代經綸之跡；史傳國是，備九重清暇之觀。荷掄選以編摩，敢對揚而進獻。臣公亮誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：竊惟握幾圖理，常重保邦之謨；因事納忠，貴得資治
translation_en:
…said: “Though the diagram contains no writing, all that I say throughout the day never departs from it.” With this understanding, one may indeed discern the meaning of the Changes.

Memorial
A memorial modeled on Zeng Gongliang’s presentation of the New History of the Tang in the fifth year of Jiayou under the Song dynasty [1060].
By Ma Xiangqian.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhai, School Instructor: “Most candidates in the examination strive for empty ornament. This composition alone develops its exposition through authoritative precedents and substantive facts, while a heart of loyalty and devotion reveals itself naturally throughout. It should be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, School Instructor: “Classical and well regulated; worthy of inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner Song, School Instructor: “It observes the proper form and structure.”

On a certain day of the sixth month of the fifth year of Jiayou, your servant Zeng Gongliang, holding the requisite offices, respectfully presents the New History of the Tang that has been compiled.

I humbly consider that the Way elucidates imperial designs, revealing the achievements of a dynasty’s ordering of the realm; history transmits the guiding principles of the state, providing reading for Your Majesty’s tranquil leisure within the palace. Having received the favor of selection for this work of compilation, I venture to acknowledge and extol that charge by presenting the completed work. Your servant Gongliang, in profound fear and trembling, bows low and knocks his head upon the ground to submit these words:

I humbly reflect that, in grasping the pivotal workings of affairs and planning good government, one always esteems counsels for preserving the state; in offering loyal advice through past events, one values obtaining what will assist governance…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之要自皇極演於龜範彝訓是陳迄書法
精於麟經勸懲斯備繼有左右史之職廼
為紀言動之官雖王者能自得師惟
大聖取人為善顧兹唐紀義切殷盤武德紀元
一朝之得失攸在天祐竣簡歷世之興衰
具存草創于吳兢之文就緒于劉昫之手
但文繁而實則隱致意晦而詞徒多故善
惡不炳於丹青而義例未彰於方冊難仍
舊貫宜創新規兹蓋伏遇
===
神功丕顯
聖德難名
恭儉性成四海樂時雍之治
寬仁天縱八荒懷文德之威
闢黃樞以求言圜青衿而論道謂享國長久
已徵於成周而近代箴規莫切於唐室載
稽往牒爰集衆思董以臣脩而任綜核之
司副以臣祁而嚴考訂之責如臣庸品亦
punctuated: 之要。自皇極演於龜範，彝訓是陳；迄書法精於麟經，勸懲斯備。繼有左右史之職，廼為紀言動之官。雖王者能自得師，惟大聖取人為善。顧兹唐紀，義切殷盤。武德紀元，一朝之得失攸在；天祐竣簡，歷世之興衰具存。草創于吳兢之文，就緒于劉昫之手。但文繁而實則隱，致意晦而詞徒多。故善惡不炳於丹青，而義例未彰於方冊。難仍舊貫，宜創新規。兹蓋伏遇神功丕顯，聖德難名，恭儉性成，四海樂時雍之治；寬仁天縱，八荒懷文德之威。闢黃樞以求言，圜青衿而論道。謂享國長久，已徵於成周，而近代箴規，莫切於唐室。載稽往牒，爰集衆思。董以臣脩，而任綜核之司；副以臣祁，而嚴考訂之責。如臣庸品，亦
translation_en:
…the essentials of aiding governance. From the exposition of the August Ultimate in the tortoise-derived Great Plan, enduring precepts were set forth; with the refinement of historical writing in the Classic of the Qilin—the Spring and Autumn Annals—the means of encouragement and admonition were fully supplied. There followed the offices of the Historiographers of the Left and Right, officials charged with recording words and deeds. Though a true king can himself find a teacher, it is the great sage who draws upon others to practice goodness.

Considering this history of the Tang, its import is as pertinent as that of the Yin document Pan Geng. Beginning its chronology with the Wude era, it encompasses the successes and failures of an entire dynasty; bringing its record to a close with the Tianyou era, it preserves the rise and decline of successive reigns in full. It was first drafted in the writings of Wu Jing and brought into order by Liu Xu. Yet its text was prolix and the facts obscured, leaving its meaning unclear amid a mere profusion of words. Thus good and evil were not vividly distinguished in its written record, and its principles and conventions were not made manifest in its volumes. It was difficult to retain the old arrangement; a new framework was needed.

Now we have reverently encountered Your Majesty, whose divine achievements are gloriously manifest and whose sagely virtue is beyond naming. Reverence and frugality are innate in your nature; all within the Four Seas rejoice in your harmonious rule. Heaven has endowed you with generosity and benevolence; the Eight Regions cherish the majesty of your civil virtue. You open the palace’s central precincts to solicit counsel and gather blue-collared scholars about you to discuss the Way. You hold that the means of securing a dynasty’s long duration were already demonstrated by the Zhou, while among more recent precedents none offers more pertinent admonitions than the Tang ruling house. Accordingly, you examined earlier records and assembled the insights of many. You placed your servant Xiu in charge, entrusting him with overall scrutiny, and appointed your servant Qi as his deputy, imposing exacting responsibility for verification and correction. Even one of such mediocre abilities as your servant also…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
忝清班付以提舉之專責諸委託之重自
綸音旣示不敢憚竹帛之勞而汗簡頗繁亦且
費芟艾之力事兼述作義裁古今鉤玄析
類參以彼己之長挈領提綱務盡異同之
見冠本紀以明
帝系敘列傳而辨人賢剛禮樂儀衞之繁盡天
地律曆之變食貨後於選舉刑法先乎藝
文方鎭特書而夷夏之防斯峻爵秩聯列
而堂階之分以昭體統攸存幾微具見事
===
===
雖增而文則省書雖舊而義則新聊備近
世之章程用補名家之闕典竊念臣公亮
等識陋左狐才疎班馬共讎藜閣纂輯凡
三百年累易光陰先後計十七載憂深瘝
曠幸遂
進呈儻芻蕘或採於
萬幾庶葵藿少輸於一得伏願
量弘臨智
心體咸虛
punctuated:
忝清班，付以提舉之專，責諸委託之重。自綸音旣示，不敢憚竹帛之勞；而汗簡頗繁，亦且費芟艾之力。事兼述作，義裁古今，鉤玄析類，參以彼己之長；挈領提綱，務盡異同之見。冠本紀以明帝系，敘列傳而辨人賢，剛禮樂儀衞之繁，盡天地律曆之變。食貨後於選舉，刑法先乎藝文，方鎭特書而夷夏之防斯峻，爵秩聯列而堂階之分以昭。體統攸存，幾微具見。事雖增而文則省，書雖舊而義則新。聊備近世之章程，用補名家之闕典。
竊念臣公亮等，識陋左狐，才疎班馬，共讎藜閣，纂輯凡三百年，累易光陰，先後計十七載。憂深瘝曠，幸遂進呈。儻芻蕘或採於萬幾，庶葵藿少輸於一得。伏願量弘臨智，心體咸虛。
translation_en:
…unworthily occupy a place among the distinguished officials, entrusted with sole responsibility for supervising the undertaking and charged with the weight of this commission. Once the imperial command had been issued, I dared not shrink from the labor of writing on bamboo and silk. Yet the historical records were exceedingly copious, and pruning them also required considerable effort. The undertaking combined transmission with composition, weighing past and present in determining its purport. We probed obscurities and distinguished categories, drawing upon the strengths of others and ourselves; we grasped the essentials and established the main divisions, striving to set out fully the points of agreement and difference. We placed the Basic Annals first to clarify the imperial succession and arranged the biographies to distinguish worthy men. We pruned [?] the profuse material on rites, music, ceremonial, and guards, and fully recorded changes concerning heaven and earth, pitch standards, and calendars. Food and Money follows Selection and Appointment; Punishments and Laws precedes Literature. The regional military commands receive a separate account, thereby making stringent the boundary between non-Chinese peoples and the Chinese realm. Ranks and grades are listed together, making clear the hierarchical distinctions between hall and steps. The organizing framework is preserved, and the subtlest details are fully revealed. Although the matters recorded have increased, the wording has been reduced; although the records are old, their import is new. We offer this to furnish institutional precedents for recent times and to supply what is missing from the works of eminent historians.
I humbly reflect that your servants Gongliang and the others fall short of Zuo and Hu [?] in learning and of Ban and Sima in talent. Together we collated texts in the library, compiling an account spanning three hundred years. Time passed repeatedly in this work: from beginning to end, seventeen years elapsed. Deeply anxious lest we neglect our duties, we have fortunately now succeeded in submitting it to the throne. If something from these woodcutters’ humble counsels should be adopted amid Your Majesty’s myriad affairs, we hope that our devotion, like that of plants turning toward the sun, may yield some small contribution through a single useful insight. We humbly pray that Your Majesty’s capacity be expansive and Your oversight wise, and that Your mind embody complete receptivity …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
鑒憲無愆比弦韋而置諸几座資古有獲切夢
卜而睹乎羹牆
龍德日新上纘綏和之盛
駿謨天保直追沕穆之隆則
寶祚衍於靈長佇見圖書再出而
玉曆傳之永久將與天地無疆臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所撰新唐書二百二十
五卷隨表上
進以
聞
第參塲
策
第一問
王弘誨
同考試官教諭蕭批我
太祖暨我
皇上好生之德先後同揆遠稽堯舜之仁古今合一子能歷歷揄揚之
punctuated:
鑒憲無愆，比弦韋而置諸几座；資古有獲，切夢卜而睹乎羹牆。龍德日新，上纘綏和之盛；駿謨天保，直追沕穆之隆。則寶祚衍於靈長，佇見圖書再出；而玉曆傳之永久，將與天地無疆。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹以所撰《新唐書》二百二十五卷，隨表上進以聞。
第參塲
策
第一問
王弘誨
同考試官教諭蕭批：我太祖暨我皇上，好生之德，先後同揆；遠稽堯舜之仁，古今合一。子能歷歷揄揚之
translation_en:
…May you be without error in taking these precedents as your mirror and rule, placing them beside your desk and seat like the bowstring and leather thong that serve as admonitions; may you gain from consulting antiquity, earnestly seeking the worthy through dreams and divination, and beholding the ancient sages in your broth and upon your walls. May your dragon virtue be renewed daily, carrying forward the flourishing harmony of former times; may Heaven safeguard your grand designs, which directly emulate the profound majesty of antiquity. Then your precious imperial succession will extend through long ages, and we may expect to see the River Chart and Luo Writing appear anew; your imperial calendar will be transmitted forever, enduring without limit alongside Heaven and Earth. Your servant, looking up to Heaven and reverently regarding Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain his intense emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit herewith the 225 juan of the New History of the Tang that we have compiled, accompanying this memorial, for Your Majesty’s notice.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Wang Honghui
Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “Our Taizu and our present Emperor have followed the same standard in their virtue of cherishing life. Tracing this virtue far back to the benevolence of Yao and Shun, we find antiquity and the present united as one. You have been able to extol it clearly, point by point…”

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
盖涵濡有得者他日服官政必其推廣此心者耶
同考試官教諭曾批
聖人之德莫大教民生民二端此作紬繹問目而敷演成章有養之士
也錄之以風天下
考試官教諭黃批
聖朝滋培
國脉全在於此子也仰窺而極贊其盛是得於久道之化者
考試官學正宋批〔敷對詳明獨見此篇〕
聖人之御天下無所不用其仁其敷教也
===
所以奠民性也其恤刑也所以壽民生也
天之生人若有恒性未嘗不欲其奠麗天
地之大德曰生又何嘗不欲斯民之壽且
孳也天何言哉聖人者出體天之心法天
之令建中正以為極本彝倫以為教威之
休之蒸蒸向乂以完其天終身游泳俾勿
壞焉書曰天佑下民作之君作之師惟其
克相上帝寵綏四方是也聖人南面而治
章善癉惡整齊人道刑固不廢然哀矜懲
punctuated:
盖涵濡有得者，他日服官政，必其推廣此心者耶？
同考試官教諭曾批：聖人之德，莫大教民、生民二端。此作紬繹問目，而敷演成章，有養之士也。錄之以風天下。
考試官教諭黃批：聖朝滋培國脉，全在於此。子也仰窺而極贊其盛，是得於久道之化者。
考試官學正宋批〔敷對詳明，獨見此篇。〕
聖人之御天下，無所不用其仁。其敷教也，所以奠民性也；其恤刑也，所以壽民生也。天之生人，若有恒性，未嘗不欲其奠麗。天地之大德曰生，又何嘗不欲斯民之壽且孳也？天何言哉？聖人者出，體天之心，法天之令，建中正以為極，本彝倫以為教，威之休之，蒸蒸向乂，以完其天，終身游泳，俾勿壞焉。《書》曰：「天佑下民，作之君，作之師，惟其克相上帝，寵綏四方。」是也。聖人南面而治，章善癉惡，整齊人道，刑固不廢，然哀矜懲
translation_en:
…Having absorbed this nurturing influence and benefited from it, surely he will extend this same concern when he one day holds office and administers government?
Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: Of the sage’s virtues, none surpass these two: teaching the people and sustaining their lives. This composition draws out the meaning of the question and develops it into a coherent essay. Its author is a man of cultivated character. We record it to offer an example to all under Heaven.
Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: The sagely dynasty’s nurturing of the state’s lifeblood rests entirely upon this. Looking reverently upward, you perceive and lavishly praise its flourishing achievement: you have benefited from the transforming influence of the Way sustained over time.
Examiner Song, School Instructor, comments: 〔Only in this essay do we find an exposition so detailed and clear.〕
In governing all under Heaven, the sage applies his benevolence everywhere. His dissemination of teaching serves to establish the people’s moral nature securely; his compassionate handling of punishments serves to prolong their lives. When Heaven brings human beings into existence, they seem to possess a constant nature [?], and Heaven always desires that it be securely established. The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life: how could they not desire that these people live long and multiply? Yet what does Heaven say? The sage emerges, embodies Heaven’s heart, and models himself upon Heaven’s commands. He establishes centrality and uprightness as the ultimate standard and bases his teaching upon the enduring human relationships. He awes the people and bestows blessings upon them, so that they advance steadily toward good order and preserve intact their Heaven-endowed nature. Throughout their lives they remain immersed in this teaching, so that their nature suffers no damage. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven aids the people below, making rulers and teachers for them, that they may assist the Lord on High in cherishing and bringing peace to the four quarters.” This is what it means. The sage faces south and governs, making goodness manifest and chastising evil, bringing order to human conduct. Punishments are certainly not abolished; yet, with pity and compassion, he seeks to deter…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
創不盡法以為刑俾之知所顧避回翔倫
理以全其生易曰聖人以順動則刑罰清
而民服是也彼堯舜之仁天下豈無所用
其心哉洪荒之時彝倫未叙天下之生乆
矣乃急急焉命契為司徒敬敷五教民始
知方又命臯陶為士師明刑以弼之民始
知法又繼之曰欽哉欽哉惟刑之恤哉若
不樂於用刑聖人之意可識矣故當時之
民不見威福心志不揺日用飲食怡然相
===
安於垂裳之盛忘堯舜之刑而歌堯舜之
仁天下之情可想矣故稱聖人之至者必
曰堯舜而稱仁壽之極者亦必曰堯舜帝
典在焉固賛天行仁之準也巍巍蕩蕩不
可尚已迄周以降脩短代殊仁厚立國者
未免禮樂之讓文學飾治者祗矜縱囚之
歸堯舜之澤乆不曁巳仰體天地之德弘
開唐虞之治其惟我
太祖與我
punctuated: 創，不盡法以為刑，俾之知所顧避，回翔倫理，以全其生。《易》曰：「聖人以順動，則刑罰清而民服。」是也。彼堯舜之仁天下，豈無所用其心哉？洪荒之時，彝倫未叙，天下之生乆矣。乃急急焉命契為司徒，敬敷五教，民始知方；又命臯陶為士師，明刑以弼之，民始知法；又繼之曰：「欽哉！欽哉！惟刑之恤哉！」若不樂於用刑，聖人之意可識矣。故當時之民，不見威福，心志不揺，日用飲食，怡然相安於垂裳之盛，忘堯舜之刑，而歌堯舜之仁，天下之情可想矣。故稱聖人之至者，必曰堯舜；而稱仁壽之極者，亦必曰堯舜。帝典在焉，固賛天行仁之準也。巍巍蕩蕩，不可尚已！迄周以降，脩短代殊，仁厚立國者，未免禮樂之讓；文學飾治者，祗矜縱囚之歸。堯舜之澤，乆不曁巳。仰體天地之德，弘開唐虞之治，其惟我太祖與我
translation_en:
…in chastising them, they do not impose punishments to the full severity of the law. They enable the people to know what to heed and avoid, and to move within the bounds of proper human relationships, thereby preserving their lives. The Book of Changes says: “When the sage acts in accordance with the proper order, punishments become clear and the people submit.” This is what it means. When Yao and Shun extended benevolence throughout the realm, surely they devoted thought and care to doing so! In primordial times, the enduring human relationships had not yet been ordered, though people had long lived in the world. They therefore urgently appointed Xie as Minister of Education to reverently disseminate the five teachings; only then did the people know the proper direction. They also appointed Gao Yao as Judge, clarifying punishments to support those teachings; only then did the people know the law. They followed this with the injunction: “Be reverent! Be reverent! Be solicitous in administering punishments!” They seemed to take no pleasure in using punishment: from this we can discern the sages’ intent. Thus the people of that time were unaware of punitive power or bestowed favor, and their hearts and purposes were untroubled. In their daily lives, eating and drinking, they lived happily and peacefully together amid the flourishing rule of sovereigns who merely let their robes hang down. They forgot Yao and Shun’s punishments and sang of Yao and Shun’s benevolence. We can imagine the feelings of all under Heaven.

Thus, those who speak of the highest sagehood invariably name Yao and Shun; those who speak of the utmost benevolence and longevity likewise invariably name Yao and Shun. The Canons of the Emperors remain: they are indeed the standard for assisting Heaven and practicing benevolence. How lofty and vast—nothing could surpass them! From the Zhou onward, lengths of life differed from age to age. Those who founded their states upon benevolence and generosity still had to concede their inferiority in rites and music; those who adorned their governance with literary learning merely vaunted the return of prisoners whom they had released. The beneficence of Yao and Shun has long ceased to reach the people. To reverently embody the virtue of Heaven and Earth and broadly inaugurate the governance of Tang and Yu—surely this falls to our Taizu and our …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上乎我
太祖高皇帝
聰明睿智
文武聖神
天厭胡元眷之
明命迅掃腥羶之毒穢大啓土宇於版章草昧
之初忿疾於頑特製
大誥三編與民更始申明五常甚惓惓焉必有
藏讀者罪得減等蓋出之干袵滌以文德
===
家傳人誦用夏變夷仁之至也及天下大
定又著
祖訓一書禁後世不用墨劓剕宮之刑歷六年
七謄藁乃獲告成
貽謀之慮遠矣此皆
聖心之獨斷臣下不得而窺者也二百年來莊
誦佩服莫不惴惴聳敬如對越
陟降之靈顧今
深仁厚澤怙冒寰區人心聯結
punctuated:
皇上乎？我太祖高皇帝，聰明睿智，文武聖神。天厭胡元，眷之明命，迅掃腥羶之毒穢，大啓土宇於版章。草昧之初，忿疾於頑，特製《大誥》三編，與民更始，申明五常，甚惓惓焉。必有藏讀者，罪得減等，蓋出之干袵，滌以文德。家傳人誦，用夏變夷，仁之至也。
及天下大定，又著《祖訓》一書，禁後世不用墨、劓、剕、宮之刑。歷六年，七謄藁，乃獲告成，貽謀之慮遠矣。此皆聖心之獨斷，臣下不得而窺者也。二百年來，莊誦佩服，莫不惴惴聳敬，如對越陟降之靈。顧今深仁厚澤，怙冒寰區，人心聯結
translation_en:
…His Majesty? Our founding emperor, Taizu Gao, was perceptive, discerning, sagacious, and wise; accomplished in civil and military affairs, sage-like and divinely gifted. Heaven, weary of the alien Yuan dynasty, favored him with its luminous mandate. He swiftly swept away their foul and poisonous pollution and greatly extended the territory entered in the registers [?]. In the unsettled days of the dynasty’s founding, angered by the obstinate, he specially composed the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao), making a fresh beginning with the people and most earnestly elucidating the Five Constant Virtues. Those who kept and read the work could have their punishments reduced in degree. His purpose was to bring them out of armed strife [?] and cleanse them through civil virtue. Transmitted in every household and recited by every person, it transformed the barbarians through the ways of Xia: this was benevolence at its utmost.
Once all under Heaven was fully pacified, he also wrote the Ancestral Injunctions (Zu Xun), forbidding later generations to employ the punishments of tattooing, cutting off the nose, amputating the feet, and castration [the transcription’s negative wording is doubtful]. Only after six years and seven transcriptions of the draft was the work completed. Far-reaching indeed was his concern to leave guidance for his descendants! These were all decisions made solely within his sagely mind, which his servants could not fathom. For two hundred years, people have solemnly recited these teachings, taken them to heart, and obeyed them, all trembling with heightened reverence, as though standing before his spirit as it ascends and descends. Now profound benevolence and abundant grace shelter the whole realm, and the people’s hearts are united…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
國脉平康丕丕無疆之基引之勿替如明問
所及者不在兹歟至我
皇上以
上聖之資操制作之柄敬
天法
祖恭
己愛民
克孝克仁
盡倫盡制甫當踐祚卽
===
命大小儒臣纂脩
明倫大典詞嚴義正裁自
宸衷伏睹
御製序曰王天下者皆本奉天命承宗祀立人
極建綱常作民之主未有舍是而外求諸道
以能化行四海澤被生民者也又曰上承乎
天奉宗祀於億萬斯年下勤乎民務盡君人
師長之道期於禮樂之興刑罰是中大哉
皇言炳如日月咸切人倫且內列歷代授次後
punctuated: 國脉平康，丕丕無疆之基，引之勿替，如明問所及者，不在兹歟？至我皇上，以上聖之資，操制作之柄，敬天法祖，恭己愛民，克孝克仁，盡倫盡制。甫當踐祚，卽命大小儒臣纂脩《明倫大典》，詞嚴義正，裁自宸衷。伏睹御製序曰：「王天下者，皆本奉天命、承宗祀、立人極、建綱常，作民之主。未有舍是而外求諸道，以能化行四海、澤被生民者也。」又曰：「上承乎天，奉宗祀於億萬斯年；下勤乎民，務盡君人師長之道，期於禮樂之興、刑罰是中。」大哉皇言！炳如日月，咸切人倫。且內列歷代授次，後
translation_en:
…the vital pulse of the state is sound and tranquil. To sustain this vast foundation of boundless duration without letting it lapse—is this not where the answer to your illuminating question lies?

Our Emperor, endowed with the qualities of the highest sage and wielding the authority to establish institutions, reveres Heaven and follows his ancestors, conducts himself reverently and loves the people. He fulfills filial piety and benevolence, giving full expression to human relationships and institutional order. Immediately upon ascending the throne, he commanded scholarly officials of all ranks to compile the Great Compendium on Clarifying Human Relationships (Minglun dadian). Its language is stern and its principles correct, determined by the imperial mind itself. I have reverently read its imperially composed preface, which says: “Those who rule all under Heaven invariably take as their foundation the honoring of Heaven’s Mandate, the continuation of ancestral sacrifices, the establishment of the supreme standard for humanity, and the institution of the cardinal bonds and constant norms, thus becoming masters of the people. Never has anyone abandoned these and sought the Way elsewhere, yet succeeded in extending moral transformation throughout the Four Seas and bringing beneficence to the people.” It also says: “Above, receive Heaven’s charge and maintain ancestral sacrifices for countless millions of years; below, labor diligently for the people, striving to fulfill the Way of their ruler, teacher, and leader, with the aim of bringing ritual and music to flourishing and making punishments fitting.”

How great are these imperial words! They shine like the sun and moon, and all bear directly upon human relationships. Moreover, the work sets out the succession of transmission through successive dynasties [?], and afterward…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
繫
本朝宗圖正閏分明統嗣章著舉世及之文義
情兼盡折人後之論邪正頓釐漢宋謬談
一洗而更新之矣是
典一布如日升暘谷普照迷方卽絕徼窮鄉亦
知引領皆曰
聖人之敎我也於是天下之人相率而趨於道
化父父子子兄兄弟弟各得其所敢有頑
冥不靈勿若于訓者乎頊
===
欲司牧臣工監于祥刑彰信兆民罔干和氣
仁言德意仰廑
綸綍伏睹
勅文曰司民牧者未盡得人或道理不明或律
法不通或任情以作威或深文以鍛獄甚或
貪賄聽屬顛倒是非不顧冤抑是何心歟又
曰省改前愆惟公惟愼盡心聽讞民以不冤
大哉
皇言霈如雲雨有裨民命且內揭古昔帝王及
punctuated:
繫本朝宗圖，正閏分明，統嗣章著。舉世及之文，義情兼盡；折人後之論，邪正頓釐。漢宋謬談，一洗而更新之矣。是典一布，如日升暘谷，普照迷方；卽絕徼窮鄉，亦知引領，皆曰：「聖人之敎我也！」於是天下之人，相率而趨於道化，父父、子子、兄兄、弟弟，各得其所，敢有頑冥不靈、勿若于訓者乎？
頊欲司牧臣工監于祥刑，彰信兆民，罔干和氣，仁言德意，仰廑綸綍。伏睹勅文曰：「司民牧者，未盡得人，或道理不明，或律法不通，或任情以作威，或深文以鍛獄，甚或貪賄聽屬，顛倒是非，不顧冤抑，是何心歟？」又曰：「省改前愆，惟公惟愼，盡心聽讞，民以不冤。」大哉皇言！霈如雲雨，有裨民命。且內揭古昔帝王及
translation_en:
…with a genealogical chart of our dynasty appended, clearly distinguishing legitimate from illegitimate succession and making the imperial line of descent manifest. By adducing the wording concerning succession from father to son and from elder to younger brother, it fully accommodates both righteousness and natural affection; by refuting the arguments concerning becoming another man’s heir, it immediately distinguishes error from correctness. The mistaken doctrines of the Han and Song are swept away, and understanding is renewed. Once this compendium was promulgated, it was like the sun rising from Yanggu, illuminating every region lost in darkness. Even in remote borderlands and impoverished villages, people knew to crane their necks in eager expectation, all saying, “This is the sage’s instruction to us!” Thus the people throughout the realm led one another toward moral transformation. Fathers acted as fathers, sons as sons, elder brothers as elder brothers, and younger brothers as younger brothers, each fulfilling his proper role. Would anyone dare remain obstinate, benighted, and unresponsive, refusing to follow these instructions?
Further [?], wishing the officials charged with shepherding the people to take humane punishments as their guide, to manifest trustworthiness before the myriad people, and not to disturb harmonious influences, His Majesty graciously expressed benevolent counsel and virtuous intentions in an imperial pronouncement. We have reverently read the edict: “Those who administer and shepherd the people have not all been suitably chosen. Some do not understand moral principles; some are unfamiliar with the statutes and laws; some indulge their whims in wielding authority; some apply the law with excessive severity to fabricate cases. Worse still, some covet bribes and heed private solicitations, reversing right and wrong without regard for injustice and oppression. What sort of heart is this?” It further says: “Examine and correct your previous faults. Be impartial and circumspect. Devote yourselves wholeheartedly to hearing and adjudicating cases, so that the people suffer no injustice.” Great indeed are these imperial words! Abundant as rain from the clouds, they benefit the lives of the people. Moreover, within the edict are cited the emperors and kings of antiquity and…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
我
祖宗罔不慎重於刑遡極源委仁愛一心災沴
休祥互發以動其善念國法神譴交儆以
弭其非心俗吏舛錯一舉而震疊之矣是
勅一頒如大寒冱凍忽轉陽春卽昆蟲草木亦
知嚅跂皆曰
聖人之生我也於是天下之人相率而守其章
程强者弱者智者愚者人人寡其過敢有怙
終不悛勿迪于政者乎我
===
皇上之敷敎卽
太祖之仁也亦天之心也有敎則民性自奠性
旣奠則良心鼓舞義氣奮揚可以奠邦矣
皇上之恤刑卽
太祖之仁也亦天之心也無刑則民生自壽民
旣壽則衆心翼戴協氣自臻可以壽國矣
其始也錫庶民之極其究也斂天下之福
後先媲美照耀萬世堯舜之盛不是過也
而所係豈其微哉自今觀之
punctuated:
我祖宗罔不慎重於刑，遡極源委，仁愛一心。災沴休祥互發，以動其善念；國法神譴交儆，以弭其非心。俗吏舛錯，一舉而震疊之矣。是勅一頒，如大寒冱凍忽轉陽春，卽昆蟲草木亦知嚅跂，皆曰：「聖人之生我也！」於是天下之人相率而守其章程，强者、弱者、智者、愚者，人人寡其過，敢有怙終不悛、勿迪于政者乎？
我皇上之敷敎，卽太祖之仁也，亦天之心也。有敎則民性自奠，性旣奠，則良心鼓舞，義氣奮揚，可以奠邦矣。皇上之恤刑，卽太祖之仁也，亦天之心也。無刑則民生自壽，民旣壽，則衆心翼戴，協氣自臻，可以壽國矣。其始也，錫庶民之極；其究也，斂天下之福。後先媲美，照耀萬世，堯舜之盛不是過也。而所係豈其微哉？自今觀之，
translation_en:
…our ancestral emperors, all of whom exercised caution and care in punishments. Tracing the matter fully to its origins and ramifications, the decree expresses a single purpose of benevolent love. Calamities and baleful influences, favorable signs and auspicious omens are invoked in turn to stir their good intentions; the laws of the state and divine chastisement offer warnings together to quell their wrongful thoughts. The errors of commonplace officials are thus checked and subdued at a single stroke. Once this decree was promulgated, it was as though the bitter cold and frozen earth had suddenly given way to sunny spring. Even insects, plants, and trees knew to stir and stretch [?], all saying: “It is the sage who gives us life!” Thereupon, the people throughout the realm led one another in observing its regulations. Strong and weak, wise and foolish, everyone reduced their faults. Would anyone dare persist in wrongdoing without repenting and refuse to follow the government’s directives?
Our Emperor’s dissemination of moral instruction is precisely the benevolence of Taizu, and also the heart of Heaven. With instruction, the people’s nature will of itself become settled. Once their nature is settled, their innate moral sense will be stirred and their spirit of righteousness roused; thereby the realm can be secured. The Emperor’s compassionate care in administering punishments is precisely the benevolence of Taizu, and also the heart of Heaven. With no punishments, the people will naturally enjoy long lives. Once the people enjoy long lives, all hearts will support their sovereign, and harmonious influences will arrive of themselves; thereby the state can be made enduring. At the outset, he bestows upon the common people the supreme standard; in the end, he gathers the blessings of all under Heaven. Successor and predecessor match one another in excellence, shining through ten thousand generations. Even the flourishing age of Yao and Shun did not surpass this. Could what is at stake be insignificant? Viewed from the present, …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
好生之德洽於民心太和之氣充塞宇宙禎符
滋至景貺洊加
壽星現焉甘露零焉玄龜出焉白鹿呈焉芝草
挺焉醴泉湧焉惟
天監觀陰隲於沕穆之中惟
皇上時憲默運於陶鈞之上於萬斯年自今伊
始天下之人遭逢
聖世家興禮讓官無繁刑利涉而思禹功含哺
而懷稷粒又皆舉手加額同聲而祝
===
===
聖人之壽彌熾彌昌與
天無極永孚于休是
典也是
勅也帝典
祖訓今古竝傳則生長壽域胥敎胥生者何可
紀極也猗歟盛哉治之至巳生也南海之
人未探
金匱石室之藏然涵濡
聖化畜積亦有日矣蠡測之見無補高深敬以
punctuated: 好生之德洽於民心，太和之氣充塞宇宙，禎符滋至，景貺洊加。壽星現焉，甘露零焉，玄龜出焉，白鹿呈焉，芝草挺焉，醴泉湧焉。惟天監觀，陰隲於沕穆之中；惟皇上時憲，默運於陶鈞之上。於萬斯年，自今伊始。天下之人遭逢聖世，家興禮讓，官無繁刑，利涉而思禹功，含哺而懷稷粒，又皆舉手加額，同聲而祝聖人之壽，彌熾彌昌，與天無極，永孚于休。是典也，是勅也，帝典祖訓，今古竝傳，則生長壽域、胥敎胥生者，何可紀極也！猗歟盛哉，治之至巳！生也，南海之人，未探金匱石室之藏，然涵濡聖化，畜積亦有日矣。蠡測之見，無補高深，敬以
translation_en:
…The virtue of cherishing life permeates the people's hearts, and the breath of supreme harmony fills the universe. Auspicious signs arrive in increasing numbers, and great blessings repeatedly descend. The Star of Longevity appears; sweet dew falls; a dark tortoise emerges; a white deer presents itself; auspicious fungi spring up; and sweet springs gush forth. Heaven watches over all, silently ordering things amid its profound stillness; His Majesty takes Heaven as his model, silently wielding the potter's wheel of creation. May his reign endure for ten thousand years, beginning now. All under Heaven, fortunate to live in this sagely age, cultivate ritual propriety and deference in their households, while officials impose no excessive punishments. Crossing the waters safely, they recall Yu's achievements; with food in their mouths, they remember Hou Ji's gift of grain. All raise their hands to their foreheads and pray with one voice that the sage sovereign's longevity may flourish ever more abundantly, boundless as Heaven, and forever attended by blessings. This canon and this edict—the imperial canon and the ancestral instructions—are transmitted together across past and present. How could one ever count all those who, born and raised in this realm of longevity, are together instructed and preserved in life? Ah, how magnificent! This is the pinnacle of good government!
I, a student, am a man of Nanhai. Though I have not explored the treasures preserved in golden coffers and stone chambers, I have long been steeped in the sage sovereign's transforming influence and have accumulated some learning. My views, like measuring the sea with a gourd, contribute nothing to such heights and depths. Respectfully, I offer…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一得之愚揄揚
今日之盛
第二問
何天衢
同考試官教諭童批經書之旨道同教殊古
今學者之準的是作發揮所以然處甚明非潛心
理學者不能也
同考試官教諭孫批聖賢因人施教學者由
教體道載在經書無不合□作能闡明其義而末
===
復誦說程子之語以示窮理讀書之要能知所本
者
考試官教諭黃批發明殆盡
考試官學正宋批能知理學源委
聖人之道統於心者也其同而異者所以
為教也聖人之教求諸心者也其異而同
者所以為學也知其所以異而後可以論
學知其所以同而後可以體道譬之水焉
山下出泉無異源也由是之焉為澗為沚
punctuated:
一得之愚，揄揚今日之盛。

第二問
何天衢

同考試官教諭童批：經書之旨，道同教殊，古今學者之準的。是作發揮所以然處甚明，非潛心理學者不能也。

同考試官教諭孫批：聖賢因人施教，學者由教體道，載在經書，無不合。□作能闡明其義，而末復誦說程子之語，以示窮理讀書之要，能知所本者。

考試官教諭黃批：發明殆盡。

考試官學正宋批：能知理學源委。

聖人之道，統於心者也；其同而異者，所以為教也。聖人之教，求諸心者也；其異而同者，所以為學也。知其所以異，而後可以論學；知其所以同，而後可以體道。譬之水焉，山下出泉，無異源也；由是之焉，為澗為沚。
translation_en:
…with this one modest insight, to extol the flourishing age of today.

Second Question
He Tianqu

Comment by Associate Examiner Tong, Instructor: The purport of the canonical writings is that the Way is one, while teachings differ. This is the standard for scholars past and present. This composition explains very clearly why this is so. Only someone who has devoted himself to the Learning of Principle could accomplish this.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor: Sages and worthies adapt their teaching to the person; scholars embody the Way through that teaching. What is recorded in the canonical writings is entirely consistent with this. This composition [?] elucidates its meaning and, at the end, again cites and explains Master Cheng’s words to show the essentials of investigating principle and reading books. Its author understands the foundation on which to rely.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: The elucidation is almost exhaustive.

Comment by Examiner Song, School Instructor: He understands the origins and ramifications of the Learning of Principle.

The Way of the sages is unified in the heart-mind. Its differentiation from unity is what constitutes teaching. The teaching of the sages is sought within the heart-mind. Its convergence from difference into unity is what constitutes learning. Only after understanding why it differs can one discuss learning; only after understanding why it is one can one embody the Way. Take water as an analogy: a spring issues from beneath a mountain, with no difference in its source. Flowing onward from there, it becomes a mountain stream or an islet [?]…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
爲江河其支流至衆也然莫非水之分也
是道之所以異敎也及其歸也以江以河
浮于淮達于泗而皆放乎海焉是學之所
以同於道也又譬之往上都者或帆於水
或馳於陸及其止也無異致也故曰天下
之道殊塗而同歸百慮而一致嗚呼觀其
深矣稽之上古道原於天而備於人然惟
統會於聖人之一心故聖人者道之管也
堯以是傳之舜舜以是傳之禹禹以是傳
===
之湯湯以是傳之文王周公以及於孔子
無異道也一中之授受歷數聖人而不易
焉無異統也乃其因時以立敎而垂之爲
經著之爲書斯其所指不同始言人人殊
矣而其所以爲道與所以造於道未甞異
也今以六經言之自孔子而上聖人達而
在上其道行其紀載聖人之言行有易書
詩禮春秋之爲經皆所以載道也而敎存
乎其中矣其同而異者也經解之言曰溫
punctuated:
爲江河，其支流至衆也，然莫非水之分也，是道之所以異敎也。及其歸也，以江以河，浮于淮，達于泗，而皆放乎海焉，是學之所以同於道也。又譬之往上都者，或帆於水，或馳於陸，及其止也，無異致也。故曰：「天下之道，殊塗而同歸，百慮而一致。」嗚呼，觀其深矣！稽之上古，道原於天而備於人，然惟統會於聖人之一心，故聖人者，道之管也。堯以是傳之舜，舜以是傳之禹，禹以是傳之湯，湯以是傳之文王、周公，以及於孔子，無異道也。一中之授受，歷數聖人而不易焉，無異統也。乃其因時以立敎，而垂之爲經，著之爲書，斯其所指不同，始言人人殊矣，而其所以爲道與所以造於道，未甞異也。

今以六經言之，自孔子而上，聖人達而在上，其道行。其紀載聖人之言行，有《易》《書》《詩》《禮》《春秋》之爲經，皆所以載道也，而敎存乎其中矣，其同而異者也。《經解》之言曰：「溫
translation_en:
…becoming great rivers, with exceedingly numerous tributaries; yet all are divisions of the same water. This is how the Way gives rise to different teachings. When they return, flowing by the great rivers, floating upon the Huai and reaching the Si, they all discharge into the sea. This is how learning converges upon the Way. It is also like those traveling to the capital: some sail by water and others hasten overland, but when they stop, their destination is the same. Hence it is said: “The ways of the world take different paths but return to the same destination; a hundred deliberations arrive at one result.” Ah, how profound this is to contemplate! Looking back to high antiquity, the Way originated in Heaven and was fully embodied in human beings, yet it was comprehensively united only in the single heart of the sage. Thus the sage is the conduit of the Way. Yao transmitted it to Shun, Shun to Yu, Yu to Tang, and Tang to King Wen and the Duke of Zhou, and thence to Kongzi. There was no different Way. The transmission and reception of the single Mean remained unchanged through successive sages: there was no different line of succession. Yet they established teachings according to their times, bequeathing them as classics and setting them down in writings. Their purports differed, and their words began to vary from person to person [?]; nevertheless, what constituted the Way and the means of attaining it never differed.

Now, to speak of the Six Classics: from Kongzi back to earlier times, sages attained eminence and occupied high positions, and their Way was put into practice. Among the classics recording the sages’ words and deeds are the Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites, and Spring and Autumn Annals. All serve to carry the Way, and their teachings reside within them. These are instances of what is the same becoming different. “Explanations of the Classics” states: “Warm…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
良敦厚詩敎也疏通知遠書敎也廣博易
良樂敎也潔淨精微易敎也恭儉莊敬禮
敎也屬辭比事春秋敎也是故因性爲敎
以著入國之義然其明六經之指要不可
易也稽之後儒則荀楊其辨矣荀卿氏曰
禮之敬文也樂之中和也詩書之博也春
秋之微也楊雄氏曰說天莫辨乎易說事
莫辨乎書說體莫辨乎禮說志莫辨乎詩
說理莫辨乎春秋固皆沿戴記之遺義也
===
然非二道也易之通變宜民亦書之政事
也書之降衷恒性亦詩之性情也中和且
平非禮樂之由興乎命德討罪非春秋之
微權乎故曰六經之道同歸實未嘗不相
爲用也雖有爲指之殊者道固本同也以
是而類推焉則所謂詩以道志書以道事
樂以道和易以道陰陽春秋以道名分者
莫非道也莫非聖人之所以爲敎也是謂
聖人有異敎而無異道孟子有曰夫道一
punctuated:
良敦厚，詩敎也；疏通知遠，書敎也；廣博易良，樂敎也；潔淨精微，易敎也；恭儉莊敬，禮敎也；屬辭比事，春秋敎也。是故因性爲敎，以著入國之義。然其明六經之指要，不可易也。稽之後儒，則荀、楊其辨矣。荀卿氏曰：「禮之敬文也，樂之中和也，詩書之博也，春秋之微也。」楊雄氏曰：「說天莫辨乎易，說事莫辨乎書，說體莫辨乎禮，說志莫辨乎詩，說理莫辨乎春秋。」固皆沿戴記之遺義也。

然非二道也。易之通變宜民，亦書之政事也；書之降衷恒性，亦詩之性情也。中和且平，非禮樂之由興乎？命德討罪，非春秋之微權乎？故曰：「六經之道同歸。」實未嘗不相爲用也。雖有爲指之殊者，道固本同也。以是而類推焉，則所謂詩以道志，書以道事，樂以道和，易以道陰陽，春秋以道名分者，莫非道也，莫非聖人之所以爲敎也。是謂聖人有異敎而無異道。孟子有曰：「夫道一」
translation_en:
…kind, sincere, and generous: this is the teaching of the Odes; comprehending broadly and knowing the distant past: this is the teaching of the Documents; being broad-minded, accommodating, and good: this is the teaching of Music; being pure, discerning, and subtle: this is the teaching of the Changes; being respectful, frugal, dignified, and reverent: this is the teaching of the Rites; arranging words and correlating events: this is the teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals.” Thus teaching accords with human dispositions, making clear the meaning of the passage about entering a state and discerning its teachings. Yet this account of the essential purport of the Six Classics cannot be altered. If we examine later Confucian scholars, Xun and Yang distinguished these teachings clearly. Xun Qing said: “The Rites concern reverence and refinement; Music concerns balance and harmony; the Odes and Documents concern breadth of learning; the Spring and Autumn Annals concern subtlety.” Yang Xiong said: “For explaining Heaven, nothing is more discerning than the Changes; for explaining affairs, nothing is more discerning than the Documents; for explaining proper forms, nothing is more discerning than the Rites; for explaining aspirations, nothing is more discerning than the Odes; for explaining principles, nothing is more discerning than the Spring and Autumn Annals.” All these statements indeed follow the meaning handed down in Dai’s Record of Rites.

Yet these are not different Ways. The Changes’ adaptation to change for the benefit of the people is also the governmental business of the Documents. The Documents’ account of Heaven’s bestowal of moral integrity and the constant human nature is also the concern with human nature and feelings found in the Odes. Are balance, harmony, and peace not the source from which rites and music arise? Are appointing the virtuous and punishing the guilty not the subtle judgments of the Spring and Autumn Annals? Thus it is said: “The Ways of the Six Classics converge upon the same end.” Indeed, they have always served one another. Though their purports differ, the Way is fundamentally the same. Extending this reasoning by analogy, the statements that the Odes express aspirations, the Documents recount affairs, Music expresses harmony, the Changes expound yin and yang, and the Spring and Autumn Annals explain distinctions of status and duty all concern the Way; all are means by which the sages teach. This is what is meant by saying that the sages have different teachings but no different Ways. Mengzi said: “The Way is one …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而已矣誠然哉見道之言與以四書言之
自孔子而下聖賢窮而在下其道明其傳
述師弟子之問答有論語大學中庸孟子
之爲書皆所以爲教也而學存乎其中矣
其異而同者也朱子之言曰論語之言莫
非操存涵養之要七篇之旨類多體驗擴
充之功不先乎大學無以盡論孟之精微
不參之論孟無以極中庸之歸趣不會其
極於中庸無以建立大本而經綸天下之
===
大經是雖標别次第以示積德之基然其
明四書之指要不可易也考之聖門則其
說焉詳矣論語專言爲仁直指人心之原
七篇並詳仁義兼統立人之道大學始教
以誠意爲自脩之道明德新民之端也中
庸體道由明誠慎獨以造於篤恭聖神功
化之極也固不外乎朱子之達論也然非
二致也無適無莫未始不言義也强恕求
仁固亦專言仁也誠意爲功而格致先之
punctuated:
而已矣。」誠然哉，見道之言與！以四書言之，自孔子而下，聖賢窮而在下，其道明，其傳述師弟子之問答，有《論語》《大學》《中庸》《孟子》之爲書，皆所以爲教也，而學存乎其中矣，其異而同者也。朱子之言曰：「《論語》之言，莫非操存涵養之要；七篇之旨，類多體驗擴充之功。不先乎《大學》，無以盡《論》《孟》之精微；不參之《論》《孟》，無以極《中庸》之歸趣；不會其極於《中庸》，無以建立大本而經綸天下之大經。」是雖標别次第，以示積德之基，然其明四書之指要，不可易也。

考之聖門，則其說焉詳矣。《論語》專言爲仁，直指人心之原；七篇並詳仁義，兼統立人之道。《大學》始教，以誠意爲自脩之道，明德新民之端也；《中庸》體道，由明誠慎獨以造於篤恭，聖神功化之極也。固不外乎朱子之達論也。然非二致也。「無適無莫」，未始不言義也；「强恕求仁」，固亦專言仁也。誠意爲功，而格致先之
translation_en:
…and that is all.” How true! These are surely words expressing insight into the Way! To speak of the Four Books: from Confucius onward, sages and worthies found themselves in straitened circumstances and lowly positions, yet their Way was clear. Their transmitted accounts and the questions and answers between masters and disciples became such books as the Analects, the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, and the Mencius. All served to teach, and learning was contained within them. Here, too, there is unity amid difference. Master Zhu said: “The words of the Analects are all essentials for holding fast to and nurturing the mind; the purport of the seven books of the Mencius largely concerns the work of personal realization and extension. Without beginning with the Great Learning, one cannot fully comprehend the subtle profundities of the Analects and the Mencius. Without consulting the Analects and the Mencius, one cannot fathom the ultimate import of the Doctrine of the Mean. Without bringing their highest principles together in the Doctrine of the Mean, one cannot establish the great foundation and put in order the great guiding principles of all under Heaven.” Although this distinguishes a sequence to show the foundation for accumulating virtue, its elucidation of the essential purport of the Four Books admits of no alteration.

If we examine the teachings of the school of the Sage, this explanation becomes clear in detail. The Analects speaks particularly of practicing benevolence, pointing directly to the source of the human mind. The seven books of the Mencius elaborate both benevolence and righteousness, comprehensively encompassing the Way by which human beings establish themselves. The Great Learning provides the initial teaching, taking sincerity of intention as the path of self-cultivation: this is the starting point for making bright virtue manifest and renewing the people. The Doctrine of the Mean embodies the Way, proceeding through understanding, sincerity, and vigilance when alone to attain profound reverence—the culmination of the transformative achievements of sageliness and spiritual efficacy. These teachings indeed fall within Master Zhu’s comprehensive account. Yet they do not lead to different ends. “Neither insisting upon nor rejecting any course” has never been without reference to righteousness; “striving to practice reciprocity in pursuit of benevolence” likewise speaks particularly of benevolence. Making the intentions sincere is the work to be done, but investigating things and extending knowledge precede it…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
矣是亦明善也知幾入門而敬信繼之矣
是亦誠意也故曰及其成功一也實未甞
不統于同也間有立言之別者教之或異
也以是而引伸焉則所謂終始之事中和
之致博約之誨存養之說者莫非教也莫
非學者之所以造於道也是謂聖人有異
教而無異學子夏有曰君子學以致其道
誠然哉造道之言與斯義也萬古一道千
聖一心故其道本同而所以異者因時之
===
教也不害其為同其教雖異而所以同者
造道之歸也無病於其異此經書之要準
而為學之不可不審者也自夫仲尼沒而
異端起九師興而易道微三傳作而春秋
散齊魯毛韓詩之末也大戴小戴禮之衰
也書殘于古今詩失于齊魯至於家語齊
論間見雜出大學中庸混編戴記孟氏之
好辯當其時且訾焉而聖人之道之教幾
乎晦矣宋儒類出表章而發明之然後經
punctuated:
矣，是亦明善也。知幾入門而敬信繼之矣，是亦誠意也。故曰：「及其成功，一也。」實未甞不統于同也。間有立言之別者，教之或異也。以是而引伸焉，則所謂終始之事、中和之致、博約之誨、存養之說者，莫非教也，莫非學者之所以造於道也。是謂聖人有異教而無異學。子夏有曰：「君子學以致其道。」誠然哉，造道之言與！斯義也，萬古一道，千聖一心。故其道本同，而所以異者，因時之教也，不害其為同；其教雖異，而所以同者，造道之歸也，無病於其異。此經書之要準，而為學之不可不審者也。

自夫仲尼沒而異端起，九師興而易道微，三傳作而春秋散。齊魯毛韓，詩之末也；大戴小戴，禮之衰也。書殘于古今，詩失于齊魯。至於家語、齊論，間見雜出；大學、中庸，混編戴記。孟氏之好辯，當其時且訾焉，而聖人之道之教幾乎晦矣。宋儒類出，表章而發明之，然後經
translation_en:
… This, too, is making goodness clear. Recognizing the incipient signs provides entry, and reverence and trustworthiness follow: this, too, is making the intentions sincere. Thus it is said, “When success is achieved, it is one and the same.” In truth, these have never failed to converge in unity. Where differences of formulation occasionally occur, it is because the teaching may differ. Extending this reasoning, what are called the affairs of beginning and end, the attainment of equilibrium and harmony, the instruction in broad learning and restraint, and the teachings on preserving and nourishing the mind are all teaching; all are means by which learners advance toward the Way. This is what is meant by saying that the sages differ in their teaching but not in their learning. Zixia said, “The gentleman learns in order to realize his Way.” How true—these are words about attaining the Way!
