Those five men and those nine men ranked foremost among the ministers, and their achievements benefited later generations. Can they truly be beyond our aspiration and attainment? Their moral nature was surely the same as that of others. Zhang Jiuling said, “Those whose achievements benefit the people receive great auspicious signs.” Cui Yuzhi said, “An auspicious person is a treasure of the state.” Both were worthy predecessors from our own region. If talent unites with sincerity, enabling us to live up to their words, would this not promise enduring and great achievement? The Analects says, “In the age of Tang and Yu, and at this time, talent was most abundant.” I, Dasheng, though untalented, venture to bow with clasped hands and raise my voice: toward those above, in praise of this day; toward those below, in exhortation to the many scholars.
Respectfully prefaced by Song Dasheng, Instructor in the Confucian School of Taicang Subprefecture, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili.

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子貢問曰賜也何如子曰女器也曰何器
也曰瑚璉也
仲尼祖述堯舜憲章文武
仁之於父子也義之於君臣也禮之於賓
主也智之於賢者也聖人之於天道也
易
嘉會足以合禮
===
天施地生其益无方
以言乎天地之間則備矣夫乾其靜也專
其動也直是以大生焉夫坤其靜也翕
其動也闢是以廣生焉廣大配天地
物大然後可觀故受之以觀
書
夔曰於予擊石拊石百獸率舞庶尹允諧
帝庸作歌曰勅天之命惟時惟幾乃歌
曰股肱喜哉元首起哉百工熙哉臯陶
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

子貢問曰：「賜也何如？」子曰：「女器也。」曰：「何器也？」曰：「瑚璉也。」

仲尼祖述堯舜，憲章文武。

仁之於父子也，義之於君臣也，禮之於賓主也，智之於賢者也，聖人之於天道也。

易

嘉會足以合禮。

天施地生，其益无方。

以言乎天地之間，則備矣。夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。廣大配天地。

物大然後可觀，故受之以觀。

書

夔曰：「於！予擊石拊石，百獸率舞，庶尹允諧。」帝庸作歌，曰：「勅天之命，惟時惟幾。」乃歌曰：「股肱喜哉，元首起哉，百工熙哉！」臯陶
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Zigong asked, “What sort of person am I, Ci?” The Master said, “You are a vessel.” He asked, “What kind of vessel?” The Master said, “A hu or lian”—precious vessels used in ancestral sacrifices.

Zhongni transmitted the traditions of Yao and Shun and took Kings Wen and Wu as his models.

Benevolence in the relationship between father and son; righteousness between ruler and minister; ritual propriety between guest and host; wisdom in discerning the worthy; and the sage’s relation to the Way of Heaven.

Book of Changes

The gathering of what is excellent suffices to accord with ritual propriety.

Heaven bestows and earth brings forth; their benefits know no bounds.

Speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, it is all fully encompassed. Qian, when still, is concentrated; when moving, it is direct. Thus it brings forth greatness. Kun, when still, is closed; when moving, it opens. Thus it brings forth breadth. In breadth and greatness they match Heaven and Earth.

Only after things become great can they be contemplated; hence it is followed by Guan, “Contemplation.”

Book of Documents

Kui said, “Ah! I strike the stone chimes, tapping them gently; the hundred beasts all dance, and the many officials are truly in harmony.” The emperor then composed a song, saying, “Heed Heaven’s mandate: attend to the proper time and the slightest beginnings.” Then he sang, “When the arms and legs rejoice, the head rises up, and all officials flourish!” Gao Yao…

首明哉股肱良哉庶事康哉
俾萬姓咸曰大哉王言又曰一哉王心克
綏先王之祿永底烝民之生
五者來備各以其敍庶草蕃廡
六服羣辟罔不承德
詩
七月食瓜八月斷壺九月叔苴采荼薪樗
===
食我農夫九月築場圃十月納禾稼黍
稷重穋禾麻菽麥
卜爾百福如幾如式
天生烝民有物有則民之秉彝好是懿德
我受命溥將自天降康豐年穰穰
春秋
秋及江人黃人伐陳〔僖公四年〕
春王二月秦人入滑 夏四月辛巳晉人
及姜戎敗秦于殽〔俱僖公三十有三年〕
punctuated:
拜手稽首，颺言曰：「念哉！率作興事，愼乃憲，欽哉！屢省乃成，欽哉！」乃賡載歌曰：「元首明哉，股肱良哉，庶事康哉！」
俾萬姓咸曰：「大哉王言！」又曰：「一哉王心！」克綏先王之祿，永底烝民之生。
五者來備，各以其敍，庶草蕃廡。
六服羣辟，罔不承德。

詩
七月食瓜，八月斷壺，九月叔苴，采荼薪樗，食我農夫。九月築場圃，十月納禾稼，黍稷重穋，禾麻菽麥。
卜爾百福，如幾如式。
天生烝民，有物有則。民之秉彝，好是懿德。
我受命溥將，自天降康，豐年穰穰。

春秋
秋，及江人、黃人伐陳。〔僖公四年〕
春，王二月，秦人入滑。夏，四月辛巳，晉人及姜戎敗秦于殽。〔俱僖公三十有三年〕
translation_en:
…bowed with hands joined and forehead to the ground, and proclaimed: “Be mindful! In leading undertakings and initiating affairs, take care over your laws; be reverent! Repeatedly examine your accomplishments; be reverent!” Then he continued the song: “When the head is enlightened, the limbs are worthy, and all affairs prosper!”
Cause all the people to say, “Great are the king’s words!” and also, “Undivided is the king’s heart!” Thus may you secure the blessings of the former kings and forever establish the livelihood of the multitude.
When all five come in full measure, each in its proper sequence, all plants flourish luxuriantly.
Among the many rulers of the six service zones, none fails to receive his virtuous influence.

The Book of Odes
In the seventh month we eat melons; in the eighth month we cut gourds; in the ninth month we gather hemp seed. We pick bitter greens and cut ailanthus for firewood, to feed our farmers. In the ninth month we prepare the threshing grounds from the vegetable plots; in the tenth month we bring in the crops: broomcorn and foxtail millet, late- and early-ripening grain, grain and hemp, beans and wheat.
We divine a hundred blessings for you, according to expectation and established pattern [?].
Heaven gives birth to the multitude; for every thing there is a rule. The people hold fast to their constant nature and love this excellent virtue.
The mandate we have received is vast and great; from Heaven descends well-being, with abundant harvests year after year.

The Spring and Autumn Annals
In autumn, we joined the men of Jiang and Huang in attacking Chen. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi.〕
In spring, in the second month of the royal calendar, the men of Qin entered Hua. In summer, on the xinsi day of the fourth month, the men of Jin and the Jiang Rong defeated Qin at Yao. 〔Both in the thirty-third year of Duke Xi.〕

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
春王二月甲子晉侯及秦師戰于彭衙
秦師敗績〔文公二年〕秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕
晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕
春公孫歸父會楚子于宋〔宣公十有五年〕
秋公會劉子晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹
伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子于
平丘 八月甲戌同盟于平丘〔俱昭公十有三年〕
禮記
===
凡養老有虞氏以燕禮夏后氏以饗禮殷
人以食禮周人脩而兼用之
故樂者天地之命中和之紀人情之所不
能免也
天子者與天地參故德配天地兼利萬物
禮之以和爲貴忠信之美優游之法
第貳場
論
萬世文字之祖
punctuated:
春王二月甲子，晉侯及秦師戰于彭衙，秦師敗績〔文公二年〕。秦人伐晉〔文公三年〕。晉侯伐秦〔文公四年〕。
春，公孫歸父會楚子于宋〔宣公十有五年〕。
秋，公會劉子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子于平丘。八月甲戌，同盟于平丘〔俱昭公十有三年〕。
禮記
凡養老，有虞氏以燕禮，夏后氏以饗禮，殷人以食禮，周人脩而兼用之。
故樂者，天地之命，中和之紀，人情之所不能免也。
天子者，與天地參，故德配天地，兼利萬物。
禮之以和爲貴，忠信之美，優游之法。
第貳場
論
萬世文字之祖。
translation_en:
In spring, on the jiazi day of the second month by the royal calendar, the Marquis of Jin fought the Qin army at Pengya. The Qin army suffered a crushing defeat. 〔Second year of Duke Wen.〕 The men of Qin attacked Jin. 〔Third year of Duke Wen.〕 The Marquis of Jin attacked Qin. 〔Fourth year of Duke Wen.〕
In spring, Gongsun Guifu met the Viscount of Chu in Song. 〔Fifteenth year of Duke Xuan.〕
In autumn, the Duke of Lu met the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu at Pingqiu. On the jiaxu day of the eighth month, they jointly entered into a covenant at Pingqiu. 〔Both in the thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕
Record of Rites (Liji)
In caring for the aged, the house of Yu used the rites of informal banquets; the rulers of Xia used the rites of ceremonial feasts; and the people of Yin used the rites of formal meals. The people of Zhou refined these and employed them together.
Thus, music is the mandate of Heaven and Earth, the ordering principle of equilibrium and harmony, and something that human feelings cannot dispense with.
The Son of Heaven forms a triad with Heaven and Earth; hence his virtue matches Heaven and Earth, and he benefits all things alike.
Ritual prizes harmony, esteems loyalty and trustworthiness, and takes unhurried ease as its model.
Second Session
Discourse
The progenitor of writing for all ages.

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢議振貸及養老詔文帝元年
擬唐以李泌爲中書侍郎同平章事誥貞
元二年
擬宋曾公亮進新唐書表嘉祐五年
判語五條
官吏給由
轉解官物
鄉飲酒禮
===
優恤軍屬
帶造段疋
第叄場
策五道
問孟子曰人倫明於上小民親於下夫惟
明倫也而後民知親親親則愛身敬事
遠於刑辟仰率聖人之敎以臻仁壽之
域故曰聖人久於其道而天下化成豈
其微哉惟我
punctuated:
詔誥表內科一道。
擬漢議振貸及養老詔，文帝元年。
擬唐以李泌爲中書侍郎、同平章事誥，貞元二年。
擬宋曾公亮進新唐書表，嘉祐五年。
判語五條。
官吏給由。
轉解官物。
鄉飲酒禮。
優恤軍屬。
帶造段疋。
第叄場
策五道。
問：孟子曰：「人倫明於上，小民親於下。」夫惟明倫也，而後民知親；親親則愛身敬事，遠於刑辟，仰率聖人之敎，以臻仁壽之域。故曰：「聖人久於其道，而天下化成。」豈其微哉！惟我
translation_en:
One composition from among the edict, patent, and memorial categories [?].
Compose an edict in the voice of the Han emperor on deliberating relief loans and provision for the elderly, dated the first year of Emperor Wen’s reign.
Compose a Tang patent appointing Li Mi Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Administrator of Affairs, dated the second year of Zhenyuan.
Compose a memorial in the voice of the Song official Zeng Gongliang presenting the New History of the Tang, dated the fifth year of Jiayou.
Five legal judgments:
Issuing certificates of service to officials and clerks.
Forwarding government property.
The community wine-drinking ceremony.
Preferential relief for military dependents.
The supplementary manufacture of bolts of satin [?].
Third Session
Five policy questions.
Question: Mencius said, “When human relationships are made clear above, the common people below are affectionate toward one another.” Only after these relationships have been clarified do the people understand affection. By loving their kin, they cherish their own persons, attend respectfully to their duties, and keep far from criminal punishments. Reverently following the sage’s teachings, they thereby attain a realm of benevolence and longevity. Thus it is said, “The sage remains constant in his Way, and the transformation of all under Heaven is accomplished.” Could its significance be slight? Now our …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝甫當踐阼卽申五常懷生之類孰
不佩誦興起而於
祖訓又禁後世不用墨劓剕宮之刑其滋培
國脉衞養元神以綿丕丕無疆之基者良有
由矣至我
皇上敬
天法
祖恭
己愛民壽考萬年自今伊始曩者出自
===
宸衷特脩
明倫大典一刊千古之謬以植萬世之綱常
頒布海宇
日照月臨皆曰
聖人之敎我也頃
欲臣工愼刑罔干和氣仰廑
勅旨懇示
欽恤洋洋
聖訓雲行雨施又皆曰
punctuated: 太祖高皇帝甫當踐阼，卽申五常，懷生之類孰不佩誦興起？而於《祖訓》又禁後世不用墨、劓、剕、宮之刑，其滋培國脉、衞養元神，以綿丕丕無疆之基者，良有由矣。至我皇上敬天法祖，恭己愛民，壽考萬年，自今伊始。曩者出自宸衷，特脩《明倫大典》，一刊千古之謬，以植萬世之綱常，頒布海宇，日照月臨，皆曰：「聖人之敎我也。」頃欲臣工愼刑，罔干和氣，仰廑勅旨，懇示欽恤。洋洋聖訓，雲行雨施，又皆曰：
translation_en:
…Emperor Taizu Gao, upon ascending the throne, immediately reaffirmed the Five Constant Virtues. Among all living people, who did not cherish and recite his teachings and feel inspired to action? Moreover, in the Ancestral Instructions he prohibited later generations from employing the punishments of tattooing, cutting off the nose, amputating the feet, and castration [?; the transcription contains an apparent double negative]. There was indeed good reason for his nurturing the lifeblood of the state and safeguarding its vital spirit, thereby perpetuating its magnificent, boundless foundations.

Now our Emperor reveres Heaven, follows his ancestors, conducts himself with reverence, and loves the people. May his long life of ten thousand years begin anew from this day! Previously, moved by his own imperial resolve, he specially commissioned the compilation of the Great Compendium on Clarifying Human Relationships (Minglun dadian), correcting at one stroke the errors of a thousand ages and establishing the cardinal bonds and constant virtues for ten thousand generations. It was promulgated throughout the realm, and wherever the sun and moon shone, all declared: “This is the sage teaching us.” Recently, desiring his officials to exercise caution in punishment and never disturb harmonious influences, he graciously issued an imperial edict earnestly enjoining reverence and compassion in administering punishment. His abundant sagely instructions spread like moving clouds and falling rain, and again all declared: …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
聖人之生我也
好生之德洽於民心
帝祉靈承與
天無極天下之民熙熙皞皞歌舞
聖人之壽彌熾彌昌以迓億萬年永永之庥將
康衢華封不足尚矣何幸而躬逢其盛
哉諸士涵濡
聖澤鼓舞有年願鋪張而揚厲之用昭
謨烈於無窮
===
問夫道一而已矣道一則學為道者亦一
古今聖賢不容殊異為也夷攷古昔帝
王所傳咸謂得統經傳稱說莫匪心法
然不能盡一焉何也說者謂六經之用
同歸乃戴記經解所述入國之敎及荀
卿楊雄氏所謂六經辨說各有攸指于
今沿為體要豈又不相為用與四書垂
訓孔門所授受也由觀魯論專言為仁
七篇之作並詳仁義大學始敎以誠為
punctuated:
聖人之生我也。好生之德洽於民心，帝祉靈承，與天無極。天下之民熙熙皞皞，歌舞聖人之壽，彌熾彌昌，以迓億萬年永永之庥，將康衢華封不足尚矣。何幸而躬逢其盛哉！諸士涵濡聖澤，鼓舞有年，願鋪張而揚厲之，用昭謨烈於無窮。

問：夫道一而已矣，道一則學為道者亦一，古今聖賢不容殊異為也。夷攷古昔帝王所傳，咸謂得統；經傳稱說，莫匪心法，然不能盡一焉，何也？說者謂六經之用同歸，乃戴記《經解》所述入國之敎，及荀卿、楊雄氏所謂六經辨說，各有攸指，于今沿為體要，豈又不相為用與？四書垂訓，孔門所授受也。由觀魯論專言為仁，七篇之作並詳仁義，《大學》始敎以誠為
translation_en:
…“It is the sage who gives us life.” His virtue of cherishing life permeates the hearts of the people. May imperial blessings be auspiciously received, enduring without limit alongside Heaven. The people throughout the realm, joyful and contented, sing and dance in celebration of the sage’s longevity. Ever more flourishing and prosperous, they welcome blessings lasting for countless ages. Even the songs of Kangqu and the blessings offered by the border warden of Hua would scarcely surpass this. How fortunate we are to witness such magnificence in person! You scholars have been steeped in imperial grace and inspired by it for years. We ask you to expound and extol it, thereby making the imperial plans and achievements illustrious for all time.

Question: The Way is one, and nothing more. If the Way is one, then the learning of those who pursue it must also be one; the sages and worthies of antiquity and the present cannot have differed in their practice. Examining impartially what the emperors and kings of antiquity transmitted, all are said to have received the succession to the Way. What the classics and their commentaries expound is invariably the method of cultivating the mind. Yet these teachings cannot all be brought into complete unity. Why is this? Commentators say that the applications of the Six Classics converge upon the same end. Yet the teachings discernible upon entering a state, as described in “Explanation of the Classics” in Dai’s Record of Rites, and the accounts distinguishing the Six Classics given by Xun Qing and Yang Xiong each have their particular focus. These distinctions have continued down to the present as essential principles. Could it be that they do not also serve one another in practice? The instructions handed down in the Four Books were transmitted and received within the school of Confucius. Looking at the Analects of Lu [?], we find that it speaks particularly of practicing benevolence, while the work in seven books, the Mencius, treats both benevolence and righteousness in detail. The Great Learning, in its initial instruction, takes sincerity as…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
自脩之首中庸入德則由明誠慎獨臻
于神化儒先遂以涵養省察體驗擴充
標别為諸書大都其果然與夫味道之
深則表章輔治皆聖人之徒也苟求諸
心而未得焉則古本之定疑孟之作亦
志於道者所不容已耶盍試言之以協
于一
問記曰今人與居古人與稽春秋而降賢
哲類出嘉言善行紀載備矣請以一二
===
所疑者與諸士詳之夫扣角之歌賤士
也而齊賴以霸駔儈之流薄計也而魏
式其閭豈固有當於心與深源既起以
素望也而無功於山桑房相醇儒殆重
器也而無救於陳濤豈真不適於用與
渭川之屯遺恨吞吳而與客圍碁者乃
成淮淝之捷好水之役無徵智膽而歡
呼達旦者顧定澶淵之功他如雲長偉
烈厄於麥城鵬舉精忠阻於恢復豈業
punctuated:
自脩之首；中庸入德，則由明誠、慎獨，臻于神化。儒先遂以涵養、省察、體驗、擴充，標别為諸書大都，其果然與？夫味道之深，則表章輔治，皆聖人之徒也。苟求諸心而未得焉，則古本之定、疑孟之作，亦志於道者所不容已耶？盍試言之，以協于一？
問：記曰：「今人與居，古人與稽。」春秋而降，賢哲類出，嘉言善行，紀載備矣。請以一二所疑者，與諸士詳之。夫扣角之歌，賤士也，而齊賴以霸；駔儈之流，薄計也，而魏式其閭。豈固有當於心與？深源既起以素望也，而無功於山桑；房相醇儒，殆重器也，而無救於陳濤。豈真不適於用與？渭川之屯，遺恨吞吳，而與客圍碁者，乃成淮淝之捷；好水之役，無徵智膽，而歡呼達旦者，顧定澶淵之功。他如雲長偉烈，厄於麥城；鵬舉精忠，阻於恢復。豈業
translation_en:
…the foremost requirement in self-cultivation; in the Doctrine of the Mean, entry into virtue proceeds through understanding, sincerity, and vigilance when alone, reaching spiritual transformation. Earlier Confucian masters accordingly distinguished nurturing, self-examination, experiential realization, and extension as the main purports of the respective books. Is this indeed so? Those who deeply savor the Way, elucidating it and assisting government, are all followers of the sages. Yet if they seek it within their hearts and have not attained it, are such undertakings as establishing the ancient text and composing Doubting Mencius also things that those devoted to the Way cannot refrain from doing? Explain this, so that these approaches may be brought into unity.
Question: A record says: “Dwell with the people of the present; examine the people of antiquity.” Since the Spring and Autumn period, worthy and wise men have appeared in succession, and their admirable words and good deeds have been amply recorded. Let us examine in detail with you candidates one or two matters that occasion doubt. The man who sang while tapping an ox’s horn was a lowly scholar, yet Qi relied upon him to attain hegemony. The man from the ranks of brokers pursued a humble livelihood, yet the ruler of Wei bowed against his carriage crossbar in respect at his neighborhood gate. Was there something in them that accorded with the rulers’ hearts? Shenyuan rose to office on the strength of his established reputation, yet accomplished nothing at Shansang. Chief Minister Fang was a thoroughly learned Confucian, surely a man capable of bearing great responsibilities, yet could not avert disaster at Chentao. Were they truly unsuited to practical service? The encampment by the Wei River left lingering regret over the attempt to swallow Wu [?], whereas the man who played encirclement chess with a guest achieved victory at Huai–Fei. The battle at Haoshui gave no proof of wisdom or courage, whereas the man whose jubilant shouts continued until dawn secured the achievement at Chanyuan. In other cases, Yunchang, for all his magnificent exploits, came to grief at Maicheng; Pengju, for all his wholehearted loyalty, was thwarted in restoring the lost territory. Could it be that achievement …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有所限耶聖人之稱讓於先識國門之
待輸心六丈知固有不及耶夫名實之
際君子之慎所與也乃若所就固有幸
不幸者時耶勢耶抑所遇然也此皆稽
諸古而不能無疑者何以示我
問守令係重民生自古記之矣粤故嶺海
之外而制置之吏正已率物導利興理
代不乏人其循良較著者可更僕數與
夫來晚興歌酌泉勵操不可及矣乃有
===
務清簡而江山名廉易舊政而去珠復
返以至辭俸却餉投珎江中不持一硯
其潔已之致足以廉頑立懦豈聞風興
起者耶抑所植之性爾也又有脩敎庠
序督訓蠶桑使民從化就利而移石奠
瀧陶瓦禦火除苛政減繁課或化輕揚
之俗或感諸番之學無不膾炙人口雖
古所稱道德齊禮何加焉其進於是者
若誠以驅鱷文足起衰至今誦之不忘
punctuated:
有所限耶？聖人之稱，讓於先識；國門之待，輸心六丈。知固有不及耶？夫名實之際，君子之慎所與也。乃若所就，固有幸不幸者，時耶？勢耶？抑所遇然也？此皆稽諸古而不能無疑者，何以示我？

問：守令係重民生，自古記之矣。粤故嶺海之外，而制置之吏，正已率物，導利興理，代不乏人。其循良較著者，可更僕數與？夫來晚興歌，酌泉勵操，不可及矣。乃有務清簡而江山名廉，易舊政而去珠復返，以至辭俸却餉，投珎江中，不持一硯。其潔已之致，足以廉頑立懦，豈聞風興起者耶？抑所植之性爾也？又有脩敎庠序，督訓蠶桑，使民從化就利，而移石奠瀧，陶瓦禦火，除苛政，減繁課，或化輕揚之俗，或感諸番之學，無不膾炙人口。雖古所稱道德齊禮，何加焉？其進於是者，若誠以驅鱷，文足起衰，至今誦之不忘。
translation_en:
…were their achievements subject to limits? Even one acclaimed as a sage yielded to another’s foresight; in waiting at the capital gate, one conceded inwardly to “Sixth Elder” [?]. Does knowledge indeed have its limitations? In matters of reputation and actual merit, the gentleman is cautious about whom he endorses. As for what people accomplish, there are certainly fortunate and unfortunate cases. Is this a matter of the times, of circumstances, or simply of what they happen to encounter? These are all matters that, when examined against antiquity, cannot fail to raise doubts. What can you offer to instruct me?

Question: Prefects and county magistrates bear a weighty responsibility for the people’s livelihood; this has been recorded since ancient times. Guangdong lies beyond the mountain passes, toward the sea. Yet in every age there have been officials administering it who rectified themselves to lead others, promoted benefits, and fostered good order. Could even a succession of attendants enumerate those particularly renowned for conscientious and benevolent government?

Those whose arrival inspired songs lamenting that they had come so late, and who drank from the spring to fortify their integrity, were beyond emulation. Others pursued pure and simple administration, so that rivers and mountains were named for their incorruptibility; or reformed former policies, so that pearls which had disappeared returned. Some even declined their salaries and refused provisions, cast precious objects into the river, and took away not so much as a single inkstone. Their consummate personal integrity could make the avaricious honest and give the weak resolve. Were they stirred to action by hearing of exemplary conduct, or was this simply their innate disposition?

Others cultivated instruction in the schools and supervised training in sericulture, enabling the people to accept moral transformation and gain material benefits. They moved rocks to pacify rapids, fired roof tiles to guard against fire, abolished oppressive policies, and reduced burdensome levies. Some transformed frivolous and flighty customs; others inspired learning among the various foreign peoples [?]. All were celebrated on people’s lips. How could even the ancient ideal of guiding through virtue and bringing order through ritual surpass these achievements? Among those who advanced still further was one whose sincerity drove away crocodiles and whose writings could revive a declining literary tradition: to this day people recite them without forgetting …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而提刑過化洗冤澤物有以啓伊洛之
傳而暨及南粤非特循良已也方今飭
新吏治屢厪
詔旨濱海之區思得若人理之意甚急也而未
之多見豈古今人不相及耶諸士繹思
古昔以論其世盍詳著之將以告夫有
位者
問東廣之患莫過山寇海倭然已非一日
矣文武諸臣防禦亦殫力焉今固未敢
===
再犯城郭顧漳贛惠潮峒酋糾結出沒
山海互為倚伏乃民無完宇野有棄田
在在瘡痍公私告急矣憂時者可不諮
求其故乎議者曰盜皆民也撫之為宜
彼慾已饜未有少挫敵鋒者撫以徇之
是厚其毒而誨之侮也又能必後之不
跳梁乎議者曰盜猶水也不決不潰毅
然大舉力為驅除以雪神人之憤又恐
一隅兵食勞且費焉不能支也議者曰
punctuated:
而提刑過化，洗冤澤物，有以啓伊洛之傳而暨及南粤，非特循良已也。方今飭新吏治，屢厪詔旨，濱海之區，思得若人理之，意甚急也，而未之多見。豈古今人不相及耶？諸士繹思古昔，以論其世，盍詳著之，將以告夫有位者。
問：東廣之患，莫過山寇海倭，然已非一日矣。文武諸臣防禦亦殫力焉，今固未敢再犯城郭。顧漳贛惠潮峒酋糾結，出沒山海，互為倚伏，乃民無完宇，野有棄田，在在瘡痍，公私告急矣。憂時者可不諮求其故乎？議者曰：「盜皆民也，撫之為宜。」彼慾已饜，未有少挫敵鋒者，撫以徇之，是厚其毒而誨之侮也，又能必後之不跳梁乎？議者曰：「盜猶水也，不決不潰。」毅然大舉，力為驅除，以雪神人之憤，又恐一隅兵食，勞且費焉，不能支也。議者曰：
translation_en:
…And the judicial commissioner exerted a transforming influence wherever he went, redressed injustices, and bestowed benefits upon others, helping to extend the transmission of the teachings of Yi and Luo into Nanyue. These were more than merely conscientious and benevolent administrators. Now that repeated imperial edicts call for reforming local administration, the desire to obtain such men to govern the coastal districts is urgent indeed; yet few have appeared. Can it be that men today cannot measure up to those of antiquity? You candidates should reflect carefully upon the past and assess those times. Why not set out your views in detail, so that they may be conveyed to those holding office?
Question: Of the troubles afflicting eastern Guang, none surpass the mountain bandits and Japanese pirates at sea. Yet these troubles are hardly new. The civil and military officials have exhausted their strength in defense, and for now the raiders have indeed not dared to attack the walled cities again. Nevertheless, the chiefs of the mountain settlements of Zhang, Gan, Hui, and Chao band together, appearing and disappearing among the mountains and along the sea, supporting and sheltering one another. Consequently, the people have no intact homes, fields lie abandoned, devastation is everywhere, and both public and private resources are in crisis. Can those concerned about the times fail to inquire into the causes?
Some argue: “The bandits are all common people; it is fitting to pacify them.” Their appetites have already been sated, and no one has dealt even a slight check to the enemy’s onslaught. To pacify them by yielding to them would aggravate their harm and teach them to treat us with contempt. Moreover, could one guarantee that they would not run rampant again?
Some argue: “Bandits are like water: unless a breach is opened, they will not disperse.” [?] Yet if we resolutely launch a major campaign and strive to drive them out, thereby assuaging the indignation of spirits and men alike, there is also the fear that supplying troops and provisions from a single region would entail labor and expense beyond its capacity to sustain. Some argue: …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
倭突則攻海寇嘯則攻山官分信地兵
亦異施僨事者刑師律者否夫合三省
之力協庶官之心尤懼不逮乃分以任
之業相推諉安所圖成乎玆皆疑而未
決者諸士睹厥利害審切乃心必有犁
掃之術可佐安攘者幸昌言以對將採
而用焉
punctuated: 倭突則攻海，寇嘯則攻山，官分信地，兵亦異施；僨事者刑，師律者否。」夫合三省之力，協庶官之心，尤懼不逮，乃分以任之，業相推諉，安所圖成乎？玆皆疑而未決者。諸士睹厥利害，審切乃心，必有犁掃之術可佐安攘者，幸昌言以對，將採而用焉。
translation_en:
…“When Japanese raiders strike, attack at sea; when bandits rally, attack in the mountains. Assign officials separate defense sectors and deploy troops differently in each. Punish those who bring operations to ruin, but not those who observe military discipline [?].” Yet even with the combined strength of three provinces and the united resolve of all the officials, we still fear that these will prove insufficient. If responsibilities are instead divided among them, and they are already shifting blame onto one another, how can success be expected?

These are all matters that remain doubtful and unresolved. You candidates have observed the advantages and dangers involved and carefully weighed them in your minds. Surely you have methods for sweeping away these enemies that can help secure peace within and repel threats from without. Please state your views fully in your replies; they will be considered for adoption and put into practice.

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子貢問曰賜也何如子曰女器也曰何器
也曰瑚璉也
王弘誨
同考試官教諭蕭〔標〕批子貢之才之美全在器
與瑚璉上見此作不用實事意含語中而文采自
露且得夫子之肯宜錄以式
同考試官教諭曾〔士彥〕批提掇□綴不離本意而
===
詞復清勁當是作者
考試官教諭黃〔士元〕批說器與瑚璉處簡健切
實
考試官學正宋〔大昇〕批詞不落套可以為文
聖人因賢者之問而深許其才之美焉甚矣美
才之難得也賢者之才亦器之不凡者聖人之
許之也有以哉昔夫子稱子賤為君子子貢蓋
聞之矣然思齊之念不容自已也乃直以己為
問曰賜也何如將以考其成焉夫子就其才而
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

子貢問曰：「賜也何如？」子曰：「女器也。」曰：「何器也？」曰：「瑚璉也。」

王弘誨

同考試官教諭蕭〔標〕批：「子貢之才之美，全在器與瑚璉上見。此作不用實事，意含語中，而文采自露，且得夫子之肯，宜錄以式。」

同考試官教諭曾〔士彥〕批：「提掇□綴，不離本意，而詞復清勁，當是作者。」

考試官教諭黃〔士元〕批：「說器與瑚璉處，簡健切實。」

考試官學正宋〔大昇〕批：「詞不落套，可以為文。」

聖人因賢者之問，而深許其才之美焉。甚矣，美才之難得也！賢者之才，亦器之不凡者，聖人之許之也有以哉！昔夫子稱子賤為君子，子貢蓋聞之矣。然思齊之念不容自已也，乃直以己為問曰：「賜也何如？」將以考其成焉。夫子就其才而
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Zigong asked, “What do you think of me, Ci?” The Master said, “You are a vessel.” He asked, “What kind of vessel?” The Master said, “A hu or lian sacrificial vessel.”

Wang Honghui

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao〔Biao〕, Instructor: “The excellence of Zigong’s talents is revealed entirely in ‘vessel’ and ‘hu and lian sacrificial vessels.’ This composition uses no concrete historical examples; its meaning is held within its language, while its literary elegance reveals itself naturally. Moreover, it captures the Master’s approval. It should be recorded as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng〔Shiyan〕, Instructor: “Its drawing out and □ linking together [?] do not depart from the original meaning, and its language is also lucid and vigorous. This must be the work of an accomplished writer.”

Comment by Examiner Huang〔Shiyuan〕, Instructor: “The passages explaining ‘vessel’ and ‘hu and lian sacrificial vessels’ are concise, vigorous, and pertinent.”

Comment by Examiner Song〔Dasheng〕, Schoolmaster: “Its language avoids stock formulas; it qualifies as accomplished writing.”

In response to the worthy man’s question, the sage warmly acknowledged the excellence of his talents. How difficult it is to find fine talent! The worthy man’s talents were those of an extraordinary vessel, and the sage had good reason to commend him! Formerly, the Master had called Zijian a gentleman, and Zigong had presumably heard this. Yet he could not restrain his wish to equal him, so he asked directly about himself: “What do you think of me, Ci?” He intended thereby to assess his own attainment. The Master, considering his talents, …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
許之曰物之言利者莫如器先王制之以前民
用者也女也穎悟幾於上智納之至繁而不匱
通達裕於平居投之所向而各適藏乎己者優
然以待用效之動也恢乎有餘地焉不是之器
而何哉夫子旣命之矣然擬議之間未敢自信
也乃又以器為問曰何器也將以究其歸焉夫
子又就其美而許之曰器之可貴者莫如瑚璉
夏商用之以享宗廟者也女也質美之中涵有
以增天下之重才華之外見又以貴天下之觀
===
俾立朝而潤色皇猷其清廟之望乎或從政而
宣昭物采其邦家之光乎是亦瑚璉也已矣夫
先之以有用之才繼之以不凡之器聖人之敎
人也如此子貢方人其容以器自安哉抑子貢
之在聖門視顏閔亦不多讓似非歉於德者夫
子但器其才而於君子若靳焉何耶蓋自切磋
琢磨之時已知其不器矣勵而進之然後達一
貫之旨至聞性與天道而晚年宮牆之喻天階
日月之說則又造乎高明之域所謂君子者非
punctuated: 許之曰：「物之言利者，莫如器，先王制之以前民用者也。女也穎悟幾於上智，納之至繁而不匱；通達裕於平居，投之所向而各適。藏乎己者，優然以待用；效之動也，恢乎有餘地焉。不是之器而何哉？」夫子旣命之矣，然擬議之間，未敢自信也，乃又以器為問曰：「何器也？」將以究其歸焉。夫子又就其美而許之曰：「器之可貴者，莫如瑚璉，夏商用之以享宗廟者也。女也質美之中涵，有以增天下之重；才華之外見，又以貴天下之觀。俾立朝而潤色皇猷，其清廟之望乎？或從政而宣昭物采，其邦家之光乎？是亦瑚璉也已矣。」夫先之以有用之才，繼之以不凡之器，聖人之敎人也如此。子貢方人，其容以器自安哉？抑子貢之在聖門，視顏閔亦不多讓，似非歉於德者。夫子但器其才，而於君子若靳焉，何耶？蓋自切磋琢磨之時，已知其不器矣。勵而進之，然後達一貫之旨，至聞性與天道，而晚年宮牆之喻、天階日月之說，則又造乎高明之域。所謂君子者，非
translation_en:
…praised him, saying: “Among things considered in terms of their usefulness, nothing surpasses a vessel: the former kings fashioned vessels to guide the people in their use of things. Your keen understanding approaches the highest wisdom; even when presented with matters of the utmost complexity, it is never exhausted. Your comprehensive understanding gives you ample resources in ordinary life; wherever you are employed, you prove equal to the task. What you possess within yourself is abundantly sufficient, awaiting employment; when put into action, it leaves ample scope to spare. What could this be but a vessel?”

The Master had thus characterized him, but as he pondered the comparison, he did not yet dare feel certain of himself. He therefore asked further about the vessel: “What sort of vessel?” He wished to pursue the judgment to its ultimate meaning. The Master then praised his excellence, saying: “Among precious vessels, nothing surpasses the hu and lian, which the Xia and Shang used for offerings in their ancestral temples. The excellence of your substance, held within, adds to the weight the world accords you; the brilliance of your talents, manifested outwardly, further ennobles you in the world's eyes. Were you to take your place at court and embellish imperial policies, would you not be an admired figure in the pure ancestral temple? Or, employed in government to make manifest the splendor of things, would you not be a glory to the state? This is indeed to be a hu or lian vessel.”

First he spoke of useful talent, then of an extraordinary vessel: such was the sage's way of teaching. Zigong judged other people; could he allow himself to rest content with being a vessel? Moreover, among the sage's disciples, Zigong scarcely yielded to Yan Hui or Min Sun, and seems not to have been deficient in virtue. Why, then, did the Master merely treat his talent as that of a vessel, while seeming to withhold the designation “gentleman”? In fact, from the time of their discussion of cutting, filing, carving, and polishing, he already knew that Zigong was no mere vessel. He encouraged him to advance, until he grasped the meaning of the single thread running through the Master's teaching and came to hear about human nature and the Way of Heaven. In his later years, Zigong's analogy of the palace wall and his statements about reaching Heaven by steps and about the sun and moon showed that he had attained a realm of lofty illumination. As for what is called a gentleman, was he not…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
歟器不足言矣乃知聖人之敎所以達材亦以
成德
仲尼祖述堯舜憲章文武
何天衢
同考試官敎諭童〔天寵〕批場中作者往往於堯舜
文武上發揮而祖述憲章四字殊欠分曉獨此篇
體認親切隨義闡明一洗浮蔓之習非精於理者
不能式之
同考試官敎諭孫〔曜〕批莊重典雅無一字不從
===
題上發出而末言仲尼得統於人何等氣象大家
之作也
考試官敎諭黃〔光〕批自是說理文字
考試官學正宋〔大昇〕批渾厚精確迥異他作
帝王之道法聖人兼體之焉夫堯舜盡道文武
盡法也夫子兼之非天下之至聖其孰能與於
此且夫蘊諸心之謂道顯諸政之謂法帝王一
而已矣合而有之其惟仲尼乎何者五帝之先
莫不有道而執一中以建極堯舜之道斯全矣
punctuated:
歟？器不足言矣。乃知聖人之敎，所以達材，亦以成德。

仲尼祖述堯舜，憲章文武。
何天衢

同考試官敎諭童〔天寵〕批：場中作者往往於堯舜、文武上發揮，而祖述憲章四字殊欠分曉。獨此篇體認親切，隨義闡明，一洗浮蔓之習。非精於理者不能，式之。

同考試官敎諭孫〔曜〕批：莊重典雅，無一字不從題上發出，而末言仲尼得統於人，何等氣象！大家之作也。

考試官敎諭黃〔光〕批：自是說理文字。

考試官學正宋〔大昇〕批：渾厚精確，迥異他作。

帝王之道法，聖人兼體之焉。夫堯舜盡道，文武盡法也。夫子兼之，非天下之至聖，其孰能與於此？且夫蘊諸心之謂道，顯諸政之謂法，帝王一而已矣。合而有之，其惟仲尼乎？何者？五帝之先，莫不有道，而執一中以建極，堯舜之道斯全矣。
translation_en:
…is he not? To call him a vessel is no longer adequate. Thus we understand that the sage’s teaching brings talent to full expression and also perfects virtue.

“Zhongni transmitted the traditions of Yao and Shun and took Wen and Wu as his models.”
He Tianqu

Comment by Associate Examiner Tong Tianchong, Instructor: Candidates in this examination often elaborate on Yao and Shun, Wen and Wu, yet are distinctly unclear about the four characters meaning “transmitted the traditions” and “took as his models.” This essay alone grasps their meaning intimately and elucidates it point by point, entirely sweeping away the habit of superficial, rambling exposition. Only someone with a refined understanding of principle could achieve this. Take it as a model.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun Yao, Instructor: Dignified and classically elegant, with not a single word that does not arise from the topic. At the end it speaks of Zhongni receiving the succession from earlier men—what grandeur of vision! This is the work of a master.

Comment by Examiner Huang Guang, Instructor: This is indeed writing that expounds principle.

Comment by Examiner Song Dasheng, Instructor: Substantial, profound, and precise; markedly different from the other compositions.

The sage embodied together the Way and the institutional models of the emperors and kings. Yao and Shun brought the Way to its fullest expression; Wen and Wu brought institutional models to their fullest expression. The Master combined both. Who but the supreme sage of all under Heaven could attain this? What is held within the heart is called the Way; what is manifested in government is called an institutional model. For emperors and kings, these are one and the same. Was it not Zhongni alone who possessed them together? Why is this so? Even before the Five Emperors, none lacked the Way; but through holding fast to the single Mean and thereby establishing the supreme standard, the Way of Yao and Shun attained its completeness.

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
仲尼生周之時世相遠也而道之所在其能違
乎是以祖而述之稽神化於唐虞獨宗授受之
秘會幾微於精一庸泯制作之勞於刪書而嘉
其盛焉往者賴以承也於尚論而賛其大焉後
者賴以啓也雖南面之治未甞親炙於其庭而
萬世心學之源若出於口授者矣其所以祖述
堯舜者如此三王之世莫不有法而監二代以
成文文武之法斯備矣仲尼為周之人時相近
也而法之所在能無從乎是以憲章之念斯
===
文之未墜遵成度以周旋幸謨烈之具存昭耿
光以對越在周禮者秩之恪乎其持循也在方
策者舉之煥乎其彰明也雖東周之興未能少
酬乎其志而一代維王之制皆由之終身者矣
其所以憲章文武者如此是則遠宗其道道外
無法也近守其法法外無道也玆仲尼集羣聖
之大成而盡中庸之道者歟雖然仲尼之生得
統於天者也故其道法上與天合凡律天時襲
水土行四時明日月育萬物植乾坤於不毀者
punctuated: 仲尼生周之時，世相遠也，而道之所在，其能違乎？是以祖而述之，稽神化於唐虞，獨宗授受之秘；會幾微於精一，庸泯制作之勞？於刪書而嘉其盛焉，往者賴以承也；於尚論而賛其大焉，後者賴以啓也。雖南面之治未甞親炙於其庭，而萬世心學之源若出於口授者矣。其所以祖述堯舜者如此。三王之世莫不有法，而監二代以成文，文武之法斯備矣。仲尼為周之人，時相近也，而法之所在，能無從乎？是以憲章之，念斯文之未墜，遵成度以周旋；幸謨烈之具存，昭耿光以對越。在周禮者秩之，恪乎其持循也；在方策者舉之，煥乎其彰明也。雖東周之興未能少酬乎其志，而一代維王之制皆由之終身者矣。其所以憲章文武者如此。是則遠宗其道，道外無法也；近守其法，法外無道也。玆仲尼集羣聖之大成而盡中庸之道者歟！雖然，仲尼之生得統於天者也，故其道法上與天合。凡律天時、襲水土、行四時、明日月、育萬物、植乾坤於不毀者
translation_en:
…Zhongni [Confucius] was born in the Zhou period, many generations removed from them; yet could he depart from where the Way resided? Thus he took them as his forebears and transmitted their teachings. Investigating the wondrous transformations wrought under Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun], he took as his sole guiding principle the secret of their transmission and reception of the Way. Comprehending its subtlest workings through refinement and single-mindedness, how could he let their labors in establishing institutions be obscured? In editing the Book of Documents, he praised their flourishing achievements, thereby carrying forward what had come before; in discussing the ancients, he extolled their greatness, thereby enlightening those who came after. Although he had never personally received instruction at their courts in the art of ruling while facing south, the source of the learning of the mind for all ages seemed to have been transmitted orally to him. Such was the manner in which he took Yao and Shun as his forebears and transmitted their teachings.

The ages of the Three Kings all possessed institutional models; by looking to the two preceding dynasties and bringing their cultural forms to completion, Kings Wen and Wu perfected these models. Zhongni was a man of Zhou, close to them in time; where such models existed, could he fail to follow them? Thus he took them as his standards. Mindful that this cultural tradition had not yet fallen away, he conducted himself according to established measures; rejoicing that their plans and achievements survived intact, he made their brilliant light manifest in reverent response to them. What was preserved in the rites of Zhou he set in order, scrupulously adhering to it; what was recorded on tablets and bamboo slips he brought forth, splendidly illuminating it. Although the revival of an Eastern Zhou never afforded even partial fulfillment of his aspirations, throughout his life he followed all the royal institutions of that dynasty. Such was the manner in which he took Wen and Wu as his standards.

Thus he revered the Way of the distant past, for outside the Way there are no institutional models; he upheld the models of the more recent past, for outside those models there is no Way. Was this not how Zhongni brought together the achievements of all the sages and fully realized the Way of the Mean? Yet Zhongni was born receiving the succession from Heaven. Hence his Way and his models accorded above with Heaven. All that takes Heaven’s seasons as its rule, accords with water and soil, moves the four seasons, illuminates the sun and moon, nurtures the myriad things, and establishes Heaven and Earth beyond destruction…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皆是物也豈止宗典謨之數語守周官之一書
而後盡聖人之能事哉故仲尼不獨會帝王之
全而又成天地之大
仁之於父子也義之於君臣也禮之於賓
主也智之於賢者也聖人之於天道也
馬象乾
同考試官教諭翟批此篇機軸變化迥異諸
作且措詞瑩潔可式
考試官教諭黃批結發□聖人盡倫合天
===
處尤妙
考試官學正宋批順鬯
大賢舉至理各屬於人責成之意有在矣蓋仁
義禮智天道人固有之也而各有所屬焉學者
可不責成於已耶孟子之意以為斯道之在天
下也有不可易之分則體道之在吾人也有不
容已之功今自其分而言之德愛曰仁天下無
適而非仁也而父子之恩則無所解焉其所以
愛而能勞養而能敬怡然有恩以相親者非此
punctuated:
皆是物也。豈止宗典謨之數語，守周官之一書，而後盡聖人之能事哉？故仲尼不獨會帝王之全，而又成天地之大。

仁之於父子也，義之於君臣也，禮之於賓主也，智之於賢者也，聖人之於天道也。

馬象乾

同考試官教諭翟批：此篇機軸變化，迥異諸作，且措詞瑩潔，可式。

考試官教諭黃批：結發□聖人盡倫合天處尤妙。

考試官學正宋批：順鬯。

大賢舉至理，各屬於人，責成之意有在矣。蓋仁義禮智天道，人固有之也，而各有所屬焉，學者可不責成於已耶？孟子之意以為斯道之在天下也，有不可易之分；則體道之在吾人也，有不容已之功。今自其分而言之，德愛曰仁，天下無適而非仁也，而父子之恩則無所解焉。其所以愛而能勞，養而能敬，怡然有恩以相親者，非此
translation_en:
…all are this same reality. Could the sage’s full achievement consist merely in taking a few phrases from the Canons and Counsels as his model and adhering to the single book, the Offices of Zhou? Thus Zhongni not only brought together the full achievements of the emperors and kings, but also fulfilled the greatness of Heaven and Earth.

“Benevolence in the relationship between father and son; righteousness in that between ruler and minister; ritual propriety in that between guest and host; wisdom in relation to the worthy; and the sage in relation to the Way of Heaven.”

Ma Xianggan

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhai, Instructor: This essay’s organizing conception shifts and develops in ways markedly different from the other compositions. Its wording is also lucid and polished, worthy of imitation.

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: The conclusion brings out [?] how the sage fulfills human relationships and accords with Heaven; this passage is especially fine.

Comment by Examiner Song, Assistant Instructor: Fluent and clear.

The great worthy sets forth the highest principles, assigning each to its human sphere; his intention to hold people responsible for fulfilling them is evident. Benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, wisdom, and the Way of Heaven are inherently possessed by human beings, yet each has its particular sphere. Can learners fail to hold themselves responsible for their fulfillment? Mencius means that, as this Way exists throughout the world, it has distinctions that cannot be altered; accordingly, embodying the Way within ourselves requires effort that cannot cease. Now, speaking in terms of these distinctions: virtue expressed as love is called benevolence [?]. Nowhere in the world is benevolence absent, yet the affection between father and son is a bond that cannot be dissolved. They love and can therefore toil for one another; they provide support and can do so with reverence; in harmonious affection they draw close to one another—is this not this very …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
仁之浹洽乎德宜曰義天下無適而非義也而
君臣之義則無所逃焉其所以令而不違共而
不二恪然有分以相守者非此義之綱維乎以
節文者存乎禮則於賓主焉見之退讓以飾情
嘉會以章度酬酢之秩固會通之觀矣以甄別
者存乎智則於賢否焉見之秉哲以知人作謀
以辨物權度之精固明覺之良矣至於神明之
撰性命之原淵微而莫測於穆而不已者有天
道焉合一而無間其惟聖人乎窮神以繼其志
===
其藏諸用者渾然天道之本體也知化以述其
事其顯諸仁者燦然天道之流行也非聖人其
孰能之哉是則命之在人者固有不同而性之
在我者則無或異矯其異而歸之同盡性者當
知所從事矣大抵仁義禮智之性即天道之流
行而賦於物者蓋五行之生各一其性其在我
者則有厚薄之稟在人者則有遇不遇之殊而
聖人盡性以立極脩人以合天此其所以爲人
倫之至孟子對舉而互言之示人以希聖之準
punctuated: 仁之浹洽乎？德宜曰義，天下無適而非義也，而君臣之義則無所逃焉。其所以令而不違，共而不二，恪然有分以相守者，非此義之綱維乎？以節文者存乎禮，則於賓主焉見之：退讓以飾情，嘉會以章度，酬酢之秩，固會通之觀矣。以甄別者存乎智，則於賢否焉見之：秉哲以知人，作謀以辨物，權度之精，固明覺之良矣。至於神明之撰、性命之原，淵微而莫測，於穆而不已者，有天道焉。合一而無間，其惟聖人乎？窮神以繼其志，其藏諸用者，渾然天道之本體也；知化以述其事，其顯諸仁者，燦然天道之流行也。非聖人，其孰能之哉？是則命之在人者固有不同，而性之在我者則無或異。矯其異而歸之同，盡性者當知所從事矣。大抵仁義禮智之性，即天道之流行而賦於物者。蓋五行之生，各一其性；其在我者，則有厚薄之稟；在人者，則有遇不遇之殊。而聖人盡性以立極，脩人以合天，此其所以爲人倫之至。孟子對舉而互言之，示人以希聖之準
translation_en:
…the pervasive influence of this benevolence? Virtue expressed in fitting conduct is called righteousness. Nowhere under Heaven is righteousness absent, yet the righteousness binding ruler and minister allows no escape. Commands are obeyed, service is undivided, and each reverently keeps to his allotted role: is this not the sustaining framework of righteousness? Regulation and refinement reside in ritual propriety, which is manifest in relations between guest and host. Deference and yielding give cultivated expression to feelings; harmonious gatherings display proper standards. The ordered exchange of wine offerings and responses indeed reveals how people come together in mutual understanding. Discrimination resides in wisdom, which is manifest in distinguishing the worthy from the unworthy. One employs discernment to understand people and deliberates to distinguish things. Precision in weighing and judging is indeed the excellence of clear awareness.

As for the workings of spiritual intelligence and the source of human nature and destiny—profound, subtle, and unfathomable, august and unceasing—there is the Way of Heaven. Who but the sage can unite with it without any separation? By fathoming the spiritual, he carries forward its intent; what is concealed in practical operation is the undivided fundamental substance of Heaven’s Way. By understanding transformation, he carries on its work; what is manifested in benevolence is the radiant unfolding of Heaven’s Way. Who but the sage could accomplish this?

Thus, what is allotted to people as destiny certainly differs, whereas the nature within us is in no respect different. Those who would fully realize their nature should know where to direct their efforts: to correct these differences and return to what is common. In general, the nature comprising benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom is precisely the unfolding of Heaven’s Way as bestowed upon things. In the generation of things through the Five Phases, each has its own nature. Within us, endowments vary in strength and weakness; among people, circumstances differ according to whether or not they meet with favorable opportunities. The sage, however, fully realizes his nature to establish the supreme standard and cultivates the human to accord with Heaven. This is why he represents the utmost perfection of human relationships. Mencius presents these matters in paired terms that illuminate one another, showing people the standard by which to aspire to sagehood…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也然則學者當何如亦曰盡倫盡性則聖可至
天可合矣故曰道之大原出於天
易
嘉會足以合禮
何天衢
同考試官教諭童〔天胤〕批嘉會處便是禮凡一事
一物都到恰好處便是嘉會此作發明殆盡錄之
同考試官教諭孫〔燿〕批辭不費而意足得潔淨
精微之旨者
===
考試官教諭黃〔子元〕批有體認有布置
考試官學正宋〔大昇〕批說理明白
惟君子能全乎禮之德以見其合天之功也夫
禮之德本無不全者也君子能嘉其所會則禮
即此而在矣是不可見其合天之亨哉文言之
意以爲乾道之亨即人性之禮而爲嘉之會者
人皆有之也能全之者鮮矣惟君子則反情以
和其志殊事有合敬之休可觀可度煥乎其有
章焉比類以成其行隨在皆文德之懿盡善盡
punctuated:
也。然則學者當何如？亦曰：盡倫盡性，則聖可至，天可合矣。故曰：「道之大原出於天。」

易
嘉會足以合禮
何天衢

同考試官教諭童〔天胤〕批：嘉會處便是禮，凡一事一物都到恰好處，便是嘉會。此作發明殆盡，錄之。
同考試官教諭孫〔燿〕批：辭不費而意足，得潔淨精微之旨者。
考試官教諭黃〔子元〕批：有體認，有布置。
考試官學正宋〔大昇〕批：說理明白。

惟君子能全乎禮之德，以見其合天之功也。夫禮之德，本無不全者也。君子能嘉其所會，則禮即此而在矣。是不可見其合天之亨哉？文言之意，以爲乾道之亨，即人性之禮，而爲嘉之會者，人皆有之也。能全之者鮮矣。惟君子則反情以和其志，殊事有合敬之休，可觀可度，煥乎其有章焉；比類以成其行，隨在皆文德之懿，盡善盡
translation_en:
…indeed. What, then, should those who study do? The answer is simply this: fully discharge human relationships and fully realize one’s nature; then sagehood can be attained and harmony with Heaven achieved. Hence it is said: “The great source of the Way issues from Heaven.”

Book of Changes
“The conjunction of excellence suffices to accord with ritual propriety.”
He Tianqu

Comment by Associate Examiner Tong Tianyin, Instructor: Wherever excellence comes together, there is ritual propriety. When every affair and every thing reaches precisely its proper condition, this is the conjunction of excellence. This composition elucidates the matter almost exhaustively; I have selected it for inclusion.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun Yao, Instructor: Its wording is economical, yet its meaning complete. It captures the purport of purity, refinement, and subtlety.

Comment by Examiner Huang Ziyuan, Instructor: It displays both personal understanding and careful arrangement.

Comment by Examiner Song Dasheng, School Instructor: Its exposition of principle is clear.

Only the gentleman can fully realize the virtue of ritual propriety and thereby manifest his achievement in according with Heaven. Now, the virtue of ritual propriety is intrinsically complete in every respect. If the gentleman can bring excellence to what he brings together, ritual propriety is present in that very act. Can we not see in this the free fruition through which he accords with Heaven? The meaning of the Commentary on the Words of the Text is that the free fruition of the Way of Qian is precisely ritual propriety in human nature. Everyone possesses that which constitutes the conjunction of excellence, but few can fully realize it. Only the gentleman turns back upon his feelings to harmonize his intentions. In diverse affairs there is the beauty of united reverence, worthy of observation and emulation, brilliantly displaying its ordered pattern. He brings like things together to perfect his conduct; wherever he finds himself, there is the beauty of cultivated virtue, perfectly good and…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
美郁乎其有文焉苟斯須之未和非嘉會也自
一心以施於四體有周旋焉有折旋焉而動容
所及無一而非莊敬之發見也或彼此之少乖
非嘉會也自一身以達之五倫有主恩焉有主
義焉而交際所接無一而非和順之貫徹也夫
君子嘉其所會如此而謂不足以合禮耶蓋天
理有自然之節文也兹焉觀其會通則文明以
止適得乎天秩之體人事有當然之儀則也兹
焉履其中正則經緯有章允協乎人紀之常周
===
===
旋者其中規也折旋者其中矩也嘉之所在即
會之所在其與天道之咸章也夫豈異哉主恩
者其懽然也主義者其燦然也會之所存即禮
之所存其與品物之咸亨也抑何殊哉噫君子
法天成性之功至矣雖然亨於時為夏萬物皆
相見於後天之卦為離文明之象也君子致禮
以飾治囿天下於文明之中使百姓和天地官
羣物咸若若記之所稱述皆大順之實也豈特
嘉會一身而已哉故曰大禮與天地同節
punctuated: 美，郁乎其有文焉。苟斯須之未和，非嘉會也。自一心以施於四體，有周旋焉，有折旋焉，而動容所及，無一而非莊敬之發見也。或彼此之少乖，非嘉會也。自一身以達之五倫，有主恩焉，有主義焉，而交際所接，無一而非和順之貫徹也。夫君子嘉其所會如此，而謂不足以合禮耶？蓋天理有自然之節文也，兹焉觀其會通，則文明以止，適得乎天秩之體；人事有當然之儀則也，兹焉履其中正，則經緯有章，允協乎人紀之常。周旋者，其中規也；折旋者，其中矩也。嘉之所在，即會之所在，其與天道之咸章也，夫豈異哉？主恩者，其懽然也；主義者，其燦然也。會之所存，即禮之所存，其與品物之咸亨也，抑何殊哉？噫！君子法天成性之功至矣！雖然，亨於時為夏，萬物皆相見；於後天之卦為離，文明之象也。君子致禮以飾治，囿天下於文明之中，使百姓和、天地官、羣物咸若，若記之所稱述，皆大順之實也。豈特嘉會一身而已哉？故曰：「大禮與天地同節。」
translation_en:
…beautiful, richly displaying its patterned refinement. If there is even a moment’s lack of harmony, this is no gathering of excellence. Extending from the single heart to the four limbs, there are circling movements and angular turns; in every movement and expression, nothing fails to manifest solemnity and reverence. If there is even a slight discord between one person and another, this is no gathering of excellence. Extending from one’s own person to the five human relationships, some take affection as their governing principle, others righteousness; in every social encounter, harmony and accord run through all. When the gentleman thus brings excellence to what he gathers together, could one say that this is insufficient to accord with ritual propriety?

Heavenly principle has its natural articulations and patterns. By observing how these converge and interconnect, he unites cultured brilliance with restraint, attaining precisely the substance of Heaven’s ordained order. Human affairs have their proper forms and rules. By practicing their centrality and correctness, he gives clear pattern to the warp and weft of his conduct, truly conforming to the constant norms of human relationships. His circling movements accord with the compass; his angular turns accord with the square. Where excellence is found, there too is its gathering. How does this differ from the Way of Heaven, in which all is manifest? Where affection governs, there is joy; where righteousness governs, there is radiant clarity. Where this gathering abides, there too ritual propriety abides. How does this differ from the flourishing of all varieties of things?

Ah! The gentleman’s achievement in modeling himself on Heaven and bringing his nature to completion is supreme! Yet flourishing corresponds among the seasons to summer, when the myriad things all come into view; among the trigrams of the Later Heaven arrangement, it corresponds to Li, the image of cultured brilliance. The gentleman brings ritual propriety to its fullest realization to adorn his governance, embracing all under Heaven within cultured brilliance. He brings the common people into harmony, Heaven and Earth to the discharge of their offices, and all things into accord. Such conditions, as recounted in the Record of Rites, are all concrete realizations of the great harmony. Could this merely be a gathering of excellence within his own person? Thus it is said: “Great ritual shares the rhythms of Heaven and Earth.”

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以言乎天地之間則備矣夫乾其靜也專
其動也直是以大生焉夫坤其靜也翕
其動也闢是以廣生焉廣大配天地
梁紹蓁
同考試官敎諭童批易之廣大本模倣天地
而有此作推其相生相配始終一貫言之可謂善
發易之精蘊者矣
同考試官敎諭孫批天地乾坤廣大其名雖
殊其實皆易理也此作能提出此意非深於易者
===
不能
考試官敎諭黃批精當
考試官學正宋批明淨
大傳論易之廣大察乎天地因推其相生相配
之妙焉蓋天地之間無乎不備易之廣大也然
不推其相生相配之實抑何以知其然哉大傳
賛易之意謂夫易之爲書也語法象則謂之天
地語性情則謂之乾坤語功用則謂之廣大是
廣大也不但遠近之不遺已也極而言之仰觀
punctuated:
以言乎天地之間，則備矣。夫乾，其靜也專，其動也直，是以大生焉。夫坤，其靜也翕，其動也闢，是以廣生焉。廣大配天地。

梁紹蓁

同考試官敎諭童批：「易之廣大，本模倣天地而有。此作推其相生相配，始終一貫言之，可謂善發易之精蘊者矣。」

同考試官敎諭孫批：「天地、乾坤、廣大，其名雖殊，其實皆易理也。此作能提出此意，非深於易者不能。」

考試官敎諭黃批：「精當。」

考試官學正宋批：「明淨。」

大傳論易之廣大，察乎天地，因推其相生相配之妙焉。蓋天地之間，無乎不備，易之廣大也。然不推其相生相配之實，抑何以知其然哉？大傳賛易之意，謂夫易之爲書也，語法象則謂之天地，語性情則謂之乾坤，語功用則謂之廣大。是廣大也，不但遠近之不遺已也。極而言之，仰觀
translation_en:
“Speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, it encompasses everything. Qian, in stillness, is concentrated; in movement, it is direct: thus it brings forth greatness. Kun, in stillness, draws together; in movement, it opens out: thus it brings forth breadth. In breadth and greatness, it matches Heaven and Earth.”

Liang Shaozhen 梁紹蓁

Comment by Associate Examiner Tong, Instructor: “The breadth and greatness of the Changes arise fundamentally from its modeling itself upon Heaven and Earth. This essay explores their generation and correspondence, explaining them consistently from beginning to end. It may be called skillful in revealing the profound essentials of the Changes.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor: “Heaven and Earth, Qian and Kun, breadth and greatness: although their names differ, in substance they are all the principles of the Changes. This essay brings out that meaning—something only a person deeply versed in the Changes could accomplish.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Precise and apt.”

Comment by Examiner Song, School Director: “Clear and lucid.”

In discussing the breadth and greatness of the Changes, the Great Commentary examines Heaven and Earth and thereby explores the subtle workings of generation and correspondence. Everything between Heaven and Earth is encompassed: such is the breadth and greatness of the Changes. Yet without exploring the actual workings of generation and correspondence, how could one know that this is so? In praising the Changes, the Great Commentary means that, regarding the Changes as a book, when speaking of patterns and images, one calls them Heaven and Earth; when speaking of inherent nature and disposition, one calls them Qian and Kun; when speaking of efficacy and operation, one calls them breadth and greatness. This breadth and greatness mean more than merely leaving out nothing, whether distant or near. To speak of this to its fullest extent, looking upward …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
俯察散殊而不可盡者孰充塞是上際下蟠充
周而不可窮者孰森布是蓋天地之間莫非氣
也而亦莫非理也易之廣大有如此然豈無所
自耶亦本之乾坤耳夫乾天下之至健也其爲
物也一而實靜專以蘊化育之機而動直以達
流行之用藏諸用者顯諸仁舉天下之道器盡
在其包羅之中乾之所以大也易之大不於是
而生耶夫坤天下之至順也其爲物也二而虛
靜翕以涵各正之體而動闢以運無方之化復
===
乎命者育乎神舉天下之形色咸在其含弘之
內坤之所以廣也易之廣不於是而生耶夫廣
大之相生於乾坤若此則其相配乎天地也夫
焉有所强哉蓋天以無不覆爲大而易以無不
備爲德異位同功大有以配乎天矣地以無不
載爲廣而易以無不包爲量異形同體廣有以
配乎地矣天地也乾坤也廣大也一皆易書之
實理也故曰以言乎天地之間則備矣此易之
所以與天地準也與抑天地之廣大由於動靜
punctuated: 俯察，散殊而不可盡者，孰充塞是？上際下蟠，充周而不可窮者，孰森布是？蓋天地之間莫非氣也，而亦莫非理也。易之廣大有如此，然豈無所自耶？亦本之乾坤耳。夫乾，天下之至健也。其爲物也，一而實，靜專以蘊化育之機，而動直以達流行之用。藏諸用者顯諸仁，舉天下之道器，盡在其包羅之中，乾之所以大也。易之大不於是而生耶？夫坤，天下之至順也。其爲物也，二而虛，靜翕以涵各正之體，而動闢以運無方之化。復乎命者育乎神，舉天下之形色，咸在其含弘之內，坤之所以廣也。易之廣不於是而生耶？夫廣大之相生於乾坤若此，則其相配乎天地也，夫焉有所强哉？蓋天以無不覆爲大，而易以無不備爲德，異位同功，大有以配乎天矣。地以無不載爲廣，而易以無不包爲量，異形同體，廣有以配乎地矣。天地也，乾坤也，廣大也，一皆易書之實理也。故曰：「以言乎天地之間，則備矣。」此易之所以與天地準也與？抑天地之廣大由於動靜
translation_en:
…and looking downward to examine: what fills this realm with things so diverse that they cannot be exhausted? Extending to the heights above and spreading through the depths below, what arrays these things that fill every quarter without limit? Between Heaven and Earth there is nothing that is not vital force, and likewise nothing that is not principle. Such is the breadth and greatness of the Changes; yet could these have no source? They are rooted in Qian and Kun alone.

Qian is the utmost vigor in all under Heaven. In its constitution it is one and substantial. In stillness it is concentrated, storing the impulse of transformation and nurture; in movement it is direct, bringing into operation its ceaseless circulation. What is concealed in its functioning is manifest in its benevolence. All the ways and concrete things under Heaven lie within its embrace: this is what makes Qian great. Does not the greatness of the Changes arise from this?

Kun is the utmost compliance in all under Heaven. In its constitution it is twofold and empty. In stillness it closes, containing the substance through which each thing attains its proper nature; in movement it opens, setting in motion transformations unrestricted by any fixed direction. What returns to its allotted destiny is nurtured through its spiritual efficacy. All the forms and colors under Heaven lie within its capacious embrace: this is what makes Kun broad. Does not the breadth of the Changes arise from this?

Since breadth and greatness arise thus from Qian and Kun, how could there be anything forced in their correspondence with Heaven and Earth? Heaven is great because there is nothing it does not cover, while the virtue of the Changes is that there is nothing it does not comprise. Though their positions differ, their accomplishment is the same: in greatness, the Changes can match Heaven. Earth is broad because there is nothing it does not support, while the capacity of the Changes is such that there is nothing it does not encompass. Though their forms differ, their substance is the same: in breadth, the Changes can match Earth. Heaven and Earth, Qian and Kun, breadth and greatness—all are the substantive principles of the book of Changes. Thus it says: “Speaking of what lies between Heaven and Earth, it comprises everything.” Is this not why the Changes is commensurate with Heaven and Earth? Yet the breadth and greatness of Heaven and Earth derive from movement and stillness…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之互根而人心之廣大則由於主靜以立體蓋
靜無不存則動無不得矣性由此盡命由此立
而參賛位育之功有不難致者至此則廣大不
在易而在吾身不以易配天地而以吾身配天
地矣體易之功於是為大
書
夔曰於予擊石拊石百獸率舞庶尹允諧
帝庸作歌曰勅天之命惟時惟幾乃歌
曰股肱喜哉元首起哉百工熙哉皐陶
===
拜手稽首颺言曰念哉率作興事慎乃
憲欽哉屢省乃成欽哉乃賡載歌曰元
首明哉股肱良哉庶事康哉
葉夢熊
同考試官教授秦批史臣先述作樂以紀盛
後述賡歌以示警事不相蒙而意實相成此篇發
明意在言外可與言史者矣
考試官教諭黄批善模寫太和氣象
考試官學正宋批明順
punctuated:
之互根，而人心之廣大則由於主靜以立體。蓋靜無不存，則動無不得矣。性由此盡，命由此立，而參賛位育之功有不難致者。至此，則廣大不在易而在吾身，不以易配天地而以吾身配天地矣。體易之功於是為大。
書
夔曰：「於！予擊石拊石，百獸率舞，庶尹允諧。」帝庸作歌曰：「勅天之命，惟時惟幾。」乃歌曰：「股肱喜哉，元首起哉，百工熙哉！」皐陶拜手稽首，颺言曰：「念哉！率作興事，慎乃憲，欽哉！屢省乃成，欽哉！」乃賡載歌曰：「元首明哉，股肱良哉，庶事康哉！」
葉夢熊
同考試官教授秦批：史臣先述作樂以紀盛，後述賡歌以示警。事不相蒙，而意實相成。此篇發明意在言外，可與言史者矣。
考試官教諭黄批：善模寫太和氣象。
考試官學正宋批：明順。
translation_en:
…being mutually rooted in one another; the breadth and greatness of the human mind, however, arise from giving primacy to stillness in order to establish its foundation. For when nothing is left unpreserved in stillness, nothing will fail to find its proper realization in activity. Through this, one fully realizes one’s nature and establishes one’s Heaven-conferred destiny; the achievement of assisting Heaven and Earth in their proper ordering and nurturing of all things is then not difficult to attain. At this point, breadth and greatness reside not in the Book of Changes but in oneself. It is no longer the Changes that matches Heaven and Earth, but oneself. Herein lies the greatness of the achievement of embodying the Changes.
Book of Documents
Kui said: “Oh! When I strike and tap the stone chimes, the hundred beasts all dance, and the various officials are truly in harmony.” The emperor thereupon composed a song, saying: “Attend diligently to Heaven’s mandate; heed the times and the first stirrings of events.” Then he sang: “When the limbs rejoice, the head rises, and the hundred officials flourish!” Gao Yao bowed with his hands together and his head to the ground, and raised his voice, saying: “Keep this in mind! When leading undertakings and initiating affairs, be careful of your rules. Be reverent! Repeatedly examine your accomplishments. Be reverent!” Then he continued the song: “When the head is enlightened, the limbs are worthy, and all affairs prosper!”
Ye Mengxiong
Comment by Associate Examiner Qin, Prefectural School Instructor: “The court historian first recounts the making of music to record flourishing rule, and then recounts the continuation of the song to convey an admonition. The incidents do not directly bear upon one another, yet their meanings complement each other. This essay elucidates the meaning beyond the words. Its author is someone with whom one may discuss history.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, County School Instructor: “Skillfully depicts the atmosphere of supreme harmony.”
Comment by Examiner Song, Departmental School Instructor: “Clear and coherent.”

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
史臣卽樂以徵治而因述夫君臣交儆之言焉
夫樂以象成功而昭治道者也有虞之治而君
臣責難之無已此其不可及也歟作虞史者以
爲作樂之本在上不在下感召之機以實不以
文觀夔之言曰莫難和者石聲之立辨也予則
於石之小者輕以擊之而其聲清以揚焉於石
之大者重以擊之而其聲濁以下焉石聲旣和
八音有不和者乎莫難感者人物之異情也今
則見夫百獸之舞而物無不和可徵焉見夫庶
尹之諧而人無不和可徵焉人物旣和政治有
不和者乎此皆君德之至而風動之象也治云
尚矣而虞之君臣未已焉帝用作歌以爲靡常
者天之命也而可弗敬乎天無時而不在則無
時而不敬可也天無事而不在則無事而不敬
可也然豈徒君爲然哉乃歌曰君之資臣猶元
首之資股肱也股肱而喜則元首之起庶事之
熈自有不期而然者矣勑天之道不有望于臣
乎臯陶賡歌以爲惟艱者君之位也而可弗念
punctuated:
史臣卽樂以徵治，而因述夫君臣交儆之言焉。

夫樂以象成功而昭治道者也。有虞之治，而君臣責難之無已，此其不可及也歟？作虞史者以爲，作樂之本在上不在下，感召之機以實不以文。觀夔之言曰：「莫難和者，石聲之立辨也。予則於石之小者，輕以擊之，而其聲清以揚焉；於石之大者，重以擊之，而其聲濁以下焉。石聲旣和，八音有不和者乎？莫難感者，人物之異情也。今則見夫百獸之舞，而物無不和可徵焉；見夫庶尹之諧，而人無不和可徵焉。人物旣和，政治有不和者乎？」此皆君德之至而風動之象也。治云尚矣，而虞之君臣未已焉。帝用作歌，以爲靡常者天之命也，而可弗敬乎？天無時而不在，則無時而不敬可也；天無事而不在，則無事而不敬可也。然豈徒君爲然哉？乃歌曰：「君之資臣，猶元首之資股肱也。股肱而喜，則元首之起、庶事之熈，自有不期而然者矣。」勑天之道，不有望于臣乎？臯陶賡歌，以爲惟艱者君之位也，而可弗念
translation_en:
The historian takes music as evidence of good government and accordingly recounts the words by which ruler and ministers admonished one another.

Music represents accomplished achievements and makes manifest the way of government. Under the rule of Yu, ruler and ministers never ceased demanding difficult accomplishments of one another. Was this not what made their rule unsurpassable? The writer of Yu’s history considered that the foundation of making music lay with those above, not those below, and that the workings of influence and response depended on substance, not ornament. Consider Kui’s words: “Nothing is harder to harmonize than the sharply differentiated tones of stone chimes. I strike the smaller stones lightly, and their notes are clear and soaring; I strike the larger stones heavily, and their notes are deep and low. Once the stone chimes are in harmony, can any of the eight classes of musical instruments fail to harmonize? Nothing is harder to move than the differing dispositions of people and other creatures. Yet now we see the hundred beasts dancing, evidence that all creatures are in harmony; we see the various chief officials in accord, evidence that all people are in harmony. Once people and creatures are in harmony, can government fail to be harmonious?” All these are signs of the utmost virtue of the ruler, moving others as the wind does.

Such government was indeed exalted, yet the ruler and ministers of Yu did not stop there. The emperor therefore composed a song, considering that Heaven’s mandate is inconstant: could one fail to be reverent? Since Heaven is present at every moment, one must be reverent at every moment; since Heaven is present in every affair, one must be reverent in every affair. Yet could this apply to the ruler alone? Thus he sang: “The ruler’s reliance on his ministers is like the head’s reliance on the arms and legs. When the arms and legs serve gladly, the head rises and all affairs flourish, naturally and without deliberate contrivance.” Does not the way of attending reverently to Heaven place expectations upon ministers?

Gao Yao continued the song, considering that the ruler’s position is fraught with difficulty: could one fail to bear this in mind…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
哉興事之難而成始不可以不敬也考成之難
而成終不可以不敬也然豈臣所敢與哉乃歌
曰臣之輔君猶股肱之輔元首也元首而明則
股肱之良庶事之康亦有不期而然者矣御下
之權是不在於君乎噫于功成作樂之後而不
忘交相警戒之言有虞太和氣象不可以想見
其盛歟雖然天運于上而百物生者以雨風露
雷之各成其能焉耳君運于上而萬事理者以
禮樂刑政之各舉其職焉耳故簡以御煩而責
===
成乎臣者此之謂善用其明勞以代逸而效法
乎君者此之謂善用其言蓋君道猶天然而臣
道也地道也終其事而不敢有其功者也
六服羣辟罔不承德
蔡蘭
同考試官教授秦批成王承文武大定之後
而首勤攘外安内之功可謂儆戒無虞者矣此作
體貼得出錄之
考試官教諭黄批六服通乎内外此篇發
punctuated:
哉？興事之難，而成始不可以不敬也；考成之難，而成終不可以不敬也。然豈臣所敢與哉？乃歌曰：「臣之輔君，猶股肱之輔元首也。元首而明，則股肱之良、庶事之康，亦有不期而然者矣。御下之權，是不在於君乎？」噫！于功成作樂之後，而不忘交相警戒之言，有虞太和氣象，不可以想見其盛歟？雖然，天運于上而百物生者，以雨風露雷之各成其能焉耳；君運于上而萬事理者，以禮樂刑政之各舉其職焉耳。故簡以御煩而責成乎臣者，此之謂善用其明；勞以代逸而效法乎君者，此之謂善用其言。蓋君道猶天，然而臣道也，地道也，終其事而不敢有其功者也。

六服羣辟罔不承德
蔡蘭

同考試官教授秦批：「成王承文武大定之後，而首勤攘外安内之功，可謂儆戒無虞者矣。此作體貼得出，錄之。」

考試官教諭黄批：「六服通乎内外，此篇發
translation_en:
…could one fail to keep it in mind? Initiating undertakings is difficult, so their inception must be approached with reverence; assessing their accomplishment is difficult, so their completion must likewise be approached with reverence. Yet how could a minister presume to intervene in this? He therefore sang: “Ministers assist their ruler as the limbs assist the head. When the head is clear-sighted, the excellence of the limbs and the good order of all affairs will follow even without deliberate pursuit. Does not the authority to govern subordinates rest with the ruler?” Ah! Even after their achievements were complete and music had been composed, they did not forget words of mutual admonition. Can we not imagine from this the flourishing atmosphere of supreme harmony under Yu Shun? Nevertheless, Heaven moves above and the myriad things come into being only because rain, wind, dew, and thunder each fulfill their capacities. The ruler acts above and all affairs are ordered only because rites, music, punishments, and government each perform their functions. Thus, governing complexity through simplicity and holding ministers responsible for results is what it means to make good use of one's clear-sightedness. Undertaking toil in place of the ruler's ease and modeling oneself upon the ruler is what it means to make good use of one's words. For the ruler's way resembles Heaven, whereas the minister's way is the way of Earth: to bring his work to completion without daring to claim its merit.

“Among the many lords of the six zones of service, none failed to receive his virtue.”
Cai Lan

Associate Examiner Qin, Professor, comments: “King Cheng succeeded to the great settlement achieved by Kings Wen and Wu, yet devoted his first efforts to warding off external threats and securing peace within. He may indeed be said to have remained vigilant when there was no cause for alarm. This composition successfully brings out that understanding. Include it.”

Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “The six zones of service encompass both the inner and outer regions. This essay develops…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
發揮承德處殆盡
考試官學正宋批典雅可錄
觀羣侯之尊王而聖世之治昭矣夫臣者行君
之令而致之民者也于其承德也不可以見一
王之治哉史臣將記成王之訓官而先之以此
意謂人君之御天下也惟德之所施者博則威
之所制者廣周王之撫萬邦也果何如哉但見
自王畿而外有所謂侯甸男采衛焉分土之廣
狹不必其盡同均之爲天子之土也自天子而
===
下有所謂公侯伯子男焉列爵之崇卑不必其
皆齊均之爲天子之臣也侯度固其所素謹者
今則覩王政之惟新益篤其忠貞之念成憲固
其所克遵者今則仰王威之丕振益勤其嚮往
之心知王之考度凡以爲民也而所以承順其
德意者不但朝聘之禮爲然也凡夫敷五典時
地利而聚民之所欲者莫不事爲之制焉知王
之戡亂亦以爲民也而所以對揚其休命者不

punctuated:
發揮承德處殆盡。
考試官學正宋批：典雅可錄。
觀羣侯之尊王，而聖世之治昭矣。夫臣者，行君之令而致之民者也。于其承德也，不可以見一王之治哉？史臣將記成王之訓官，而先之以此，意謂人君之御天下也，惟德之所施者博，則威之所制者廣。周王之撫萬邦也，果何如哉？但見自王畿而外，有所謂侯甸男采衛焉，分土之廣狹，不必其盡同，均之爲天子之土也。自天子而下，有所謂公侯伯子男焉，列爵之崇卑，不必其皆齊，均之爲天子之臣也。侯度固其所素謹者，今則覩王政之惟新，益篤其忠貞之念；成憲固其所克遵者，今則仰王威之丕振，益勤其嚮往之心。知王之考度，凡以爲民也，而所以承順其德意者，不但朝聘之禮爲然也。凡夫敷五典、時地利而聚民之所欲者，莫不事爲之制焉。知王之戡亂，亦以爲民也，而所以對揚其休命者，不但征伐之事爲然也。凡夫詰姦慝、刑暴亂而去
translation_en:
…almost exhaustively develops the meaning of receiving and upholding the king’s virtue.

Comment by Examiner Song, Instructor: Elegant and classical; worthy of inclusion.

Observe how the assembled lords honor the king, and the good government of a sage’s age becomes manifest. Ministers carry out their ruler’s commands and extend them to the people. In their receiving and upholding his virtue, can we not discern the government of an entire reign? When the court historian was about to record King Cheng’s instructions to his officials, he prefaced them with this statement. Its meaning is that, when a ruler governs All under Heaven, only when his virtue reaches widely does his authority exercise control broadly. How, then, did the king of Zhou nurture the myriad states?

Beyond the royal domain lay the zones called hou, dian, nan, cai, and wei. The territories allotted to them were not necessarily all equal in extent, yet all alike were the Son of Heaven’s lands. Below the Son of Heaven were those ranked duke, marquis, earl, viscount, and baron. Their noble ranks were not necessarily equal in dignity, yet all alike were the Son of Heaven’s subjects. They had always scrupulously observed the rules governing the feudal lords; now, seeing the renewal of royal government, they became still more steadfast in their loyalty. They had faithfully followed established laws; now, looking up to the great resurgence of royal authority, they became still more devoted in their allegiance.

They understood that the king’s examination of institutions and standards was wholly for the people’s sake. Accordingly, their means of receiving and complying with his virtuous intentions were not confined to the rites of court attendance and diplomatic visits. In everything concerning the propagation of the five constant duties, the timely use of the land’s resources, and the gathering of what the people desired, they established regulations for every undertaking. They understood that the king’s suppression of disorder was likewise for the people’s sake. Accordingly, their means of responding to and extolling his gracious commands were not confined to military campaigns. In everything concerning the investigation of wickedness, the punishment of violence and rebellion, and the removal of…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
民之所惡者靡不曲爲之防焉外攘之舉卽內
治之脩其在外服者猶其在內服也孰有違上
所命而棄于王化之外者哉畏威之念卽懷德
之心其在大邦者猶其在小邦也孰有自作不
典以干夫王法之譴者哉吁觀此而周王大一
統之治可見矣抑成王承文武之後謨烈具存
固無所謂不庭者淮夷之征止于一隅又安有
所謂四征哉史臣紀成王之初政固以見安不
忘危之心亦以見王者無外之化耳噫有周官
===
以訓百官則自公孤而至卿牧皆有常職治人
備矣有周禮以治天下則自朝廷而達邦國皆
有常禮治法具矣人法具備此有周之治所以
享國長久也歟
詩
天生烝民有物有則民之秉彝好是懿德
王弘誨
同考試官敎諭蕭 批 此題性理之學塲中作
者非浮卽枯是篇以本色語發之沛然殆無餘蘊
punctuated:
民之所惡者，靡不曲爲之防焉。外攘之舉，卽內治之脩；其在外服者，猶其在內服也，孰有違上所命而棄于王化之外者哉？畏威之念，卽懷德之心；其在大邦者，猶其在小邦也，孰有自作不典，以干夫王法之譴者哉？吁！觀此而周王大一統之治可見矣。抑成王承文武之後，謨烈具存，固無所謂不庭者；淮夷之征止于一隅，又安有所謂四征哉？史臣紀成王之初政，固以見安不忘危之心，亦以見王者無外之化耳。噫！有《周官》以訓百官，則自公孤而至卿牧，皆有常職，治人備矣；有《周禮》以治天下，則自朝廷而達邦國，皆有常禮，治法具矣。人法具備，此有周之治所以享國長久也歟？

天生烝民，有物有則。民之秉彝，好是懿德。
