Considering this history of the Tang, its significance is as pressing as that of the Shang’s “Pan Geng.” Beginning its chronology with the Wude era, it encompasses the successes and failures of an entire dynasty; concluding its record with the Tianyou era, it preserves the rise and decline of successive reigns in full. First drafted in the writings of Wu Jing, it was brought into order at the hands of Liu Xu. Yet its prolix writing obscures the facts, leaving its meaning dark while merely multiplying words. Thus good and evil are not clearly illuminated in its painted portraits, nor are its interpretive principles made manifest in its volumes. It would be difficult to retain the old framework; a new design is called for.
We have now humbly encountered Your Majesty, whose divine achievements shine forth magnificently and whose sagely virtue defies description. Reverence and frugality are innate in your nature; all within the Four Seas rejoice in your harmonious government. Heaven has endowed you with generosity and benevolence; the Eight Regions cherish the majesty of your civil virtue. You open the central councils to solicit counsel and gather scholars in blue collars to discuss the Way. You consider that the possibility of a dynasty’s enduring rule has already been demonstrated by the Zhou, while among more recent times no admonitory example bears more directly upon the present than the Tang house. Accordingly, you have examined earlier records and assembled the deliberations of many. You appointed your servant Xiu to direct the work, entrusting him with overall scrutiny, and your servant Qi to assist him, imposing a rigorous responsibility for verification and correction. Even one of such mediocre capacity as your servant likewise…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
忝清班付以提舉之專責諸委託之重自
綸音既示不敢憚竹帛之勞而汗簡頗繁亦且
費芟艾之力事兼述作義裁古今鉤玄析
類參以彼己之長挈領提綱務盡異同之
見冠本紀以明
帝系敘列傳而辨人賢刪禮樂儀衞之繁盡天
地律曆之變食貨後於選舉刑法先乎藝
文方鎭特書而夷夏之防斯峻爵秩聯列
而堂階之分以昭體統攸存幾微具見事
===
雖增而文則省書雖舊而義則新聊備近
世之章程用補名家之闕典竊念臣公亮
等識陋左狐才疎班馬共讎藜閣纂輯凡
三百年累易光陰先後計十七載憂深瘝
曠幸遂
進呈儻芻蕘或採於
萬幾庶葵藿少輸於一得伏願
量弘臨智
心體咸虚
punctuated: 忝清班，付以提舉之專責，諸委託之重。自綸音既示，不敢憚竹帛之勞；而汗簡頗繁，亦且費芟艾之力。事兼述作，義裁古今，鉤玄析類，參以彼己之長；挈領提綱，務盡異同之見。冠本紀以明帝系，敘列傳而辨人賢，刪禮樂儀衞之繁，盡天地律曆之變。食貨後於選舉，刑法先乎藝文；方鎭特書，而夷夏之防斯峻；爵秩聯列，而堂階之分以昭。體統攸存，幾微具見。事雖增而文則省，書雖舊而義則新。聊備近世之章程，用補名家之闕典。竊念臣公亮等，識陋左狐，才疎班馬，共讎藜閣，纂輯凡三百年；累易光陰，先後計十七載。憂深瘝曠，幸遂進呈。儻芻蕘或採於萬幾，庶葵藿少輸於一得。伏願量弘臨智，心體咸虚。
translation_en:
…unworthily occupy a distinguished rank and have been entrusted with the special responsibility of superintendent—a weighty charge [?]. Once the imperial pronouncement had been issued, we dared not shrink from the labor of writing on bamboo and silk. Yet the historical records were voluminous, and pruning them also required considerable effort. Our undertaking combined transmission and composition, its principles bringing judgment to bear on past and present. We probed obscurities and distinguished categories, drawing on the strengths of others and ourselves; we grasped the essentials and set out the main divisions, striving to present fully the points of agreement and difference.

We placed the Basic Annals first to clarify the imperial succession and arranged the Individual Biographies to distinguish worthy men. We reduced excessive detail concerning rites, music, ceremonial, and guards, while fully treating changes in celestial and terrestrial phenomena, pitch standards, and calendrical systems. Food and Money follows Selection and Appointment; Punishments and Laws precedes Arts and Letters. Regional Military Commands receives separate treatment, making the boundary between the non-Chinese peoples and the Chinese more stringent; titles and official ranks are listed together, making distinctions of status as clear as those between a hall and its steps. The governing framework is preserved, and subtle implications are fully revealed. Although the matters covered have increased, the wording has been reduced; although the records are old, their import is new. This may furnish precedents for recent times and supply omissions in the authoritative works of renowned scholars.

Your servant Gongliang and his colleagues humbly reflect that our learning falls short of Zuo and Hu [?], and our talents fall far short of Ban Gu and Sima Qian. Together we collated texts in the imperial library, compiling the history of some three hundred years. Time passed repeatedly: from beginning to end, the work occupied seventeen years. Deeply anxious lest we neglect our duties, we have fortunately at last been able to submit it for imperial inspection. If these humble woodcutters’ words should find acceptance amid Your Majesty’s myriad affairs, we hope that our devotion, like that of plants turning toward the sun, may offer some small contribution through a single useful insight. We humbly wish that Your Majesty may enlarge your capacity through the wisdom of Overseeing and embody in your heart the openness of Influence…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
鑒憲無愆比弦韋而置諸几座資古有獲切夢
卜而睹乎羹牆
龍德日新上纘綏和之盛
駿謨天保直追沕穆之隆則
寶祚衍於靈長佇見圖書再出而
玉曆傳之永久將與天地無疆臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹以所撰新唐書二百二十
五卷隨表上
===
進以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
王弘誨
同考試官敎諭蕭 批 我
太祖暨我
皇上好生之德先後同揆遠稽堯舜之仁古今合一子能歷歷揄揚之
punctuated:
鑒憲無愆，比弦韋而置諸几座；資古有獲，切夢卜而睹乎羹牆。龍德日新，上纘綏和之盛；駿謨天保，直追沕穆之隆。則寶祚衍於靈長，佇見圖書再出；而玉曆傳之永久，將與天地無疆。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屛營之至，謹以所撰《新唐書》二百二十五卷，隨表上進以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
王弘誨
同考試官敎諭蕭批：「我太祖暨我皇上，好生之德，先後同揆；遠稽堯舜之仁，古今合一。子能歷歷揄揚之」
translation_en:
…May you examine these precedents without error, setting them beside your desk and seat like the bowstring and leather thong used as reminders of self-discipline; may you gain from antiquity, earnestly seeking worthy ministers through dreams and divination and beholding the sages of old in your soup and upon the wall. May your dragon virtue be renewed daily, continuing the flourishing peace and harmony of earlier times; may Heaven preserve your magnificent plans, that you may directly rival the profound majesty of antiquity. Then your precious imperial throne will endure through distant ages, and we may soon behold the auspicious Chart and Writing appear once more; your imperial succession will be transmitted forever, boundless as Heaven and Earth. Your servant, looking up to Heaven and reverently regarding Your Sagely Majesty, cannot contain his intense emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit herewith the New History of the Tang, which we have compiled in 225 juan, accompanying this memorial for your imperial notice.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Wang Honghui

Comment by Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor: “Our Taizu and our reigning emperor have followed the same standard in their virtue of cherishing life. Tracing this far back to the benevolence of Yao and Shun, we find antiquity and the present united as one. You have been able to extol this point by point…”

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
蓋涵濡有得者他日服官政必其推廣此心者耶
同考試官教諭曾批
聖人之德莫大教民生民二端此作紬繹問目而敷演成章有養之士
也錄之以風天下
考試官教諭黃批
聖朝滋培
國脉全在於此子也仰窺而極賛其盛是得於久道之化者
考試官學正宋批敷對詳明獨見此篇
聖人之御天下無所不用其仁其敷教也
===
所以奠民性也其恤刑也所以壽民生也
天之生人若有恒性未甞不欲其奠麗天
地之大德曰生又何甞不欲斯民之壽且
孳也天何言哉聖人者出體天之心法天
之令建中正以為極本彝倫以為教感之
休之蒸蒸向乂以完其天終身游泳俾勿
壞焉書曰天佑下民作之君作之師惟其
克相上帝寵綏四方是也聖人南面而治
章善癉惡整齊人道刑固不廢然哀矜懲
punctuated:
蓋涵濡有得者，他日服官政，必其推廣此心者耶？
同考試官教諭曾批：聖人之德，莫大教民、生民二端。此作紬繹問目，而敷演成章，有養之士也。錄之以風天下。
考試官教諭黃批：聖朝滋培國脉，全在於此。子也仰窺而極賛其盛，是得於久道之化者。
考試官學正宋批：敷對詳明，獨見此篇。
聖人之御天下，無所不用其仁。其敷教也，所以奠民性也；其恤刑也，所以壽民生也。天之生人，若有恒性，未甞不欲其奠麗。天地之大德曰生，又何甞不欲斯民之壽且孳也？天何言哉？聖人者出，體天之心，法天之令，建中正以為極，本彝倫以為教，感之休之，蒸蒸向乂，以完其天。終身游泳，俾勿壞焉。《書》曰：「天佑下民，作之君，作之師，惟其克相上帝，寵綏四方。」是也。聖人南面而治，章善癉惡，整齊人道，刑固不廢，然哀矜懲
translation_en:
…Surely one who has gained something from being steeped in these influences will, when he takes office in the future, extend this same benevolent concern, will he not?
Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor: Of the sage’s virtues, none surpasses these two: educating the people and sustaining their lives. This composition draws out the strands of the question and develops them into a coherent essay. Its author is a man of cultivated character. We record it to set an example for all under Heaven.
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: The flourishing dynasty’s nourishment of the state’s vital strength rests entirely upon this. You have looked reverently upward and praised its magnificence to the utmost; you have benefited from the transforming influence of a way long maintained.
Comment by Examiner Song, School Director: Only in this essay have I seen a response so thorough and clear.
In governing all under Heaven, the sage applies his benevolence everywhere. His dissemination of instruction serves to give stability to the people’s moral nature; his solicitude in administering punishments serves to prolong their lives. When Heaven brings human beings into existence, they seemingly possess a constant moral nature [?], and Heaven invariably desires that it be securely established. The great virtue of Heaven and Earth is called life: when have they ever not desired that these people should live long and multiply? Yet what does Heaven say? The sage comes forth, embodies Heaven’s intentions, and models himself upon Heaven’s commands. He establishes centrality and rectitude as the highest standard and bases his teaching upon the enduring human relationships. He moves and nurtures the people, so that they advance steadily toward good order and preserve intact their Heaven-given nature. Throughout their lives they remain immersed in this teaching, so that their nature is not impaired. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven aids the people below, making rulers for them and teachers for them, that they may assist the Lord on High in cherishing and bringing peace to the four quarters.” This is what it means. The sage faces south and governs, commending goodness and condemning wickedness, bringing order to human conduct. Punishments certainly are not abolished; yet, with pity and compassion, he seeks to deter…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
創不盡法以為刑俾之知所顧避回翔倫
理以全其生易曰聖人以順動則刑罰清
而民服是也彼堯舜之仁天下豈無所用
其心哉洪荒之時彝倫未叙天下之生乆
矣乃急急焉命契為司徒敬敷五教民始
知方又命臯陶為士師明刑以弼之民始
知法又繼之曰欽哉欽哉惟刑之恤哉若
不樂於用刑聖人之意可識矣故當時之
民不見威福心志不揺日用飲食怡然相
===
安於垂裳之盛忘堯舜之刑而歌堯舜之
仁天下之情可想矣故稱聖人之至者必
曰堯舜而稱仁壽之極者亦必曰堯舜帝
典在焉固賛天行仁之準也巍巍蕩蕩不
可尚已迄周以降脩短代殊仁厚立國者
未免禮樂之讓文學飾治者祗矜縱囚之
歸堯舜之澤乆不曁已仰體天地之德弘
開唐虞之治其惟我
太祖與我
punctuated: 創，不盡法以為刑，俾之知所顧避，回翔倫理，以全其生。《易》曰：「聖人以順動，則刑罰清而民服。」是也。彼堯舜之仁天下，豈無所用其心哉？洪荒之時，彝倫未叙，天下之生乆矣，乃急急焉命契為司徒，敬敷五教，民始知方；又命臯陶為士師，明刑以弼之，民始知法；又繼之曰：「欽哉！欽哉！惟刑之恤哉！」若不樂於用刑，聖人之意可識矣。故當時之民，不見威福，心志不揺，日用飲食，怡然相安於垂裳之盛，忘堯舜之刑，而歌堯舜之仁，天下之情可想矣。故稱聖人之至者必曰堯舜，而稱仁壽之極者亦必曰堯舜。《帝典》在焉，固賛天行仁之準也。巍巍蕩蕩，不可尚已！迄周以降，脩短代殊，仁厚立國者未免禮樂之讓，文學飾治者祗矜縱囚之歸，堯舜之澤乆不曁已。仰體天地之德，弘開唐虞之治，其惟我太祖與我
translation_en:
…to chasten them, they did not punish to the full extent of the law, but enabled people to know what to heed and avoid, to move within proper moral relationships, and thereby to preserve their lives. The Book of Changes says: “When the sage acts in accordance with what is right, punishments are clear and the people submit.” This is what it means. In extending benevolence throughout the realm, surely Yao and Shun applied their minds to this purpose! In the primeval age, the constant moral relationships had not yet been ordered, although people had long lived in the world. They therefore urgently appointed Xie as Minister of Education to reverently disseminate the five teachings; only then did the people know the proper direction. They also appointed Gao Yao as Chief Judge to clarify punishments in support of those teachings; only then did the people know the law. They followed this with the injunction: “Be reverent! Be reverent! Be solicitous in the use of punishments!” They seemed to take no pleasure in imposing punishments: the sages’ intention can thus be understood. Accordingly, the people of that time perceived no exercise of punitive or rewarding power, and their hearts and purposes remained unshaken. In their daily lives, eating and drinking, they lived happily and peacefully together amid the flourishing order of rulers who merely let their robes hang down. They forgot Yao and Shun’s punishments and sang of their benevolence. We can imagine the feelings of all under Heaven.

Thus, anyone speaking of the utmost perfection of sages invariably names Yao and Shun; anyone speaking of the highest attainment of benevolence and longevity likewise invariably names Yao and Shun. The Canons of the Emperors remain, assuredly providing a standard for assisting Heaven and practicing benevolence. How lofty and all-encompassing—nothing could surpass them! From the Zhou onward, dynasties differed in their duration. Those who founded their states upon benevolence and generosity still incurred reproach concerning rites and music; those who embellished their governance with literary learning merely boasted that released prisoners returned. The beneficence of Yao and Shun has long ceased to reach the people. Reverently embodying the virtue of Heaven and Earth and restoring on a grand scale the governance of Tang and Yu—surely this belongs to our Taizu and our …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
皇上乎我
太祖高皇帝
聰明睿智
文武聖神
天厭胡元眷之
明命迅掃腥羶之毒穢大啓土宇於版章草昧
之初忿疾於頑特製
大誥三編與民更始申明五常甚惓惓焉必有
藏讀者罪得減等蓋出之干衽滌以文德
===
家傳人誦用夏變夷仁之至也及天下大
定又著
祖訓一書禁後世不用墨劓剕宮之刑歷六年
七謄藁乃獲告成
貽謀之慮遠矣此皆
聖心之獨斷臣下不得而窺者也二百年來莊
誦佩服莫不惴惴聳敬如對越
陟降之靈顧今
深仁厚澤怙冒寰區人心聯結
punctuated:
皇上乎？我太祖高皇帝，聰明睿智，文武聖神。天厭胡元，眷之明命，迅掃腥羶之毒穢，大啓土宇於版章。草昧之初，忿疾於頑，特製《大誥》三編，與民更始，申明五常，甚惓惓焉。必有藏讀者，罪得減等。蓋出之干衽，滌以文德，家傳人誦，用夏變夷，仁之至也。
及天下大定，又著《祖訓》一書，禁後世不用墨、劓、剕、宮之刑。歷六年，七謄藁，乃獲告成。貽謀之慮遠矣！此皆聖心之獨斷，臣下不得而窺者也。二百年來，莊誦佩服，莫不惴惴聳敬，如對越陟降之靈。顧今深仁厚澤，怙冒寰區，人心聯結。
translation_en:
…His Majesty? Our Emperor Taizu Gao was intelligent and discerning, wise and sagacious, accomplished in civil and military affairs, sage and divine. Heaven, having grown weary of the alien Yuan, favored him with its illustrious mandate. He swiftly swept away their rank and noisome corruption and greatly expanded the territory entered in the registers [?]. In the unsettled beginnings, indignant at the obstinate, he specially composed the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Da Gao), making a fresh start together with the people and most earnestly reaffirming the Five Constant Virtues. Those who possessed and read this work were entitled to a reduction in the degree of punishment for their offenses. Thus he brought them out of their former condition [?] and cleansed them through civil virtue. Transmitted in every household and recited by everyone, it transformed the alien through Chinese civilization: this was benevolence in its highest form.
Once all under Heaven was firmly pacified, he also composed the Ancestral Instructions (Zu Xun), forbidding later generations to employ the punishments of tattooing, cutting off the nose, amputating the feet, and castration [?; the transcription contains an apparent double negative]. Only after six years and seven transcriptions of the draft was the work completed. How far-reaching was his concern in laying plans for his descendants! These were all decisions made independently in his sagely mind, beyond his servants’ ability to fathom. For two hundred years, people have solemnly recited and reverently observed these teachings, all trembling with awe as though standing before his spirit as it ascends and descends. Now profound benevolence and abundant favor shelter the whole realm, and the people’s hearts are bound together…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
國脉平康丕丕無疆之基引之勿替如明問
所及者不在茲歟至我
皇上以
上聖之資操制作之柄敬
天法
祖恭
已愛民
克孝克仁
盡倫盡制甫當踐祚即
===
命大小儒臣纂脩
明倫大典詞嚴義正裁自
宸衷伏睹
御製序曰王天下者皆本奉天命承宗祀立人
極建綱常作民之主未有舎是而外求諸道
以能化行四海澤被生民者也又曰上承乎
天奉宗祀於億萬斯年下勤乎民務盡君人
師長之道期於禮樂之興刑罰是中大哉
皇言炳如日月咸切人倫且內列歷代授次後
punctuated: 國脉平康，丕丕無疆之基，引之勿替，如明問所及者，不在茲歟？至我皇上，以上聖之資，操制作之柄，敬天法祖，恭已愛民，克孝克仁，盡倫盡制。甫當踐祚，即命大小儒臣纂脩《明倫大典》，詞嚴義正，裁自宸衷。伏睹御製序曰：「王天下者，皆本奉天命、承宗祀、立人極、建綱常，作民之主，未有舎是而外求諸道，以能化行四海、澤被生民者也。」又曰：「上承乎天，奉宗祀於億萬斯年；下勤乎民，務盡君人師長之道，期於禮樂之興，刑罰是中。」大哉皇言！炳如日月，咸切人倫。且內列歷代授次，後
translation_en:
…the vital strength of the state is tranquil and sound. Is this not where the means lie to perpetuate, without decline, the ever-growing foundation of boundless rule to which your illuminating question refers? As for our Emperor, endowed with the qualities of the highest sage and wielding the authority to establish institutions, he reveres Heaven and follows his ancestors, conducts himself reverently and loves the people. He fulfills filial piety and benevolence, fully observes human relationships, and brings institutions to perfection. Upon ascending the throne, he immediately commanded scholarly officials of higher and lower rank to compile the Great Compendium Elucidating Human Relations (Minglun dadian). Its language is stern and its principles correct, determined by the imperial mind itself.
I have reverently read its imperially composed preface, which states: “Those who rule all under Heaven invariably take as their foundation the reverent acceptance of Heaven’s mandate, the continuation of ancestral sacrifices, the establishment of the highest standard of human conduct, and the institution of the cardinal bonds and constant norms, thus becoming masters of the people. Never has anyone abandoned these and sought some other Way, yet succeeded in extending moral transformation throughout the Four Seas and bringing beneficence to the living people.” It further states: “Above, receive Heaven’s mandate and maintain the ancestral sacrifices for countless millions of years; below, labor diligently for the people, striving to fulfill the Way of being their ruler, teacher, and leader, in the hope that rites and music will flourish and punishments attain their proper measure.” How great are these imperial words! They shine like the sun and moon, all bearing directly upon human relationships. Moreover, within the work are listed the successive dynasties’ orders of succession [?], and afterward …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
繋
本朝宗圖正閏分明統嗣章著舉世及之文義
情兼盡折人後之論邪正頓釐漢宋謬談
一洗而更新之矣是
典一布如日升暘谷普照迷方卽絕徼窮鄉亦
知引領皆曰
聖人之敎我也於是天下之人相率而趨於道
化父父子子兄兄弟弟各得其所敢有頑
冥不靈勿若于訓者乎頃
===
欲司牧臣工監于祥刑彰信兆民罔干和氣
仁言德意仰廑
綸綍伏睹
敕文曰司民牧者未盡得人或道理不明或律
法不通或任情以作威或深文以鍛獄甚或
貪賄聽囑顛倒是非不顧冤抑是何心歟又
曰省改前愆惟公惟愼盡心聽讞民以不冤
大哉
皇言霈如雲雨有裨民命且內揭古昔帝王及
punctuated:
繋本朝宗圖，正閏分明，統嗣章著。舉世及之文，義情兼盡；折人後之論，邪正頓釐。漢宋謬談，一洗而更新之矣。是典一布，如日升暘谷，普照迷方，卽絕徼窮鄉亦知引領，皆曰：「聖人之敎我也。」於是天下之人相率而趨於道化，父父子子，兄兄弟弟，各得其所，敢有頑冥不靈、勿若于訓者乎？
頃欲司牧臣工監于祥刑，彰信兆民，罔干和氣，仁言德意，仰廑綸綍。伏睹敕文曰：「司民牧者未盡得人，或道理不明，或律法不通，或任情以作威，或深文以鍛獄，甚或貪賄聽囑，顛倒是非，不顧冤抑，是何心歟？」又曰：「省改前愆，惟公惟愼，盡心聽讞，民以不冤。」大哉皇言！霈如雲雨，有裨民命。且內揭古昔帝王及
translation_en:
…appends the genealogical chart of our dynasty, clearly distinguishing legitimate from illegitimate succession and plainly setting out the imperial line of inheritance. It cites the wording concerning succession from father to son and from elder to younger brother, fully accommodating both principle and human feeling; it refutes the arguments concerning becoming another man's heir, immediately distinguishing error from what is right. The mistaken discussions of the Han and Song have thus been swept away and understanding renewed. Once this canon was promulgated, it was like the sun rising from Yanggu, illuminating every benighted quarter. Even in the remotest borderlands and poorest villages, people knew to crane their necks in anticipation, all saying: “This is the sage's instruction to us.” Thereupon the people throughout the realm led one another toward transformation through the Way. Fathers acted as fathers, sons as sons, elder brothers as elder brothers, and younger brothers as younger brothers, each fulfilling his proper role. Would any dare remain obstinate, ignorant, and unresponsive, refusing to follow these teachings?
Recently, wishing the officials charged with governing the people to take humane punishments as their guide, manifest their trustworthiness to the myriad people, and avoid disturbing harmonious qi, Your Majesty graciously expressed benevolent words and virtuous intentions in an imperial pronouncement. We reverently read in the edict: “Those charged with governing the people are not all suitable men. Some do not understand moral principles; some are unfamiliar with the laws. Some indulge their inclinations in wielding authority; some strain the wording of the law to fabricate criminal cases. Some even covet bribes and heed private solicitations, reversing right and wrong without regard for injustice and oppression. What manner of heart is this?” It further says: “Examine and correct your former faults. Be impartial and cautious, and devote yourselves wholeheartedly to hearing and adjudicating cases, so that the people suffer no injustice.” How great are the imperial words! Abundant as clouds and rain, they sustain the lives of the people. Moreover, the edict sets forth the examples of the emperors and kings of antiquity and…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
我
祖宗罔不慎重於刑遡極源委仁愛一心災沴
休祥互發以動其善念國法神譴交儆以
弭其非心俗吏舛錯一舉而震疊之矣是
勅一頒如大寒冱凍忽轉陽春卽昆蟲草木亦
知嚅跂皆曰
聖人之生我也於是天下之人相率而守其章
程强者弱者智者愚者人人寡其過敢有怙
終不悛勿迪于政者乎我
===
皇上之敷教卽
太祖之仁也亦天之心也有教則民性自奠性
旣奠則良心鼓舞義氣奮揚可以奠邦矣
皇上之恤刑卽
太祖之仁也亦天之心也無刑則民生自壽民
旣壽則衆心翼戴協氣自臻可以壽國矣
其始也錫庶民之極其究也斂天下之福
後先媲美照耀萬世堯舜之盛不是過也
而所係豈其微哉自今觀之
punctuated:
我祖宗罔不慎重於刑，遡極源委，仁愛一心。災沴休祥，互發以動其善念；國法神譴，交儆以弭其非心。俗吏舛錯，一舉而震疊之矣。是勅一頒，如大寒冱凍忽轉陽春，卽昆蟲草木亦知嚅跂，皆曰：「聖人之生我也！」於是天下之人相率而守其章程，强者、弱者、智者、愚者，人人寡其過，敢有怙終不悛、勿迪于政者乎？

我皇上之敷教，卽太祖之仁也，亦天之心也。有教則民性自奠，性旣奠則良心鼓舞，義氣奮揚，可以奠邦矣。皇上之恤刑，卽太祖之仁也，亦天之心也。無刑則民生自壽，民旣壽則衆心翼戴，協氣自臻，可以壽國矣。其始也，錫庶民之極；其究也，斂天下之福。後先媲美，照耀萬世，堯舜之盛不是過也。而所係豈其微哉？自今觀之
translation_en:
…our ancestral sovereigns, all of whom exercised caution and care in punishments. Tracing the matter fully to its source and ramifications, the decree expresses a single purpose of benevolence and love. Disasters and baleful portents, blessings and auspicious signs arise in turn to awaken officials’ good intentions; the laws of the state and divine condemnation jointly admonish them to quell their wrongful impulses. The errors of ordinary officials are thus checked at a single stroke. Once this edict was promulgated, it was as though the frozen depths of winter had suddenly turned to sunny spring. Even insects, plants, and trees knew to stir and stretch [?], all saying, “The sage has given us life!” Thereupon, people throughout the realm led one another in observing its regulations. Strong and weak, wise and foolish, all reduced their faults. Would any dare persist in wrongdoing without repentance and refuse to follow the government’s ordinances?

Our Emperor’s dissemination of instruction embodies the benevolence of Taizu and also the heart of Heaven. With instruction, the people’s moral nature naturally becomes settled. Once it is settled, their innate goodness is stirred and their spirit of righteousness rises, making it possible to secure the realm. The Emperor’s compassion in administering punishments embodies the benevolence of Taizu and also the heart of Heaven. When punishments cease, the people naturally enjoy long lives. When the people are long-lived, their hearts unite in supporting their sovereign, and harmony naturally ensues, making it possible to prolong the life of the state. At the outset, he bestows upon the common people the supreme standard; in the ultimate outcome, he gathers the blessings of all under Heaven. Successor and predecessor match one another in excellence, illuminating ten thousand generations. Even the flourishing reigns of Yao and Shun did not surpass this. Could what is at stake be insignificant? Viewed from this moment onward…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
好生之德洽於民心太和之氣充塞宇宙禎符
滋至景貺洊加
壽星現焉甘露零焉玄龜出焉白鹿呈焉芝草
挺焉醴泉湧焉惟
天監觀陰隲於沕穆之中惟
皇上時憲默運於陶鈞之上於萬斯年自今伊
始天下之人遭逢
聖世家興禮讓官無繁刑利涉而思禹功含哺
而懷稷粒又皆舉手加額同聲而祝
===
===
聖人之壽彌熾彌昌與
天無極永孚于休是
典也是
敕也帝典
祖訓今古竝傳則生長壽域胥教胥生者何可
紀極也猗歟盛哉治之至巳生也南海之
人未探
金匱石室之藏然涵濡
聖化畜積亦有日矣蠡測之見無補高深敬以
punctuated: 好生之德洽於民心，太和之氣充塞宇宙，禎符滋至，景貺洊加。壽星現焉，甘露零焉，玄龜出焉，白鹿呈焉，芝草挺焉，醴泉湧焉。惟天監觀，陰隲於沕穆之中；惟皇上時憲，默運於陶鈞之上。於萬斯年，自今伊始。天下之人遭逢聖世，家興禮讓，官無繁刑，利涉而思禹功，含哺而懷稷粒，又皆舉手加額，同聲而祝聖人之壽，彌熾彌昌，與天無極，永孚于休。是典也，是敕也，帝典祖訓，今古竝傳，則生長壽域、胥教胥生者，何可紀極也！猗歟盛哉，治之至巳！生也，南海之人，未探金匱石室之藏，然涵濡聖化，畜積亦有日矣。蠡測之見，無補高深，敬以
translation_en:
…The virtue of cherishing life has permeated the people’s hearts, and the breath of supreme harmony fills the universe. Auspicious signs arrive in increasing abundance, and great blessings are bestowed repeatedly. The Star of Longevity appears; sweet dew falls; a dark tortoise emerges; a white deer presents itself; numinous mushrooms spring up; and sweet springs gush forth. Heaven watches over all, secretly ordering things amid its profound mysteries; His Majesty takes Heaven as his model, silently exercising the power that shapes all things. May his reign endure for ten thousand years, beginning now.

The people of the realm, fortunate to encounter this sage age, cultivate ritual propriety and deference in their households, while officials impose no excessive punishments. Crossing the waters safely, they recall Yu’s achievements; with food in their mouths, they remember Ji’s gift of grain. All raise their hands to their foreheads and pray with one voice for the sage sovereign’s longevity: may he flourish and prosper ever more, boundless as Heaven, abiding forever in blessedness. This canon and this edict—the imperial canon and the ancestral instructions—are transmitted together across ancient and present times. How could one ever fully count those who, born and raised in this realm of longevity, are all instructed and all preserved in life? Ah, how glorious! Government has reached its highest perfection [?].

I, a student, am a man of Nanhai. I have not explored the collections preserved in golden coffers and stone chambers, yet I have long been steeped in the sage sovereign’s transforming influence and have accumulated some learning. My views, like measuring the sea with a gourd, contribute nothing to such loftiness and profundity. Respectfully, with…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一得之愚揄揚
今日之盛
第二問
何天衢
同考試官教諭童批經書之旨道同教殊古
今學者之準的是作發揮所以然處甚明非潛心
理學者不能也
同考試官教諭孫批聖賢因人施教學者由
教體道載在經書無不合□能闡明其義而末
===
復誦說程子之語以示窮經讀書之要能知所本
者
考試官教諭黃批發明殆盡
考試官學正宋批能知理學源委
聖人之道統於心者也其同而異者所以
為教也聖人之教求諸心者也其異而同
者所以為學也知其所以異而後可以論
學知其所以同而後可以體道譬之水焉
山下出泉無異源也由是之焉為澗為沚
punctuated:
一得之愚，揄揚今日之盛。
第二問
何天衢
同考試官教諭童批：經書之旨，道同教殊，古今學者之準的。是作發揮所以然處甚明，非潛心理學者不能也。
同考試官教諭孫批：聖賢因人施教，學者由教體道，載在經書，無不合□。能闡明其義，而末復誦說程子之語，以示窮經讀書之要，能知所本者。
考試官教諭黃批：發明殆盡。
考試官學正宋批：能知理學源委。
聖人之道，統於心者也；其同而異者，所以為教也。聖人之教，求諸心者也；其異而同者，所以為學也。知其所以異，而後可以論學；知其所以同，而後可以體道。譬之水焉，山下出泉，無異源也；由是之焉，為澗為沚，
translation_en:
…to offer my humble insight in praise of the splendor of the present age.
Second Policy Question
He Tianqu
Comment by Associate Examiner Tong, Instructor: The purport of the classics is that the Way is one, while teachings differ: this is the standard for scholars past and present. This composition explains very clearly why this is so. Only someone who has devoted himself to the Learning of Principle could accomplish this.
Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, Instructor: Sages and worthies adapt their teaching to the individual; learners embody the Way through that teaching. These principles are recorded in the classics, and all accord with □ [?]. This composition elucidates their meaning and, at the end, again cites and expounds Master Cheng’s words to show the essentials of thoroughly investigating the classics and reading books. Its author understands the foundation on which learning rests.
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: The exposition is nearly exhaustive.
Comment by Examiner Song, School Instructor: The author understands the origins and development of the Learning of Principle.
The Way of the sages is unified in the heart-mind; its differentiation from unity is what constitutes teaching. The teaching of the sages is to be sought within the heart-mind; its convergence from difference into unity is what constitutes learning. Only after understanding why it differs can one discuss learning; only after understanding why it is one can one embody the Way. Take water as an analogy. A spring issues from beneath a mountain, without any difference in its source. Proceeding from there, it becomes mountain streams and islets [?]…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
為江河其支流至衆也然莫非水之分也
是道之所以異教也及其歸也以江以河
浮于淮達于泗而皆放乎海焉是學之所
以同於道也又譬之往上都者或帆於水
或馳於陸及其止也無異致也故曰天下
之道殊塗而同歸百慮而一致嗚呼觀其
深矣稽之上古道原於天而備於人然惟
統會於聖人之一心故聖人者道之管也
堯以是傳之舜舜以是傳之禹禹以是傳
===
之湯湯以是傳之文王周公以及於孔子
無異道也一中之授受歷數聖人而不易
焉無異統也乃其因時以立教而垂之為
經著之為書斯其所指不同殆言人人殊
矣而其所以為道與所以造於道未甞異
也今以六經言之自孔子而上聖人達而
在上其道行其紀載聖人之言行有易書
詩禮春秋之為經皆所以載道也而教存
乎其中矣其同而異者也經解之言曰溫
punctuated:
為江河，其支流至衆也，然莫非水之分也。是道之所以異教也。及其歸也，以江以河，浮于淮，達于泗，而皆放乎海焉，是學之所以同於道也。又譬之往上都者，或帆於水，或馳於陸，及其止也，無異致也。故曰：「天下之道，殊塗而同歸，百慮而一致。」嗚呼，觀其深矣！稽之上古，道原於天而備於人，然惟統會於聖人之一心，故聖人者，道之管也。堯以是傳之舜，舜以是傳之禹，禹以是傳之湯，湯以是傳之文王、周公，以及於孔子，無異道也。一中之授受，歷數聖人而不易焉，無異統也。乃其因時以立教，而垂之為經，著之為書，斯其所指不同，殆言人人殊矣。而其所以為道與所以造於道，未甞異也。

今以六經言之，自孔子而上，聖人達而在上，其道行。其紀載聖人之言行，有易、書、詩、禮、春秋之為經，皆所以載道也，而教存乎其中矣，其同而異者也。經解之言曰：「溫
translation_en:
…forming great rivers, with exceedingly numerous tributaries; yet all are divisions of the same water. This is how the Way gives rise to differing teachings. When these waters reach their destination, flowing by the great rivers, floating upon the Huai and reaching the Si, they all discharge into the sea. This is how learning converges upon the Way. It is also like those traveling to the capital: some sail by water, while others hasten overland, but when they stop, their destination is the same. Thus it is said: “The paths under Heaven lead to the same destination by different routes; a hundred deliberations arrive at one result.” Ah, how profound this is to contemplate!

Examining high antiquity, we find that the Way originates in Heaven and is fully present in human beings, yet it is united and brought together only in the single mind of the sage. Thus the sage is the conduit of the Way. Yao transmitted this to Shun, Shun to Yu, Yu to Tang, and Tang to King Wen and the Duke of Zhou, and thence to Confucius: there was no different Way. The transmission and reception of the single Mean remained unchanged through successive sages: there was no different lineage of transmission. Yet when they established teachings suited to their times, handed them down as classics, and set them forth in writings, their purport differed, so that almost every person's words were distinct. Nevertheless, what constituted the Way and the means of attaining it never differed.

Now, speaking of the Six Classics: from Confucius back to earlier times, the sages attained eminence and occupied positions of authority, and their Way was put into practice. As records of the sages' words and deeds, there are the classics Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites, and Spring and Autumn Annals. All serve to convey the Way, and their teachings reside within them. These are instances of what is the same becoming different. The “Explanation of the Classics” says: “Gentle …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
良敦厚詩教也疏通知遠書教也廣博易
良樂教也潔淨精微易教也恭儉莊敬禮
教也屬辭比事春秋教也是故因性爲教
以著入國之義然其明六經之指要不可
易也稽之後儒則荀楊其辨矣荀卿氏曰
禮之敬文也樂之中和也詩書之博也春
秋之微也楊雄氏曰說天莫辨乎易說事
莫辨乎書說體莫辨乎禮說志莫辨乎詩
說理莫辨乎春秋固皆泝戴記之遺義也
===
然非二道也易之通變宜民亦書之政事
也書之降衷恒性亦詩之性情也中和且
平非禮樂之由興乎命德討罪非春秋之
微權乎故曰六經之道同歸實未嘗不相
爲用也雖有爲指之殊者道固本同也以
是而類推焉則所謂詩以道志書以道事
樂以道和易以道陰陽春秋以道名分者
莫非道也莫非聖人之所以爲教也是謂
聖人有異教而無異道孟子有曰夫道一
punctuated:
良敦厚，詩教也；疏通知遠，書教也；廣博易良，樂教也；潔淨精微，易教也；恭儉莊敬，禮教也；屬辭比事，春秋教也。」是故因性爲教，以著入國之義。然其明六經之指要，不可易也。稽之後儒，則荀、楊其辨矣。荀卿氏曰：「禮之敬文也，樂之中和也，詩書之博也，春秋之微也。」楊雄氏曰：「說天莫辨乎易，說事莫辨乎書，說體莫辨乎禮，說志莫辨乎詩，說理莫辨乎春秋。」固皆泝戴記之遺義也。
然非二道也。《易》之通變宜民，亦《書》之政事也；《書》之降衷恒性，亦《詩》之性情也。中和且平，非禮樂之由興乎？命德討罪，非《春秋》之微權乎？故曰：「六經之道同歸。」實未嘗不相爲用也。雖有爲指之殊者，道固本同也。以是而類推焉，則所謂詩以道志，書以道事，樂以道和，易以道陰陽，春秋以道名分者，莫非道也，莫非聖人之所以爲教也。是謂聖人有異教而無異道。孟子有曰：「夫道一
translation_en:
…goodness, sincerity, and generosity are the teaching of the Odes; breadth of understanding and knowledge of distant matters are the teaching of the Documents; breadth of learning, ease, and goodness are the teaching of Music; purity and subtle discernment are the teaching of the Changes; respectfulness, frugality, dignity, and reverence are the teaching of Rites; arranging words and comparing events are the teaching of the Spring and Autumn Annals.” Thus teaching accords with people's dispositions, making clear the meaning of the passage about entering a state. Yet this explanation of the essential purport of the Six Classics cannot be altered. Looking to later Confucians, Xun and Yang distinguished these matters clearly. Master Xun Qing said: “In Rites there are reverence and cultured forms; in Music, balance and harmony; in the Odes and Documents, breadth; in the Spring and Autumn Annals, subtlety.” Master Yang Xiong said: “For explaining Heaven, nothing is more discerning than the Changes; for explaining affairs, nothing is more discerning than the Documents; for explaining proper forms, nothing is more discerning than Rites; for explaining aspirations, nothing is more discerning than the Odes; for explaining principles, nothing is more discerning than the Spring and Autumn Annals.” All these statements indeed trace back to the meanings handed down in Dai's Record of Rites.
Yet these are not two different Ways. The Changes' adaptation to changing circumstances for the people's benefit is also the governmental business of the Documents; the Documents' account of Heaven's bestowal of moral goodness and the constant human nature is also the account of human nature and feelings in the Odes. Are balance, harmony, and peace not the source from which rites and music arise? Are appointing the virtuous and punishing the guilty not the subtle weighing of circumstances found in the Spring and Autumn Annals? Hence it is said: “The Ways of the Six Classics converge upon the same end.” Indeed, they have always served one another in their application. Although their purports differ, the Way is fundamentally the same. Extending this reasoning by analogy, the statements that the Odes express aspirations, the Documents recount affairs, Music expresses harmony, the Changes expound yin and yang, and the Spring and Autumn Annals explain distinctions of status all concern the Way; all are means by which the sages teach. This is what is meant by saying that the sages have differing teachings but no differing Ways. Mencius said: “The Way is one…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而已矣誠然哉見道之言與以四書言之
自孔子而下聖賢窮而在下其道明其傳
述師弟子之問答有論語大學中庸孟子
之爲書皆所以爲教也而學存乎其中矣
其異而同者也朱子之言曰論語之言莫
非操存涵養之要七篇之旨類多體驗擴
充之功不先乎大學無以盡論孟之精微
不參之論孟無以極中庸之歸趣不會其
極於中庸無以建立大本而經綸天下之
===
大經是雖標別次第以示積德之基然其
明四書之指要不可易也考之聖門則其
說焉詳矣論語專言爲仁直指人心之原
七篇並詳仁義兼統立人之道大學始教
以誠意爲自脩之道明德新民之端也中
庸體道由明誠愼獨以造於篤恭聖神功
化之極也固不外乎朱子之達論也然非
二致也無適無莫未始不言義也強恕求
仁固亦專言仁也誠意爲功而格致先之
punctuated:
而已矣。」誠然哉，見道之言與！以四書言之，自孔子而下，聖賢窮而在下，其道明，其傳述師弟子之問答，有《論語》《大學》《中庸》《孟子》之爲書，皆所以爲教也，而學存乎其中矣。其異而同者也。朱子之言曰：「《論語》之言，莫非操存涵養之要；七篇之旨，類多體驗擴充之功。不先乎《大學》，無以盡《論》《孟》之精微；不參之《論》《孟》，無以極《中庸》之歸趣；不會其極於《中庸》，無以建立大本而經綸天下之大經。」是雖標別次第以示積德之基，然其明四書之指要，不可易也。

考之聖門，則其說焉詳矣。《論語》專言爲仁，直指人心之原；七篇並詳仁義，兼統立人之道。《大學》始教，以誠意爲自脩之道，明德新民之端也。《中庸》體道，由明誠、愼獨以造於篤恭，聖神功化之極也。固不外乎朱子之達論也。然非二致也。無適無莫，未始不言義也；強恕求仁，固亦專言仁也。誠意爲功，而格致先之
translation_en:
…and that is all.” How true! These are surely words that reveal an understanding of the Way! Speaking of the Four Books: from Confucius onward, sages and worthies, constrained by circumstances and occupying humble positions, made their Way clear. Their transmitted teachings and records of questions and answers between masters and disciples took the form of such books as the Analects, the Great Learning, the Doctrine of the Mean, and the Mencius. All served as means of teaching, and learning was contained within them. They differ, yet are one. Master Zhu said: “Everything said in the Analects concerns the essentials of preserving the mind and nurturing its moral capacities; the purport of the seven books of the Mencius largely concerns the work of realizing these capacities in experience and extending them. Unless one begins with the Great Learning, one cannot fully comprehend the subtleties of the Analects and the Mencius. Unless one consults the Analects and the Mencius, one cannot fully grasp the ultimate meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean. Unless one brings these teachings together at their culmination in the Doctrine of the Mean, one cannot establish the great foundation and order the great governing principles of all under Heaven.” Although this distinguishes a sequence of study to show the basis for accumulating virtue, its elucidation of the essential purport of the Four Books admits of no alteration.

If we examine the teachings of the sage’s school, this account becomes clear in detail. The Analects speaks particularly of practicing benevolence, pointing directly to the source of the human mind. The seven books of the Mencius elaborate both benevolence and righteousness, together encompassing the Way by which one establishes oneself as a human being. The Great Learning provides the initial teaching: it takes making the intentions sincere as the way to cultivate oneself, the starting point for manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people. The Doctrine of the Mean embodies the Way: through understanding and sincerity, and vigilance when alone, one reaches profound reverence—the culmination of the transformative efficacy of sagely and spiritual attainment. These teachings indeed fall within Master Zhu’s comprehensive account. Yet they do not lead to different ends. To have neither fixed preferences nor fixed refusals is also to speak of righteousness; to strive at sympathetic consideration for others in seeking benevolence is indeed to speak particularly of benevolence. Making the intentions sincere is the work to be accomplished, but investigating things and extending knowledge precede it…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
矣是亦明善也知幾入門而敬信繼之矣
是亦誠意也故曰及其成功一也實未嘗
不統于同也間有立言之別者敎之或異
也以是而引伸焉則所謂終始之事中和
之致博約之誨存養之說者莫非敎也莫
非學者之所以造於道也是謂聖人有異
敎而無異學子夏有曰君子學以致其道
誠然哉造道之言與斯義也萬古一道千
聖一心故其道本同而所以異者因時之
===
敎也不害其爲同其敎雖異而所以同者
造道之歸也無病於其異此經書之要準
而爲學之不可不審者也自夫仲尼沒而
異端起九師興而易道微三傳作而春秋
散齊魯毛韓詩之末也大戴小戴禮之衰
也書殘于古今詩失于齊魯至於家語齊
論間見雜出大學中庸混編戴記孟氏之
好辯當其時且訾焉而聖人之道之敎幾
乎晦矣宋儒類出表章而發明之然後經
punctuated:
矣，是亦明善也。知幾入門，而敬信繼之矣，是亦誠意也。故曰：「及其成功，一也。」實未嘗不統于同也。間有立言之別者，敎之或異也。以是而引伸焉，則所謂終始之事、中和之致、博約之誨、存養之說者，莫非敎也，莫非學者之所以造於道也。是謂聖人有異敎而無異學。子夏有曰：「君子學以致其道。」誠然哉，造道之言與！斯義也，萬古一道，千聖一心，故其道本同，而所以異者，因時之敎也，不害其爲同；其敎雖異，而所以同者，造道之歸也，無病於其異。此經書之要準，而爲學之不可不審者也。
自夫仲尼沒而異端起，九師興而易道微，三傳作而春秋散。齊魯毛韓，詩之末也；大戴小戴，禮之衰也。書殘于古今，詩失于齊魯。至於家語齊論，間見雜出，大學中庸混編戴記，孟氏之好辯，當其時且訾焉，而聖人之道之敎幾乎晦矣。宋儒類出，表章而發明之，然後經
translation_en:
…This, too, is understanding goodness. Discerning the incipient signs provides entry, and reverence and trust follow: this, too, is making the intentions sincere. Thus it is said: “When success is achieved, it is one and the same.” These approaches have, in truth, always converged in unity. Occasional differences in formulation arise from differences in teaching. Extending this reasoning, the so-called affairs of beginning and end, the attainment of equilibrium and harmony, the instruction in broad learning and restraint, and the teachings on preserving and nourishing the mind are all teaching; all are means by which learners attain the Way. This is what is meant by saying that the sages have different teachings but no different learning. Zixia said: “The gentleman learns in order to realize his Way.” How true these words about attaining the Way! According to this principle, throughout all ages there is one Way, and the thousand sages share one mind. Thus their Way is fundamentally the same; what differs is teaching adapted to the times, which does not compromise that sameness. Although their teachings differ, what unites them is their ultimate purpose of attaining the Way, so their differences present no obstacle. This is the essential standard of the classics, which those who pursue learning must examine carefully.
After Zhongni died, heterodox doctrines arose; when the Nine Masters flourished, the Way of the Changes grew obscure; when the Three Commentaries were composed, the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals became fragmented. The Qi, Lu, Mao, and Han traditions represent the decline of the Odes; the Elder Dai and Younger Dai traditions represent the waning of ritual learning. The Documents became fragmentary in its ancient- and modern-script traditions, and the Odes suffered losses in the Qi and Lu traditions. As for the Family Sayings and the Qi Analects, they appeared intermittently in a confusing profusion. The Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean were compiled indiscriminately among the records of Dai. Mengzi’s fondness for disputation was criticized even in his own day, and the teaching of the sages’ Way was almost obscured. The Confucian scholars of the Song arose in succession, brought it to prominence, and elucidated it. Only then did the classics…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
書之蘊奧可悉得而聞其功非眇小也然
異同之辨儒先率多致意而原異求同必
達於道斯可與論學也是故以溫公之篤
信而有疑孟之作董槐之學本於輔廣而
欲重定知止之條以復於大學古本不可
謂無志於道然惟大儒朱子之說至今不
能易焉故爲得統於濂洛而上遡於周孔
其道同也後之君子明斯道之大原而求
之心不惑異說而妄自置門戶焉斯於道
===
思過半矣程子曰讀書者當觀聖人所以
作經之意與聖人所以用心聖人之所以
至於聖人而吾之所以未至所以未得者
誦味而思之平其心易其氣闕其疑則聖
人之意可見矣嗚呼知言哉
第三問
馬象乾
同考試官教諭翟批敘事中見論議是善說
古人者且備極底裏如身處其時可以爲文矣
punctuated:
書之蘊奧，可悉得而聞，其功非眇小也。然異同之辨，儒先率多致意，而原異求同，必達於道，斯可與論學也。是故以溫公之篤信，而有疑孟之作；董槐之學本於輔廣，而欲重定知止之條，以復於大學古本。不可謂無志於道，然惟大儒朱子之說，至今不能易焉。故爲得統於濂洛，而上遡於周孔，其道同也。後之君子明斯道之大原而求之心，不惑異說而妄自置門戶焉，斯於道思過半矣。程子曰：「讀書者當觀聖人所以作經之意，與聖人所以用心，聖人之所以至於聖人，而吾之所以未至、所以未得者，誦味而思之，平其心，易其氣，闕其疑，則聖人之意可見矣。」嗚呼，知言哉！

第三問
馬象乾
同考試官教諭翟批：敘事中見論議，是善說古人者。且備極底裏，如身處其時，可以爲文矣。
translation_en:
…the profound mysteries of the canonical writings could be fully apprehended and understood. Their achievement was no small one. Earlier Confucian scholars generally devoted much attention to distinguishing differences and agreements; yet only those who trace differences to their sources and seek what is shared, thereby attaining an understanding of the Way, can be engaged in a discussion of learning. Thus, despite Duke Wen’s deep conviction, he composed Doubts about Mencius; and Dong Huai, whose learning was grounded in that of Fu Guang, wished to rearrange the passages on knowing where to stop, restoring the Great Learning to its ancient text. They cannot be said to have lacked commitment to the Way. Nevertheless, the explanations of the great Confucian master Zhu Xi remain unalterable to this day. This is because he inherited the tradition of the masters of Lian and Luo, tracing it back to the Duke of Zhou and Confucius: their Way was the same. If later gentlemen understand the great source of this Way and seek it in their own hearts, without being misled by divergent doctrines into arbitrarily establishing schools of their own, they will already have progressed more than halfway in their reflection upon the Way. Master Cheng said: “Readers should consider the intentions for which the sages composed the classics, how the sages applied their minds, how they attained sagehood, and why we ourselves have not yet attained it or grasped it. Recite these writings, savor them, and reflect upon them; calm the heart, ease the temper, and leave doubtful matters unresolved. Then the sages’ intentions can be discerned.” Ah, how discerning these words are!

Third Question
Ma Xiangqian
Associate Examiner Zhai, Instructor, comments: “Argument emerges within the narration: this is someone skilled at discussing the ancients. Moreover, he explores the underlying circumstances thoroughly, as though he himself had lived in that age. He can indeed compose an essay!”

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭黃批敍論詳當
考試官學正宋批其事核其文贍
君子之所以表裏人物而尚論其世者其
道何以哉是故嚴於名實之辨者可以徵
用矣審於利鈍之故者可以觀時矣達於
運數之歸者可以語勢矣著於微漸之致
者可以燭幾矣是故用之不孚其名不足
稱也時之未遇其成不可必也運之所屈
其業不可冀也幾之所著其漸不可長也
===
以是博觀往行則權稱度量其有爽乎語
曰前事之不忘後事之師鑒也乃學者論
世尚友折衷爲要矣試於明問所及陳其
臆說焉夫邃古之初人懷敦行三代之際
咸茂令猷聖賢輩出仁義燁如也春秋而
降淳風散而物僞滋用舍殊而操行判得
失是非之辨君子以爲先務焉是故飯牛
車下扣角而歌甯戚之在齊誠賤士也桓
公感於堯舜在念之深慨而舉加上位於
punctuated:
考試官敎諭黃批：敍論詳當。
考試官學正宋批：其事核，其文贍。
君子之所以表裏人物而尚論其世者，其道何以哉？是故嚴於名實之辨者，可以徵用矣；審於利鈍之故者，可以觀時矣；達於運數之歸者，可以語勢矣；著於微漸之致者，可以燭幾矣。是故用之不孚，其名不足稱也；時之未遇，其成不可必也；運之所屈，其業不可冀也；幾之所著，其漸不可長也。以是博觀往行，則權稱度量，其有爽乎？語曰：「前事之不忘，後事之師鑒也。」乃學者論世尚友，折衷爲要矣。試於明問所及，陳其臆說焉。
夫邃古之初，人懷敦行；三代之際，咸茂令猷。聖賢輩出，仁義燁如也。春秋而降，淳風散而物僞滋，用舍殊而操行判，得失是非之辨，君子以爲先務焉。是故飯牛車下，扣角而歌，甯戚之在齊，誠賤士也。桓公感於堯舜在念之深慨，而舉加上位，於
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Huang, an Instructor (jiaoyu): The narration and argument are detailed and apt.
Comment by Examiner Song, an Instructor (xuezheng): Its facts are accurate, and its prose is ample.
By what method does the gentleman examine people outwardly and inwardly and reach back to discuss their age? Thus, one who rigorously distinguishes reputation from reality can assess fitness for employment; one who scrutinizes the causes of success and setback can discern the times; one who understands the course of fortune can discuss the configuration of circumstances; and one who clearly perceives the workings of subtle, gradual developments can illuminate the first signs of change. Thus, if a man's performance in office does not substantiate his reputation, that reputation does not merit praise. If his time has not come, his success cannot be assured. If fortune constrains him, his achievements cannot be hoped for. Where incipient signs become apparent, their gradual development must not be allowed to grow. If we use these principles to survey past conduct broadly, could our weighing and measuring go astray? As the saying goes, “Past events, if not forgotten, serve as teachers and mirrors for what follows.” Thus, for scholars who discuss past ages and seek friendship with the ancients, arriving at a balanced judgment is essential. Let me venture to present my own views on the matters raised in your discerning question.
In remote antiquity, people cherished sincere conduct; during the Three Dynasties, admirable principles flourished everywhere. Sages and worthies emerged in succession, and benevolence and righteousness shone brilliantly. From the Spring and Autumn period onward, unspoiled customs dispersed and deceit multiplied. Decisions to employ or reject men diverged, and their moral conduct became divided. The gentleman therefore regarded distinguishing gain from loss and right from wrong as his first task. Thus Ning Qi, feeding oxen beneath a cart and singing as he tapped their horns, was indeed a man of lowly station in Qi. Duke Huan was moved by the profound ardor with which he held Yao and Shun in his thoughts, and raised him to high office. Thereupon …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
是取威定霸一匡之烈亦與有力焉則誠
有其具國所利賴也豈以貧賤而有所遺
乎行雜市廛駔儈爲業段干木之在魏固
薄計也文侯仰其踰垣以避之高操而過
廬必式於是賢士歸心三晉之國天下莫
强焉則偃息藩魏仁賢之致也豈以隱逸
而無所賴乎晉之殷浩人以素望歸之至
謂深源未起如蒼生何殆與安石埒名矣
乃山桑之役遂至無功虛名之無益於用
===
也庾翼有言曰王夷甫立名非真實長華
競此輩宜束之高閣其已深中其匿與唐
之房琯帝每虛心待之琯且辭情慷慨以
天下爲己任庶幾李泌流亞矣乃陳濤斜
之戰遂至不支泥古之無效於時也賀蘭
進明有言曰迂闊大言引用浮黨真王衍
之比其蓋深得其情與孔明三代遺才師
若時雨乃渭濵之屯屈辱司馬握筭勝矣
顧終成鼎立之業者以所敵吳魏咸得其
punctuated: 是取威定霸，一匡之烈亦與有力焉，則誠有其具，國所利賴也，豈以貧賤而有所遺乎？行雜市廛，駔儈爲業，段干木之在魏固薄計也。文侯仰其踰垣以避之高操，而過廬必式。於是賢士歸心，三晉之國天下莫强焉，則偃息藩魏，仁賢之致也，豈以隱逸而無所賴乎？晉之殷浩，人以素望歸之，至謂「深源未起，如蒼生何」，殆與安石埒名矣。乃山桑之役，遂至無功，虛名之無益於用也。庾翼有言曰：「王夷甫立名非真實，長華競，此輩宜束之高閣。」其已深中其匿與？唐之房琯，帝每虛心待之，琯且辭情慷慨，以天下爲己任，庶幾李泌流亞矣。乃陳濤斜之戰，遂至不支，泥古之無效於時也。賀蘭進明有言曰：「迂闊大言，引用浮黨，真王衍之比。」其蓋深得其情與？孔明，三代遺才，師若時雨，乃渭濵之屯，屈辱司馬，握筭勝矣。顧終成鼎立之業者，以所敵吳魏咸得其
translation_en:
…thereupon he established his authority and secured his hegemony; Ning Qi, too, contributed to the achievement of bringing the realm into unity. He truly possessed the requisite abilities, from which the state benefited and on which it depended. How could poverty and low status justify passing him over?

Mingling among the marketplaces and making his living as a broker, Duan Ganmu certainly pursued a humble livelihood in Wei. Marquis Wen admired the lofty integrity with which he climbed over a wall to avoid meeting him, and whenever he passed Duan’s dwelling, he invariably bowed against his carriage rail. Worthy men consequently gave him their allegiance, and among the states of the Three Jin, none under Heaven was stronger than Wei. That Duan could protect Wei while resting at ease was the effect of his benevolence and worthiness. How could his reclusion mean that he offered nothing on which the state could depend?

Yin Hao of the Jin commanded people’s allegiance through his established reputation. They even said, “If Shenyuan does not come forth to serve, what will become of the common people?” His fame nearly equalled that of Anshi. Yet in the campaign at Shansang he accomplished nothing: empty reputation was of no practical use. Yu Yi once said, “Wang Yifu’s reputation rests on nothing genuine; he encourages ostentation and rivalry [?]. Such men should be bundled away on a high shelf.” Had he not already penetrated deeply into Yin’s concealed failings [?]?

As for Fang Guan of the Tang, the emperor always received him with an open mind. Fang’s words and sentiments were impassioned, and he took responsibility for all under Heaven upon himself, almost ranking alongside Li Mi. Yet at the battle of Chentao Xie his forces could not hold out: rigid adherence to antiquity proved ineffective in his own times. Helan Jinming once said, “Impractical and given to grand talk, he promotes frivolous partisans—a true counterpart of Wang Yan.” Had he not thoroughly grasped Fang’s true character?

Kongming possessed talents handed down from the Three Dynasties, and his army was like timely rain. When encamped on the banks of the Wei, he humbled Sima and held the calculations for victory in his grasp. Yet his achievement ultimately extended only to establishing one of three contending powers, because his opponents, Wu and Wei, had both secured their…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
人也不然則天下奇才豈能深服乎仲達
耶魏公間氣所鍾自許智膽乃好水之戰
邀擊元昊戒約審矣顧終墮泥合之計者
由所遣福懌違其節制也不然則置勝負
度外豈不誠讓於范公耶淝水之師秦衆
八十萬臨之江左蓋甚危矣安石且從容
賭墅焉則久戰之兵不可屢逞遠鬭之勢
殆於弩末安其燭之審也卒之朱序一呼
遂以八萬兵勝之亦苻堅之驕盈易乘耳
===
景略猶存安豈能無虞乎澶淵之幸邊書
一夕屢至中外殊震駭矣萊公且驩呼飲
博焉則擊之使隻輪不返創之令百年無
事準其計之深也卒之利用受戒衹以十
萬幣却之亦親征之軍氣特振耳欽若不
出準豈得如意乎關羽大節蜀將之絕倫
也乘水而攻樊城威振華夏此興復漢室
之機也陸遜乃潜躡其後至麥城之困羽
遂殞其軀焉嗟乎是天未欲漢混一吳豫
punctuated: 人也。不然，則天下奇才，豈能深服乎仲達耶？魏公間氣所鍾，自許智膽，乃好水之戰，邀擊元昊，戒約審矣。顧終墮泥合之計者，由所遣福懌違其節制也。不然，則置勝負度外，豈不誠讓於范公耶？淝水之師，秦衆八十萬臨之，江左蓋甚危矣。安石且從容賭墅焉，則久戰之兵不可屢逞，遠鬭之勢殆於弩末，安其燭之審也。卒之朱序一呼，遂以八萬兵勝之，亦苻堅之驕盈易乘耳。景略猶存，安豈能無虞乎？澶淵之幸，邊書一夕屢至，中外殊震駭矣。萊公且驩呼飲博焉，則擊之使隻輪不返，創之令百年無事，準其計之深也。卒之利用受戒，衹以十萬幣却之，亦親征之軍氣特振耳。欽若不出，準豈得如意乎？關羽大節，蜀將之絕倫也。乘水而攻樊城，威振華夏，此興復漢室之機也。陸遜乃潜躡其後，至麥城之困，羽遂殞其軀焉。嗟乎！是天未欲漢混一吳豫
translation_en:
…men of ability. Otherwise, how could a man of extraordinary talent, unrivaled under Heaven, have been so thoroughly held in check by Zhongda?

The Duke of Wei, Han Qi, was endowed with exceptional gifts and prided himself on his intelligence and courage. At the battle of Haoshui, he laid careful plans and issued precise orders for intercepting Yuanhao. Yet his forces ultimately fell into the trap at Nihe because Fu and Yi, whom he had dispatched, disobeyed his commands. Otherwise, in putting considerations of victory and defeat out of his mind, would he truly have conceded superiority to Lord Fan?

In the campaign at the Fei River, eight hundred thousand troops of Qin advanced upon the lands south of the Yangzi, placing them in grave danger. Yet Anshi, Xie An, calmly wagered his villa on a game. He clearly discerned that troops worn down by prolonged warfare could not repeatedly exert their strength, and that an army fighting far from home was like a crossbow bolt nearing the end of its flight. In the end, a single shout from Zhu Xu enabled an army of eighty thousand to defeat them. This, too, was simply because Fu Jian’s arrogance and complacency were easily exploited. Had Jinglüe, Wang Meng, still been alive, could Xie An have remained free of anxiety?

During the imperial journey to Chanyuan, dispatches from the frontier arrived repeatedly in a single night, causing great alarm both at court and beyond. Yet the Duke of Lai, Kou Zhun, cheerfully drank and gambled. His plan was profound: strike the enemy so that not a single chariot wheel returned, and inflict such a wound that there would be no further trouble for a hundred years. In the end, Liyong, having received his instructions, secured their withdrawal with only a hundred thousand in tribute payments. This, too, was simply because the emperor’s personal leadership of the campaign had greatly raised the army’s morale. Had Qinruo not gone out [?], could Kou Zhun have obtained his wish?

In his steadfast commitment to principle, Guan Yu was without equal among the generals of Shu. Taking advantage of the floodwaters, he attacked Fancheng, and his might shook the Chinese realm. Here was an opportunity to restore the house of Han. But Lu Xun secretly advanced behind him; Guan Yu was trapped at Maicheng and lost his life. Alas! Heaven did not yet wish Han to unite Wu and Yu…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
故蔣濟之計行而董昭之筭得也孫權乃
曰蒙取關羽過於子敬以是而幸勝焉權
眞漢賊也哉岳飛精忠中興之元勳也屢
戰而抵朱僊鎭兀术喪膽此恢復垂成之
業也高宗以金牌班師至片紙付吏飛遂
報歿焉嗟乎是天未欲宋重復中原故書
生之諫聽而黃龍之會阻也或者乃曰將
在軍君命有所不受以是而規飛焉是豈
純臣之義也哉知者覩未然君子之達觀
===
也李沆日奏四方水旱盜賊蓋致憂勤警
戒之意焉王旦不之然也至於他日遲回
去就之間乃曰李文靖眞聖人也旦於是
乎始歎服矣旦固恐煩聖慮者沆之知微
知彰亦萬夫之望與愛君防其漸人臣之
遠慮也范仲淹欲寬晁仲約之罪蓋章祖
宗盛德之事焉富弼莫之省也至於他日
國門待命之際乃曰范六丈聖人也弼於
是乎始輸心矣弼固欲正軍法者淹之識
punctuated:
故蔣濟之計行，而董昭之筭得也。孫權乃曰：「蒙取關羽，過於子敬。」以是而幸勝焉，權眞漢賊也哉！岳飛精忠，中興之元勳也。屢戰而抵朱僊鎭，兀术喪膽，此恢復垂成之業也。高宗以金牌班師，至片紙付吏，飛遂報歿焉。嗟乎！是天未欲宋重復中原，故書生之諫聽，而黃龍之會阻也。或者乃曰：「將在軍，君命有所不受。」以是而規飛焉，是豈純臣之義也哉？
知者覩未然，君子之達觀也。李沆日奏四方水旱盜賊，蓋致憂勤警戒之意焉。王旦不之然也。至於他日遲回去就之間，乃曰：「李文靖眞聖人也。」旦於是乎始歎服矣。旦固恐煩聖慮者，沆之知微知彰，亦萬夫之望與！愛君防其漸，人臣之遠慮也。范仲淹欲寬晁仲約之罪，蓋章祖宗盛德之事焉。富弼莫之省也。至於他日國門待命之際，乃曰：「范六丈聖人也。」弼於是乎始輸心矣。弼固欲正軍法者，淹之識
translation_en:
…Thus Jiang Ji’s plan was put into effect, and Dong Zhao’s calculations proved successful. Sun Quan then said, “In capturing Guan Yu, Meng surpassed Zijing.” Taking this as grounds to rejoice in his victory, was Quan not truly a traitor to the Han! Yue Fei, utterly loyal, was a foremost contributor to the dynastic restoration. Through repeated battles he reached Zhuxian Town, striking terror into Wuzhu. The undertaking of recovering the lost territory was on the verge of success. Emperor Gaozong used gold command tablets to recall the army; eventually a mere slip of paper was handed to the judicial officials, and Fei met his death [?]. Alas! Heaven did not yet intend the Song to recover the Central Plain, so the scholar’s remonstrance was heeded and the meeting at Huanglong was thwarted. Some say, “When a general is in the field, there are commands from his ruler that he need not accept.” They use this to reproach Fei. But could such conduct accord with the duty of a wholly loyal minister?
The wise perceive what has not yet happened: this is the gentleman’s penetrating vision. Li Hang reported daily on floods, droughts, bandits, and rebels throughout the realm, intending thereby to encourage anxious diligence and vigilance. Wang Dan disagreed with him. Later, when wavering between leaving office and remaining, he said, “Li Wenjing was truly a sage.” Only then did Dan begin to express his admiration and acknowledge him. Dan had indeed feared troubling the imperial mind; but was not Hang, who understood both the subtle and the manifest, a man to whom multitudes could look up? To love one’s ruler and guard against troubles in their beginnings is the far-reaching concern of a minister. Fan Zhongyan wished to mitigate Chao Zhongyue’s punishment, intending thereby to manifest the abundant virtue of the dynastic ancestors. Fu Bi did not understand this. Later, while awaiting orders at the capital’s gate, he said, “The venerable Fan, sixth in his family, is a sage.” Only then did Bi begin to yield his heartfelt assent. Bi had indeed wished to enforce military law; but Zhongyan’s discernment…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
微慮遠亦聖人之徒與是皆名實所由辨
時勢運數所由歸而先幾之遐覽也不可
不審也故嘗以是而合觀之甯叚之於齊
魏實浮於名也殷房之在晉唐名浮於實
也孔明稚圭其時之所為乎安石平仲其
殆審於勢乎關岳之困逢其運之厄也李
范之知炳於幾之先也是稽古之準也不
然則齊魏之賤士無左右之容名高遠遜
於浩琯而王寇之舉大非武侯魏公所可
===
希冀雲長固劣於呂蒙武穆為未盡其忠
而王富於二賢誠當訾其過慮也嗟乎此
天下所以多目論而難以語於賢豪之際
矣又嘗以是而類推之牛口之舉秦穆顯
名于天下五伯之達權也夫何讓於齊君
羊裘之訪世祖植節于東京帝王之遠慮
也又奚數乎魏主江左夷吾導固無愧於
素望顧任之審耳內相倚賴贄亦不虛其
重器誠不負於學耳鞠躬盡瘁成敗莫覩
punctuated:
微慮遠，亦聖人之徒與？是皆名實所由辨，時勢運數所由歸，而先幾之遐覽也，不可不審也。故嘗以是而合觀之：甯叚之於齊魏，實浮於名也；殷房之在晉唐，名浮於實也。孔明稚圭，其時之所為乎？安石平仲，其殆審於勢乎？關岳之困，逢其運之厄也；李范之知，炳於幾之先也。是稽古之準也。不然，則齊魏之賤士無左右之容，名高遠遜於浩琯，而王寇之舉大非武侯魏公所可希冀，雲長固劣於呂蒙，武穆為未盡其忠，而王富於二賢誠當訾其過慮也。嗟乎！此天下所以多目論，而難以語於賢豪之際矣。
又嘗以是而類推之：牛口之舉，秦穆顯名于天下，五伯之達權也，夫何讓於齊君？羊裘之訪，世祖植節于東京，帝王之遠慮也，又奚數乎魏主？江左夷吾，導固無愧於素望，顧任之審耳；內相倚賴，贄亦不虛其重器，誠不負於學耳。鞠躬盡瘁，成敗莫覩，
translation_en:
…perceiving the subtle and considering the distant consequences—was he not also a follower of the sages? These cases all show how reputation and actual merit are distinguished, how circumstances and fortune determine outcomes, and how foresight reaches beyond events before their first signs emerge. They must be examined carefully. Thus I have considered them together in this light: Ning Qi and Duan Ganmu, in Qi and Wei respectively, possessed merit exceeding their reputations; Yin Hao and Fang Guan, in Jin and Tang respectively, had reputations exceeding their merit. Were Kongming [Zhuge Liang] and Zhigui [Han Qi] products of their times? Were Anshi [Xie An] and Pingzhong [Kou Zhun] perhaps discerning judges of circumstances? Guan Yu and Yue Fei suffered because they encountered adversity in their allotted fortunes; Li Hang and Fan Zhongyan possessed understanding that shone forth before the first signs of events. These are the standards for examining antiquity. Otherwise, the humble men of Qi and Wei would find no acceptance among those attending their rulers, and their renown would fall far below that of Yin Hao and Fang Guan [?]; the accomplishments of Wang Dao and Kou Zhun would far surpass anything the Marquis of Wu [Zhuge Liang] and the Duke of Wei [Han Qi] could hope to attain; Yunchang [Guan Yu] would indeed be inferior to Lü Meng; Wumu [Yue Fei] would have failed to fulfill his loyalty; and Wang Dan and Fu Bi would certainly have been justified in criticizing those two worthy men [Li Hang and Fan Zhongyan] for excessive concern. Alas! This is why the world abounds in judgments based on appearances, and why it is difficult to discuss the distinctions among worthy and heroic men.
I have also extended this reasoning by analogy. By promoting a man from tending cattle [?], Duke Mu of Qin made his name illustrious throughout the realm: this was the adaptable judgment of one of the Five Hegemons. In what respect need he yield to the ruler of Qi? By seeking out the man in a sheepskin coat [Yan Guang], Emperor Shizu established moral integrity in the Eastern Han: this was an emperor’s far-reaching foresight. Why, then, make so much of the ruler of Wei? As the Guan Yiwu of the lands south of the Yangzi, Wang Dao certainly lived up to his established reputation; it was simply a matter of discernment in entrusting him with responsibility. Relied upon as an inner chief minister, Lu Zhi likewise justified his standing as a man fit for weighty responsibilities; truly, he did not betray his learning. Bending himself to his task and exhausting all his strength, without seeing whether it would end in success or failure…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
亮眞人龍也聲色不動兩宮晏然琦誠社
稷臣也以安之明違衆舉親而不免於絲
竹風流以準之才善斷大事而竟稱乎天
書鵓尾雲長之烈傲以取覆其偉不可及
也武穆之勳厄於垂成其忠不可掩也文
靖務抑浮薄斷斷兮古大臣之直亮矣文
正之先憂後樂其自任以天下之重乎旦
之薦準忘其短已擴然弘人之度也弼之
使虜竟定獻納偉然丈夫之節也君子達
===
觀而取節焉豈不誠然能尚論其世耶
第四問
葉夢熊
同考試官敎授秦批廉靖以持已惠利以及
民守令之賢無踰此二端是作悉數其事亦□當
世之慮者豈但記誦之文已耶
考試官敎諭黃批敘事有條理
考試官學正宋批推尊韓周二子是能知
德政本原者
punctuated:
亮眞人龍也。聲色不動，兩宮晏然，琦誠社稷臣也。以安之明，違衆舉親，而不免於絲竹風流；以準之才，善斷大事，而竟稱乎天書鵓尾。雲長之烈，傲以取覆，其偉不可及也；武穆之勳，厄於垂成，其忠不可掩也。文靖務抑浮薄，斷斷兮古大臣之直亮矣；文正之先憂後樂，其自任以天下之重乎！旦之薦準，忘其短已，擴然弘人之度也；弼之使虜，竟定獻納，偉然丈夫之節也。君子達觀而取節焉，豈不誠然能尚論其世耶？

第四問
葉夢熊

同考試官敎授秦批：廉靖以持已，惠利以及民，守令之賢無踰此二端。是作悉數其事，亦□當世之慮者，豈但記誦之文已耶？

考試官敎諭黃批：敘事有條理。

考試官學正宋批：推尊韓周二子，是能知德政本原者。
translation_en:
…Zhuge Liang was truly a dragon among men. His voice and expression unmoved, he kept both palaces at peace: Han Qi was indeed a minister who sustained the state. For all Xie An’s discernment in defying public opinion and recommending a kinsman, he could not escape an attachment to the refined pleasures of strings and pipes. For all Kou Zhun’s talent and skill in deciding great affairs, he nevertheless ended by praising the heavenly writings and the dove’s tail [?]. Guan Yunchang’s valor was brought to ruin by his arrogance, yet his greatness remains beyond reach. Wumu’s achievements were frustrated just as success approached, yet his loyalty cannot be obscured. Wenjing strove to restrain frivolity and superficiality: how steadfastly he embodied the integrity and sincerity of the great ministers of antiquity! Wenzheng worried before others and rejoiced after them: did he not take the weight of the realm upon himself? In recommending Kou Zhun, Wang Dan forgot that Kou had disparaged him, displaying the expansive generosity of a magnanimous man. On his mission to the northern enemy, Fu Bi finally settled the issue of “offering” and “remitting” tribute, displaying the imposing integrity of a true man. A gentleman takes a comprehensive view and selects what is worthy in their conduct. Is this not truly the ability to discuss the men of earlier times in light of their age?

Fourth Policy Question
Ye Mengxiong

Comment by Associate Examiner Qin, Prefectural School Professor: To conduct oneself with integrity and composure, and to extend kindness and benefits to the people—the excellence of prefects and magistrates consists above all in these two things. This essay recounts the relevant deeds in full and also [illegible] concerns about the present age [?]. How could it be merely a composition based on memorization and recitation?

Comment by Examiner Huang, County School Instructor: The account is logically ordered.

Comment by Examiner Song, Departmental School Instructor: By honoring the two masters Han and Zhou, the writer shows that he understands the foundations of virtuous government.

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
古之善爲治者其處巳也盡道然而廉靖
其本矣其處人也盡制然而惠利其先矣
能立其本則議道自巳而風化端能知先
務則置法以民而德施普是謂不求治於
人而求治於巳不求利於巳而求利於人
在當時而利賴之詠歌之故樹績也弘在
後世而傳誦之儀刑之故垂範也遠斯古
之明於不朽者德之選而治之致也執事
軫念嶺海之民慨然思古循良以風有位
===
策諸生誦說其事甚盛德也敢以嘗所繹
求而服膺之者以對夫郡縣非古也自秦
罷侯置守縣統之令以制置其民而乂安
之五嶺之外至漢始隷郡邑歷代以來率
由斯制故守令之於民最重漢宣帝曰庶
民安其田里而無歎息愁恨之心者政平
訟理也與我共此者其惟良二千石乎明
帝又曰郎官出宰百里苟非其人民受其
殃是言守令之係民者重也故曰守令者
punctuated:
古之善爲治者，其處巳也盡道，然而廉靖其本矣；其處人也盡制，然而惠利其先矣。能立其本，則議道自巳而風化端；能知先務，則置法以民而德施普。是謂不求治於人而求治於巳，不求利於巳而求利於人。在當時而利賴之、詠歌之，故樹績也弘；在後世而傳誦之、儀刑之，故垂範也遠。斯古之明於不朽者，德之選而治之致也。執事軫念嶺海之民，慨然思古循良以風有位，策諸生誦說其事，甚盛德也。敢以嘗所繹求而服膺之者以對。
夫郡縣非古也。自秦罷侯置守，縣統之令，以制置其民而乂安之。五嶺之外，至漢始隷郡邑，歷代以來率由斯制，故守令之於民最重。漢宣帝曰：「庶民安其田里而無歎息愁恨之心者，政平訟理也。與我共此者，其惟良二千石乎！」明帝又曰：「郎官出宰百里，苟非其人，民受其殃。」是言守令之係民者重也。故曰：「守令者，
translation_en:
Those in antiquity who governed well fulfilled the Way in their own conduct, taking integrity and composure as their foundation; in dealing with others, they fulfilled the requirements of proper institutions, taking benefits to the people as their first priority. If they could establish this foundation, their deliberations on the Way began with themselves, and moral transformation took its proper course. If they understood what deserved priority, they established laws with the people in mind, and the benefits of their virtue extended everywhere. This is what is meant by seeking good government in oneself rather than demanding it of others, and seeking benefits for others rather than for oneself. In their own day, people benefited from and depended upon them, celebrating them in song; thus their achievements were great. In later generations, people recounted their deeds and took them as models; thus the example they bequeathed endured. Such were the ancients who understood how to achieve immortality: outstanding in virtue and consummate in government. You, honored examiners, are deeply concerned for the people of Linghai and earnestly recall the conscientious and benevolent officials of antiquity, seeking thereby to influence those who hold office. Your asking the students in this policy question to recount and discuss their deeds manifests abundant virtue. I venture to reply with what I have previously studied, pondered, and taken to heart.
The system of commanderies and counties did not originate in high antiquity. Beginning with Qin, the enfeoffed lords were abolished and commandery governors appointed, while counties were placed under magistrates, to regulate and administer the people and bring them peace. The lands beyond the Five Ranges first came under commandery and county jurisdiction during the Han. Successive dynasties have generally followed this system; hence commandery governors and county magistrates are of the greatest importance to the people. Emperor Xuan of Han said: “When the common people live contentedly on their farms and in their villages, without sighs, sorrow, or resentment, it is because administration is equitable and lawsuits are properly adjudicated. Those who share with me the task of achieving this must surely be worthy officials of the two-thousand-bushel rank!” Emperor Ming also said: “When court gentlemen go out to govern a territory of a hundred li, if they are not the right men, the people suffer the consequences.” These words show how profoundly commandery governors and county magistrates affect the people. Thus it is said: “Commandery governors and county magistrates…”

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
所使承流而宣化者也上德不宣則恩澤
不究下情不達則幽隱莫通有意斯民者
又安得不重之耶兩漢之治號稱近古然
考之循吏傳則班史所載西漢僅於六人
范史所紀東漢亦止十二人嗟乎難矣稽
之於粤往所為郡縣者代有令德愚嘗以
二端槩之曰廉靖以持已也曰惠利以及
人也何也傳曰大人者正已而物正也此
責已之義也世之砥礪名行者鮮矣賈琮
===
之為刺史也簡選良吏蕩定諸縣乃其民
歌之則曰賈父來晚今見清平非以其能
却琛獻率厲化之乎吳隱之之為廣州也
清操踰常始終不易乃自酌貪泉有曰夷
齊試飲當不易心非有見於不見可欲使
心不亂乎費貽故節士也仕合浦而江山
名廉則莅政清簡而千載懷德無讓於古
之甘棠矣孟嘗故孝廉也守合浦而去珠
復還則革易前弊而吏民攀請庶幾乎古
punctuated: 所使承流而宣化者也。上德不宣，則恩澤不究；下情不達，則幽隱莫通。有意斯民者，又安得不重之耶？兩漢之治，號稱近古，然考之《循吏傳》，則班史所載西漢僅於六人，范史所紀東漢亦止十二人。嗟乎，難矣！稽之於粤，往所為郡縣者，代有令德。愚嘗以二端槩之：曰廉靖以持已也，曰惠利以及人也。何也？傳曰：「大人者，正已而物正也。」此責已之義也。世之砥礪名行者鮮矣！賈琮之為刺史也，簡選良吏，蕩定諸縣。乃其民歌之，則曰：「賈父來晚，今見清平。」非以其能却琛獻、率厲化之乎？吳隱之之為廣州也，清操踰常，始終不易。乃自酌貪泉，有曰：「夷齊試飲，當不易心。」非有見於「不見可欲，使心不亂」乎？費貽故節士也，仕合浦而江山名廉，則莅政清簡而千載懷德，無讓於古之甘棠矣。孟嘗故孝廉也，守合浦而去珠復還，則革易前弊而吏民攀請，庶幾乎古
translation_en:
…those commissioned to carry forward the sovereign’s beneficent influence and spread his transforming instruction. If virtue from above is not made manifest, its blessings do not reach everywhere; if circumstances below are not conveyed upward, what is obscure and hidden cannot become known. How could anyone concerned for these people fail to attach importance to such officials? The government of the two Han dynasties is reputed to have approached that of antiquity. Yet, examining the Biographies of Benevolent Officials, we find that Ban’s history records only six men of the Western Han, and Fan’s history only twelve of the Eastern Han. Alas, how difficult it is! Looking into the history of Yue, we find that in every age there were men of admirable virtue who governed its commanderies and counties. I have ventured to summarize their virtues under two headings: integrity and tranquility in governing oneself, and kindness and benefits extended to others. Why is this? The commentary says: “The great man rectifies himself, and all things are rectified.” This is the principle of holding oneself accountable. Few in this world hone their reputation and conduct!

When Jia Cong served as Regional Inspector, he selected good officials and pacified the counties. The people sang of him: “Father Jia came late; now we see purity and peace.” Was this not because he could reject offerings of precious objects and transform the people by leading and encouraging them? When Wu Yinzhi governed Guangzhou, his integrity surpassed the ordinary and remained unchanged from beginning to end. He himself drew and drank water from the Spring of Greed, saying: “Were Boyi and Shuqi to try drinking this, surely their hearts would not change.” Was this not an understanding of the saying, “Do not display desirable things, so that the heart is not disturbed”? Fei Yi was a man of steadfast principle. He served in Hepu, and its river and mountain bore the name Lian, ‘Integrity’ [?]. His administration was incorrupt and uncomplicated, and people cherished his virtue for a thousand years: he was no less worthy than the ancient official commemorated by the sweet pear tree. Meng Chang had originally been recommended as Filial and Incorrupt. When he governed Hepu, the pearls that had departed returned. He reformed earlier abuses, and officials and people clung to him, pleading that he remain; he came close to the ancient …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之惠人矣繼美處默以肅弊俗王鎮之之
行也而果不受俸祿去官無異焉眞蕭然
無營者與約戒官屬無令交通王方慶之
敎也而能受訴吏民通却參餉焉非秋毫
無索者與嶺南節度乃搜家珍投之江中
李勉之廉潔徵其沉雅矣頌德請碑豈違
道干譽之故哉端州爲守至於秩滿不持
一硯包拯之清介稱其峭直矣河清之比
豈聲音笑貌之爲哉是數君子者爲行不
===
同同歸於潔已而章章尤著者尚德哉若
人也傳又曰天生斯民使司牧之此爲民
之義也世之勤恤民隱者鮮矣衛颯之爲
桂陽也庠序婚姻之敎下車汲汲焉朞年
而民從化政何著也茨充之代颯也蠶桑
編屨之訓使民惓惓焉旣而民獲利益德
何溥也武溪之毒淫也而挑移盤石六瀧
爲奠至於行旅出途則周憬之功不衰也
茅茨之患火也而敎之陶瓦民知棟梁遂
punctuated:
之惠人矣。繼美處默，以肅弊俗，王鎮之之行也；而果不受俸祿，去官無異焉，眞蕭然無營者與！約戒官屬，無令交通，王方慶之敎也；而能受訴吏民，通却參餉焉，非秋毫無索者與！嶺南節度，乃搜家珍投之江中，李勉之廉潔徵其沉雅矣。頌德請碑，豈違道干譽之故哉？端州爲守，至於秩滿，不持一硯，包拯之清介稱其峭直矣。河清之比，豈聲音笑貌之爲哉？是數君子者，爲行不同，同歸於潔已，而章章尤著者，尚德哉，若人也！
傳又曰：「天生斯民，使司牧之。」此爲民之義也。世之勤恤民隱者鮮矣。衛颯之爲桂陽也，庠序婚姻之敎，下車汲汲焉。朞年而民從化，政何著也！茨充之代颯也，蠶桑編屨之訓，使民惓惓焉。旣而民獲利益，德何溥也！武溪之毒淫也，而挑移盤石，六瀧爲奠，至於行旅出途，則周憬之功不衰也。茅茨之患火也，而敎之陶瓦，民知棟梁，遂
translation_en:
…a benefactor like those of antiquity. To carry forward the fine example of Chumo and purge corrupt customs was Wang Zhenzhi’s practice. He indeed accepted no official salary and, when leaving office, was no different in his circumstances. Was he not truly detached and free of self-seeking? To admonish his subordinates and forbid improper dealings was Wang Fangqing’s teaching. He heard complaints from officials and commoners alike and refused all gifts brought by visitors [?]. Was he not one who sought not so much as a hair’s breadth of personal gain? As Military Commissioner of Lingnan, Li Mian gathered the precious possessions in his household and cast them into the river. His incorruptibility bore witness to his composed and refined character. When people praised his virtue and requested a commemorative stele, could this have resulted from his violating the Way to seek acclaim? As prefect of Duanzhou, Bao Zheng did not take even a single inkstone when his term ended. His purity and integrity matched his stern uprightness. Could the comparison of him to the clearing of the Yellow River have been earned merely through his voice, smiles, and outward manner? These gentlemen differed in their conduct, yet all attained the same purity of self. How conspicuously they stood out—men such as these esteemed virtue!
The Commentary further says: “Heaven brought forth these people and appointed rulers to shepherd them.” This is the principle of acting for the people. Few in this world diligently attend to the people’s hidden suffering. When Wei Sa governed Guiyang, he urgently set about instruction through schools and the regulation of marriage as soon as he arrived. Within a year, the people had responded to his transforming influence. How manifest were the effects of his government! When Ci Chong succeeded Wei Sa, he instructed the people in silkworm raising, mulberry cultivation, and sandal weaving, encouraging their diligent application. Before long, the people reaped the benefits. How widely his beneficence extended! When the dangers of Wuxi were severe, great rocks were excavated and moved, and the six rapids were made safe, allowing travelers to undertake their journeys. Thus Zhou Jing’s achievement endured. When thatched roofs posed a fire hazard, the people were taught to make roof tiles and learned the use of ridgepoles and beams, thereby…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
使延燒無患則宋璟之遺愛至今也奏去
繁課而重定田賦周渭之存恤廣南可不
謂至德乎乃其諭降交阯威信蓋益著矣
請除苛政而蠲免戶役張士遜之施惠南
雄可不謂至仁乎乃其記名御屏節槩固
有素矣余靖因廣俗輕揚而敎之禮法政
簡而不苛化之入人深也嶺海晏然偉哉
經制之烈耶程師道大脩學校而日引講
解故諸番願學感之及人遠也威愛並行
===
彬彬然德禮之致耶是數君子者爲政不
同同歸於利民而昭韙在人者仁人哉其
利溥也夫正己率物政之本也其本端而
後措之治裕如矣道利與理政之施也其
施普而後顯其德於不窮矣此合一之義
也前所紀載故各自其著者言之耳若夫
兼體備道無不可法者其惟唐宋二子乎
考之在唐有韓愈氏佛骨一表萬代所瞻
仰也乃忠誠馴鱷魚之暴文章起八代之
punctuated:
使延燒無患，則宋璟之遺愛至今也。奏去繁課而重定田賦，周渭之存恤廣南，可不謂至德乎？乃其諭降交阯，威信蓋益著矣。請除苛政而蠲免戶役，張士遜之施惠南雄，可不謂至仁乎？乃其記名御屏，節槩固有素矣。余靖因廣俗輕揚而敎之禮法，政簡而不苛，化之入人深也。嶺海晏然，偉哉，經制之烈耶！程師道大脩學校而日引講解，故諸番願學，感之及人遠也。威愛並行，彬彬然，德禮之致耶！

是數君子者，爲政不同，同歸於利民，而昭韙在人者，仁人哉，其利溥也！夫正己率物，政之本也。其本端，而後措之治裕如矣。道利與理，政之施也。其施普，而後顯其德於不窮矣。此合一之義也。前所紀載，故各自其著者言之耳。若夫兼體備道，無不可法者，其惟唐宋二子乎？考之，在唐有韓愈氏，佛骨一表，萬代所瞻仰也。乃忠誠馴鱷魚之暴，文章起八代之
translation_en:
…so that spreading fires no longer caused calamity: the enduring affection earned by Song Jing survives to this day. By memorializing to abolish onerous levies and reassessing the land tax, Zhou Wei cared for the people of Guangnan. Could this not be called consummate virtue? Moreover, his persuading Jiaozhi to submit made his authority and trustworthiness still more manifest. By requesting the abolition of harsh measures and exemption from household service obligations, Zhang Shixun bestowed benefits upon Nanxiong. Could this not be called consummate benevolence? His name was recorded on the imperial screen; indeed, his integrity had long been established. Because the customs of Guang were frivolous and flighty, Yu Jing instructed the people in ritual and law. His administration was simple and free of harshness, and his transforming influence penetrated deeply into the people. The region of the mountains and sea was at peace: how magnificent the achievement of his administrative arrangements! Cheng Shidao extensively renovated schools and daily gathered students for lectures and explanations. Thus the various non-Han peoples wished to study: his influence reached far. Authority and kindness operated together, bringing cultivated refinement—was this not the effect of virtue and ritual?

These gentlemen differed in their ways of governing, yet all worked toward benefiting the people, whose manifest approval they won. Benevolent men indeed, how widely their benefits extended! To rectify oneself and lead others is the foundation of government. Only when that foundation is sound can one apply oneself to governing with ease. Guidance, benefit, and order [?] constitute the practice of government. Only when that practice reaches everywhere can one’s virtue manifest itself without end. This is what it means for the two to form a unity. Accordingly, the preceding accounts have discussed each man only in terms of his most conspicuous achievements. As for those who embodied all these qualities and fully possessed the Way, with nothing in them unworthy of emulation, were they not the two masters of the Tang and Song? Looking to the Tang, there was Han Yu, whose single memorial on the Buddha’s bone has commanded the admiration of countless generations. His loyal sincerity tamed the ferocity of crocodiles, and his writings reversed eight dynasties of …

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
衰而潮陽之民至今知學豈徒因文見道
已耶在宋有周敦頤氏太極一圖前聖所
未發也乃羅浮發詠與道為體提刑過化
所在澤物而南粤理學至今有傳豈直一
方循良已耶是又德行政事之宗而論世
尚友者之準的也仰惟
聖明在御
恩惠覃被薄海外内無遐遺矣邇者屢厪
詔旨惻念民隱責成守令甚切當事之臣祗承
===
德意繩舉而振勵之一時郡邑之吏無不滌心
易慮遵
典則以慎脩仰前哲而興起而凡垂髫扶杖之
民無不思見德化之成誠千載一時也然
故記所存令德嘉猷皆宜則倣而揆厥要
領則敦行為先故曰人有不為也而後可
以有為此達義也當世君子誠能明決擇
而師表昔賢則仰昌黎之患而博愛行宜
所當三復廣化原也紹濂溪之學而公已
punctuated:
衰，而潮陽之民至今知學，豈徒因文見道已耶？在宋有周敦頤氏，太極一圖，前聖所未發也。乃羅浮發詠，與道為體；提刑過化，所在澤物，而南粤理學至今有傳，豈直一方循良已耶？是又德行政事之宗，而論世尚友者之準的也。
仰惟聖明在御，恩惠覃被，薄海外内，無遐遺矣。邇者屢厪詔旨，惻念民隱，責成守令甚切。當事之臣祗承德意，繩舉而振勵之。一時郡邑之吏，無不滌心易慮，遵典則以慎脩，仰前哲而興起；而凡垂髫扶杖之民，無不思見德化之成，誠千載一時也。
然故記所存令德嘉猷，皆宜則倣，而揆厥要領，則敦行為先。故曰：「人有不為也，而後可以有為。」此達義也。當世君子誠能明決擇而師表昔賢，則仰昌黎之患，而博愛行宜，所當三復廣化原也；紹濂溪之學，而公已
translation_en:
…decline, while the people of Chaoyang to this day understand the importance of learning. Was his achievement merely to reveal the Way through writing? In the Song there was Zhou Dunyi. His Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate disclosed what earlier sages had not yet expounded. He composed verses at Luofu, embodying the Way; serving as Judicial Commissioner, he transformed people wherever he passed and bestowed benefits wherever he went. The learning of principle in southern Yue has consequently been transmitted down to the present. Was he merely a conscientious and benevolent official in one locality? These men are also exemplars of virtuous conduct and government, and standards for those who study past ages and seek fellowship with the worthies of antiquity.
We reverently reflect that our sagacious sovereign occupies the throne. His benevolence reaches everywhere, to the seas and throughout the realm, leaving no distant place neglected. Recently, repeated imperial edicts have expressed compassionate concern for the people's hidden sufferings and pressed prefects and magistrates most earnestly to fulfill their responsibilities. The officials concerned reverently receive this benevolent intent, correcting misconduct and spurring others to exert themselves. Throughout the prefectures and counties, officials cleanse their hearts and reform their thinking, observing established rules to cultivate themselves conscientiously and drawing inspiration from earlier worthies. Among the people, from children with hanging locks to elders leaning on staffs, all long to witness the fulfillment of transformation through virtue. Truly, this is an opportunity encountered once in a thousand years.
The excellent virtues and admirable counsels preserved in earlier records should all be emulated. Yet, when their essentials are considered, earnest practice comes first. Thus it is said: “Only when people refrain from doing certain things can they accomplish something.” This is a universally applicable principle. If gentlemen of the present age can indeed distinguish clearly, choose decisively, and take earlier worthies as their models, then, looking up to the concerns [?] of Changli, Han Yu, they should practice universal love and act fittingly, repeatedly pondering how to broaden the source of moral transformation. Carrying forward the learning of Lianxi, Zhou Dunyi, and making themselves impartial [?]…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
公人所宜深意普德施也由是以創仁義
之塗則風俗可同以究輯綏之澤則仳離
可安以揚扞圉之威則姦宄可息以垂變
通之利則財賦可供所以幸元元而底式
序者莫此爲大矣嗟乎斯爲不失民望無
負於
明時乃後之人必有遡求德澤如今茲者
第五問
陳維翰
===
同考試官教諭曾批東廣大計莫如蕩平山
寇此策援引詳明籌畫精確必抱經濟之略者得
子良可自慶
考試官教諭黃批抵掌談兵通達時務而
所條十二略尤中機宜子非胸中有甲兵者耶是
用錄出
考試官學正宋批平寇之術鑿鑿可行取
之不徒以其文也
甞聞龔遂治渤海而盜賊散魯恭至樂安
punctuated:
公人，所宜深意普德施也。由是以創仁義之塗，則風俗可同；以究輯綏之澤，則仳離可安；以揚扞圉之威，則姦宄可息；以垂變通之利，則財賦可供。所以幸元元而底式序者，莫此爲大矣。嗟乎！斯爲不失民望，無負於明時，乃後之人必有遡求德澤如今茲者。
第五問
陳維翰
同考試官教諭曾批：東廣大計，莫如蕩平山寇。此策援引詳明，籌畫精確，必抱經濟之略者。得子，良可自慶。
考試官教諭黃批：抵掌談兵，通達時務，而所條十二略尤中機宜。子非胸中有甲兵者耶？是用錄出。
考試官學正宋批：平寇之術，鑿鑿可行，取之不徒以其文也。
甞聞龔遂治渤海而盜賊散，魯恭至樂安
translation_en:
…and treating others impartially: one should ponder deeply how to extend the benefits of virtue to all. By thus opening a path for benevolence and righteousness, customs can be brought into harmony; by fully extending the blessings of conciliation and pacification, those driven apart can be settled; by displaying the might of defense, evildoers can be suppressed; and by providing the benefits of adaptation to circumstances, fiscal revenues can be secured. Nothing is greater than this as a means of benefiting the common people and bringing them into proper order. Ah! This would fulfill the people's hopes and do justice to this enlightened age. Then future generations will surely seek out the sources of these beneficent legacies, just as we do today.
Fifth Question
Chen Weihan
Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor: For the great affairs of Guangdong, nothing is more important than thoroughly pacifying the mountain bandits. This policy essay adduces references fully and clearly, and its plans are precise and sound. Its author must possess a strategy for ordering the realm and aiding the people. Having found you, I truly have cause to congratulate myself.
Comment by Examiner Huang, Instructor: You discuss warfare with animated gestures and show a thorough understanding of current affairs. The twelve strategies you set out are especially well suited to the circumstances. Are you not a man with armies and weapons in his breast? For this reason, your essay has been selected for inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Song, Instructor: These methods for pacifying the bandits are demonstrably practicable. This essay has been selected for more than its literary merits alone.
I have heard that when Gong Sui governed Bohai, the bandits dispersed, and when Lu Gong arrived in Le'an…

title: 嘉靖四十年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而渠帥降豈有異術哉亦不過酌緩急之
宜察輕重之勢持操縱之權審進退之機
而已矣彼二子循吏也二盜未甚也故不
竟所施而業已定矣廣之山寇在門庭乎
在腹心乎將撫之乎將勦之乎其緩急輕
重操縱進退在眉睫間不待智者而知也
今夫言東南之患者皆曰莫如海倭彼以
舟楫為室家以風潮為朝夕得利即返失
利則遯猶可料也至山寇殆又甚焉生也
===
目擊其事懷憤久矣敢不直述以對請先
言三不可撫而後及十二略可乎何者福
之漳豫章之贛廣之潮惠山海參錯險不
可窺其民獷悍狡黠易於為盜即累金之
家亦樂為諸酋役使噪應如響矯之則操
戈相殘矣習俗然也邇尤相煽為虐賄殘
倭以張羽翼飾虛聲以駭見聞震動諸郡
所至蕩然荼毒之慘忍言之哉此一不可
撫也前者豨突鼠跳猶畏官府廉之今白
punctuated:
而渠帥降，豈有異術哉？亦不過酌緩急之宜，察輕重之勢，持操縱之權，審進退之機而已矣。彼二子，循吏也；二盜，未甚也。故不竟所施，而業已定矣。廣之山寇，在門庭乎？在腹心乎？將撫之乎？將勦之乎？其緩急輕重、操縱進退，在眉睫間，不待智者而知也。今夫言東南之患者，皆曰莫如海倭。彼以舟楫為室家，以風潮為朝夕，得利即返，失利則遯，猶可料也。至山寇，殆又甚焉。生也，目擊其事，懷憤久矣，敢不直述以對？請先言三不可撫，而後及十二略，可乎？
何者？福之漳、豫章之贛、廣之潮惠，山海參錯，險不可窺。其民獷悍狡黠，易於為盜，即累金之家，亦樂為諸酋役使，噪應如響。矯之，則操戈相殘矣，習俗然也。邇尤相煽為虐，賄殘倭以張羽翼，飾虛聲以駭見聞，震動諸郡，所至蕩然。荼毒之慘，忍言之哉？此一不可撫也。前者豨突鼠跳，猶畏官府廉之；今白
translation_en:
…and the bandit chiefs surrendered. Did they possess some extraordinary technique? They merely weighed when urgency or deliberation was appropriate, assessed the relative gravity of circumstances, exercised discretion in restraint and release, and judged the right moments to advance or withdraw. Those two men were exemplary officials, and the two bands of robbers had not yet become very formidable. Thus, before their measures had been fully implemented, their task was already accomplished. Are Guangdong’s mountain bandits at our gates, or within our very vitals? Shall we pacify them or suppress them by force?
